Title: Human can deny wallet tool invocations
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent exposes wallet functions as MCP tools, the application shall let the user deny each tool invocation that has legal or financial effect, and shall indicate clearly when a tool is invoked.
Rationale: The specification only says SHOULD; for signing, sealing or submitting on behalf of a legal person a human decision point is derived as an obligation.
Source extract: there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Derived obligation strengthens MCP SHOULD; legal or financial effect is undefined and untestable.

Title: Tool annotations treated as untrusted
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent acts as an MCP client, it shall treat tool annotations as untrusted unless they come from a trusted server.
Rationale: A malicious server could otherwise label a destructive wallet action as read-only to skip confirmation.
Source extract: clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Auth-required state is not itself an authorisation
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent implements A2A, the agent shall not treat the TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED transition, by itself, as authorisation for any operation, and shall define how an authorised operation is identified and checked.
Rationale: A2A does not define the scope or revocation of an in-task authorisation, so a mandate model must be supplied by the implementer.
Source extract: Agents MUST NOT treat the TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED state transition, by itself, as authorization for any particular operation.
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Two obligations: no implicit authorisation, and defined authorisation identification.

Title: Agents act by delegation, not impersonation
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent acts on behalf of a user or legal person, the agent shall use explicit on-behalf-of delegation that proves its delegated scope while remaining identifiable as distinct from the principal.
Rationale: Impersonation hides who acted and defeats accountability for business transactions.
Source extract: agents prove their delegated scope while remaining identifiable as distinct from the user they represent
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Rationale does not state the derivation; quote covers only distinct identifiability and scope proof, not a ban on impersonation.

Title: Agent identity carries model, version and capabilities
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent presents an agent identity to a relying party, the identity shall be accompanied by metadata on the underlying model, version and capabilities so that the relying party can apply risk-based access control.
Rationale: The whitepaper holds that workload identity says what an agent is but not how it behaves; the wording here is derived from that observation.
Source extract: Agent identity must be enriched with metadata about its underlying model, version
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K06 Identity and identifiers; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Quote truncated; "capabilities" and risk-based access control are not evidenced. Statement tests unclear.

Title: Delegation path verifiable end to end
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent delegates sub-tasks to other agents, a resource server at the end of the chain shall be able to cryptographically verify the entire delegation path back to the original principal and each step shall narrow scope.
Rationale: Verifying only the final agent leaves the origin of authority unprovable.
Sources: SRC-OIDF-AGENTIC (Section 3.2 Delegated Authorization and Transitive Trust)
Source extract: must be able to cryptographically verify the entire delegation path back to the original user
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: "Each step shall narrow scope" is not in the quote; split verification from attenuation.

Title: Autonomous agent actions distinguished from delegated ones
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent can act without an attributable upstream principal, such autonomous actions shall be clearly distinguished from delegated actions, for example by separate identities or token scopes.
Rationale: A relying party must know whether a human or legal person authorised an action.
Source extract: Such autonomous actions MUST be clearly distinguished from delegated ones
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)

Title: Each delegation hop scopes and re-binds context
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent takes part in a multi-hop chain of agent delegation, each hop shall explicitly scope and re-bind the security context.
Rationale: Without it authority can expand beyond what the principal granted.
Source extract: each hop in the chain MUST explicitly scope and re-bind the security context
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Re-binding context is a mechanism for the scope narrowing split out of AIF-006; fold them.

Title: Agent DID authentication separate from authorisation
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent authenticates with the W3C AI Agent Protocol DID profile, the server shall evaluate its authorisation policy independently after authentication and return an authorisation failure when the DID lacks permission.
Rationale: Proof of key control must not be mistaken for a mandate.
Source extract: the server MUST independently evaluate its authorization policy.
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Overlaps AIF-003 principle; keep because protocol-specific to W3C DID profile.

Title: Agent mandate states principal, agent, scope, limits, validity
Requirement: An agent mandate shall state the principal, the agent, the scope of permitted actions, the limits on those actions and the validity period.
Rationale: A verifier can only check an action against a mandate whose scope, limits and validity are explicit and machine-readable.
Sources: SRC-EBW-PROPOSAL (Article 3, point (19); cf. Directive (EU) 2025/25 Article 16c(4) and ST 9684/26 Annex point 12(1)(c))
Actors: wallet owner; authorised representative; AI agent
Source extract: ‘mandate’ means the authorisation granted by a European Business Wallet owner to an authorised representative
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K01 Credential data model and formats; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability
Review note: Quote is only the Article 2 mandate definition; limits and validity are derived but rationale does not mark it. Check against MAN-series requirements.

Title: Agent functions must not weaken core functionalities
Requirement: Where a provider of European Business Wallets offers agentic AI functionality as an additional functionality, that functionality shall not interfere with or compromise the confidentiality, availability or integrity of the minimum core functionalities.
Rationale: Recital 28 names agentic AI as an anticipated additional use case, which Article 5(2) permits only without harm to the core.
Source extract: do not interfere with or compromise the confidentiality, availability, or integrity of the minimum core functionalities
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Derives obligation for provider from optional-functionality wording; verify Article 5(2) text.

Title: Agent actions distinguishable in wallet log
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall record, for each action performed by an AI agent, the agent identifier and the mandate relied on, so that it is distinguishable from direct user action in the log of transactions.
Rationale: Article 6(1)(d) allows automatic interaction without manual intervention; auditors must still tell agent actions from human ones.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; AI agent
Source extract: to allow interaction with the European Business Wallets automatically without manual intervention or through direct user action
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Quote only says automatic interaction is allowed; logging of agent identifier and mandate is a derivation. Relates to NFR-002.

Title: Agent identified separately from principal
Requirement: An AI agent acting for an owner shall be identified by an identifier of its own that is distinct from the identifier of the principal and expressed as the actor of the delegation.
Rationale: Verifiers and auditors must tell who acts from on whose behalf the action is taken.
Actors: AI agent; wallet owner; authorisation server
Source extract: express that delegation has occurred and identify the acting party to whom authority has been delegated
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: AIF-004 (distinct and identifiable) and AIF-013 (own identifier as actor) state the same obligation.
Also covered: also covered in EBW-AIF-004; also covered in EBW-FUN-037; also covered in EBW-INT-029

Title: Agent keys separate from principal credentials
Requirement: The agent provider shall ensure that an AI agent cannot access, or use without a trusted surface, the signing key used to create mandates for that agent.
Rationale: If the agent can use the key that creates its own mandates, it can authorise itself beyond the owner's consent.
Source extract: The Agent Provider MUST ensure that the Agent is not able to access the Agent Provider signing key, or use it without the Trusted Surface.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Quote is AP2 specific (Agent Provider signing key, Trusted Surface); generalise terms.

Title: Owner identity preserved under delegation
Requirement: The mandate and authorisation system shall not give an authorised representative or AI agent possession of the owner identification data or the private keys of the owner's wallet unit.
Rationale: Recital 18 requires delegation that preserves the integrity of the identity of the owner of the wallet.
Actors: wallet provider; AI agent; authorised representative
Source extract: in such a way as to preserve the integrity of the identity of the owner of that Wallet
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Recital 18 wording is about preserving identity integrity; ban on possession of keys is a stronger derivation. Recitals are non-binding.

Title: Informed consent on a trusted surface before mandate creation
Requirement: Before a mandate is created for an AI agent, a trusted surface shall present the mandate content to the principal and obtain the principal's informed consent.
Rationale: A mandate that the agent drafts and the principal never saw gives no assurance of what was approved.
Actors: wallet owner; agent provider; trusted surface
Source extract: a UI surface that is trusted to get informed user consent for an Intent before creating a user-signed Mandate
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: Consent surface not driven by an AI model
Requirement: The trusted surface that obtains consent for a mandate shall be operated without a non-deterministic AI model handling its communication.
Rationale: A model-driven consent surface could be manipulated by the same agent it is meant to constrain.
Source extract: The following role MUST be non-agentic:
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Quote fragment "following role MUST be non-agentic" lacks the role; "non-deterministic AI model" in statement is a gloss.

Title: Mandate verification in deterministic code
Requirement: Validation of mandates and processing of their constraints shall be performed in deterministic code, not by an AI model.
Rationale: Verification that depends on a language model can be steered by prompt injection.
Source extract: it MUST happen in deterministic code regardless of whether the role is agentic or not
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Testable only by architecture review; "AI model" needs definition.

Title: Mandate limits enforced outside the agent
Requirement: The verifier or the wallet, not the AI agent, shall enforce the limits of a mandate on each action the agent attempts.
Rationale: AP2 treats every agent and model as a potential attacker, so limits cannot depend on the agent's own compliance.
Source extract: all LLMs and Agents MUST be considered potential attackers and are explicitly included in the threat model
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote is threat-model statement, not enforcement duty; derivation not marked. Overlaps AIF-018.

Title: Unknown mandate constraints fail evaluation
Requirement: A verifier shall treat any mandate constraint it does not recognise as failing evaluation.
Rationale: Failing closed prevents an agent from using constraint types the verifier cannot enforce.
Sources: SRC-AP2 (Agent Authorization, Verification and Processing Rules)
Source extract: Any unknown Constraints MUST be treated as failing evaluation.
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Cumulative budget across agent actions
Requirement: When a mandate contains a budget constraint, the verifier shall track the total of previous actions under that mandate and reject an action that would exceed the budget.
Rationale: Per-action limits alone do not bound the total exposure of a reusable mandate.
Source extract: the requested amount plus the total sum of amounts from previously closed Payment Mandates MUST be less than or equal to max
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: AP2 payment mandate specific; not general to business wallet; consider dropping if no payment scope.

Title: No new closed mandate before the previous is resolved
Requirement: An AI agent shall not present a further closed mandate under the same open mandate before it has received a rejection receipt for the previous one.
Rationale: This prevents one open mandate from approving several overlapping actions.
Source extract: Shopping Agents MUST NOT present any subsequent open Payment or Checkout Mandates without receiving a rejection receipt from the previous one.
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote refers to Shopping Agents and Open Payment or Checkout Mandates; statement generalises.

Title: Agent discloses only needed mandate content
Requirement: When presenting a mandate with selective disclosures, the AI agent shall disclose only the parts needed for the verifier to evaluate the closed mandate.
Rationale: Mandate constraints can reveal business intent that the verifier does not need.
Source extract: Shopping Agents MUST present only the disclosures from the open Mandates needed in the evaluation of the closed Mandates.
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Mandate validity no longer than the task needs
Requirement: A mandate for an AI agent shall carry an expiry no later than the time needed to complete the assigned task.
Rationale: A short validity period limits the damage window if the agent or its key is compromised.
Source extract: to set the exp claim for these Mandates to the smallest value that will allow the Shopping Agent to complete the assigned task.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: "No later than the time needed" is hard to test.

Title: Delegation depth bounded by the mandate
Requirement: A mandate shall state whether the AI agent may sub-delegate and the maximum number of delegation steps, and a verifier shall reject a chain that exceeds it.
Rationale: AP2 leaves agent-to-agent delegation unspecified and Council text requires over-delegation to be prevented, so the depth must be bounded explicitly.
Sources: SRC-AP2 (Specification, Agent-to-Agent Delegation; cf. ST 9684/26 Annex point 12(3)(b))
Source extract: it is possible to use this protocol to support delegation of Mandates from one Shopping Agent to another
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote only says delegation is possible; the depth limit is a derivation not marked as such. Overlaps AIF-006.

Title: Signed receipt for every mandate presentation
Requirement: Upon accepting or rejecting a presented mandate, the verifier shall return a signed receipt that references a hash of the received mandate.
Rationale: The receipt gives both parties evidence of what was presented and with what outcome.
Source extract: Upon acceptance or rejection of the Mandate, the Verifier MUST return a signed Mandate Receipt.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Hash reference of mandate in receipt not in quote.

Title: Non-repudiable evidence of mandate use
Requirement: The parties to an agent-initiated transaction shall retain the open mandate, the closed mandate and the receipt so that together they can be verified as evidence of what the principal authorised.
Rationale: AP2 leaves retention open, yet dispute resolution depends on the complete set of records.
Source extract: can be brought together to provide a non-repudiable picture of the transaction
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Retention duty and period are unstated; "non-repudiable" is legal conclusion. Overlaps NFR-002, NFR-014.

Title: Human approval above a mandate-defined threshold
Requirement: A mandate shall be able to define thresholds or action classes above which the action requires approval by a natural person, and the wallet or verifier shall withhold the action until that approval is given.
Rationale: AI Act Article 14(3) requires oversight commensurate with autonomy and risk; thresholds make this enforceable per mandate. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: The oversight measures shall be commensurate with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use of the high-risk AI system
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Art 14(3) does not require thresholds; derivation unmarked, applies only if high-risk. Overlaps EBW-LEG-041.

Title: AI literacy of staff operating AI systems
Requirement: The provider and the deployer of an AI system used in or with a business wallet shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of the AI system on their behalf.
Rationale: Applies to every AI system regardless of risk class, so a wallet provider or agent operator using AI must train its operators. Mapping to wallet provider or agent operator is a derivation (D).
Sources: SRC-AIACT (Article 4(1), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1(5))
Actors: provider of AI system; deployer of AI system; business wallet provider; agent operator
Source extract: shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Art 4 applies to AI providers and deployers generally; no wallet design effect. Quote truncated ("to their best extent" dropped).

Title: Lifecycle risk management system for high-risk AI
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system as a continuous iterative process over the entire lifecycle of that system.
Rationale: Gives the baseline process under which risks of an AI agent acting with wallet credentials are identified and mitigated. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: Risk evaluation includes foreseeable misuse
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall estimate and evaluate the risks that may emerge when the system is used in accordance with its intended purpose and under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse.
Rationale: For agents holding signing or sealing authority, misuse (for example prompt injection triggering a signature) must be assessed up front. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: Pre-market testing against defined metrics
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall test the system, prior to placing it on the market or putting it into service, against previously defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds appropriate to its intended purpose.
Rationale: Makes agent behaviour verifiable before it is trusted with credentials. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: Data governance for training, validation and testing data
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system that uses training of AI models shall subject training, validation and testing data sets to data governance and management practices covering design choices, data origin, preparation operations and bias examination.
Rationale: Constrains how wallet data (credentials, records, messages) may be used to train or tune AI models. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; business wallet provider
Source extract: shall be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: Logging capability supports traceability and monitoring
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall provide logging capabilities that record events relevant for identifying risk situations or substantial modifications, for post-market monitoring and for deployer monitoring of operation.
Rationale: Complements EBW-LEG-040 (existence of logging) by fixing the purposes the log content must serve, relevant for audit trails of agent actions on wallet data. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability
Review note: Art 12(2) purposes can be folded into LEG-040 as an additional clause.

Title: Deployer retains logs of high-risk AI system for six months
Requirement: The deployer of a high-risk AI system shall keep the logs automatically generated by that system, to the extent under its control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of at least six months.
Rationale: An organisation running an AI agent against its business wallet must retain the agent's logs itself. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: deployer of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope. Also GDPR retention tension.

Title: Instructions for use in a digital format
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall accompany the system with instructions for use in an appropriate digital format containing at least provider identity, performance characteristics and limitations, accuracy metrics, human oversight measures and log-handling mechanisms.
Rationale: Deployers (including enterprises delegating wallet operations to an agent) need this information to use the system within its intended purpose. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: shall be accompanied by instructions for use in an appropriate digital format or otherwise
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: High-risk AI system designed for effective human oversight
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall design and develop the system, including appropriate human-machine interface tools, so that natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Rationale: Underpins human-in-the-loop approval of agent actions with legal effect such as signing or sealing. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Art 14(1) design-for-oversight and 14(4) override duties overlap LEG-041; fold with AIF-038.

Title: Human can disregard, override or reverse AI output
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall enable the natural persons assigned to human oversight to decide not to use the system or to disregard, override or reverse its output.
Rationale: Complements EBW-LEG-041 (stop mechanism); an agent's proposed wallet action must be reversible or rejectable before effect. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: to decide, in any particular situation, not to use the high-risk AI system or to otherwise disregard, override or reverse the output
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Rationale calls it complement of LEG-041; same Article 14 human oversight control.

Title: Measures against data poisoning and adversarial inputs
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall include, where appropriate, technical solutions to prevent, detect, respond to, resolve and control attacks on training data, pre-trained components, adversarial inputs and confidentiality attacks.
Rationale: Extends EBW-LEG-042 (resilience against manipulation) with the AI-specific attack classes that matter for prompt injection and model evasion against wallet-connected agents. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: data poisoning
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Quote is a single word fragment "data poisoning"; verify Article 15(5) text.

Title: Serious incident reporting for high-risk AI systems
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member State where it occurred, not later than 15 days after becoming aware, with shorter periods for widespread infringements and deaths.
Rationale: AI-caused incidents involving wallet functions would be reportable in addition to cybersecurity incident duties. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation.
Source extract: not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope. Overlaps wallet incident duties (LEG-027).

Title: Post-market monitoring system for high-risk AI
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system, proportionate to the technology and risks, that actively and systematically collects and analyses performance data throughout the system's lifetime.
Rationale: Continuous monitoring of deployed agent behaviour is the feedback loop to the risk management system. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation.
Source extract: shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: Deployer uses high-risk AI per instructions for use
Requirement: The deployer of a high-risk AI system shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use the system in accordance with its instructions for use.
Rationale: An enterprise using an AI agent with its business wallet must stay within the provider's intended purpose. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: deployer of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Conditional on high-risk; pure usage-compliance duty.

Title: Deployer assigns competent persons to human oversight
Requirement: The deployer of a high-risk AI system shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.
Rationale: Maps to naming accountable human principals for agent mandates in the business wallet. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: deployer of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Conditional on high-risk; naming accountable humans already covered by AIF-010 principal.

Title: Deployer suspends use and informs on risk or serious incident
Requirement: When a deployer has reason to consider that use of a high-risk AI system in accordance with its instructions may present a risk, the deployer shall without undue delay inform the provider or distributor and the market surveillance authority and shall suspend use of the system.
Rationale: Defines the stop-and-notify behaviour when an agent connected to a wallet misbehaves. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: deployer of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: they shall, without undue delay, inform the provider or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authority, and shall suspend the use
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Rationale states conditional high-risk scope but statement does not; add scope.

Title: Deployer informs persons subject to high-risk AI decisions
Requirement: The deployer of an Annex III high-risk AI system that makes or assists in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform those natural persons that they are subject to the use of the system.
Rationale: Relevant where AI-assisted decisions about natural persons (for example employees or applicants) are taken on wallet-held data. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Annex III deployer duty; wallet-specific link is speculative.

Title: Fundamental rights impact assessment before deployment
Requirement: Before deploying a high-risk AI system referred to in Article 6(2), a deployer that is a body governed by public law or a private entity providing public services shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights, and shall notify its results to the market surveillance authority.
Rationale: Public bodies and public-service entities adopting AI around wallet-mediated B2G processes would trigger this assessment. Applies only if the AI system is classified high-risk under Article 6; mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: deployer of high-risk AI system; public sector body
Source extract: shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights that the use of such system may produce
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: FRIA only for public deployers and Article 6(2) systems.

Title: Machine-readable marking of AI-generated output
Requirement: The provider of an AI system generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall ensure that the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, using technical solutions that are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable as far as technically feasible.
Rationale: AI-generated documents or messages entering the wallet's data plane must be machine-detectable as synthetic; applies to any AI system, not only high-risk. Mapping to a wallet-integrated generator is a derivation (D). Marking exceptions in Art 50(2) not reproduced. Providers of systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 (Article 111(4)).
Actors: provider of AI system; business wallet provider; agent operator
Source extract: marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Applies to generative AI providers only; statement omits Art 50(2) exceptions; tie to wallet-integrated generators.

Title: AI interaction notice clear, timely and accessible
Requirement: The provider or deployer that must inform natural persons under Article 50(1) to (4) shall provide the information in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure, conforming to applicable accessibility requirements.
Rationale: Fixes the timing and form of the AI disclosure in EBW-LEG-043 for agents or assistants interacting with people through wallet interfaces. mapping to a wallet or agent operator is a derivation. Not limited to high-risk systems.
Actors: provider of AI system; deployer of AI system
Source extract: in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Rationale itself calls it a refinement of LEG-043; add to that requirement.

Title: Safeguards for Article 22 exceptions and special-category data
Requirement: Where a controller relies on contract necessity or explicit consent for a decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects, the controller shall implement suitable safeguards including the rights to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view and to contest the decision, and shall not base the decision on special categories of data unless Article 22(4) conditions are met.
Rationale: Adds the Art 22(2) exception structure and the Art 22(4) special-category limit to EBW-LEG-015, which covers only paragraphs (1) and (3); relevant to agents deciding on wallet-held personal data.
Actors: data controller; business wallet provider; agent operator
Source extract: Decisions referred to in paragraph 2 shall not be based on special categories of personal data
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Two obligations (safeguards; special-category limit); overlaps EBW-LEG-015 on Art 22 safeguards.

Title: Inform data subject of automated decision-making and its logic
Requirement: Where personal data are processed in automated decision-making including profiling under Article 22(1) and (4), the controller shall provide the data subject with meaningful information about the logic involved and the significance and envisaged consequences of the processing.
Rationale: Requires explainability artefacts for agent-driven decisions affecting natural persons whose data sit in or flow through the wallet.
Source extract: meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability
Review note: Applies when data collected from the data subject; statement omits that trigger.

Title: Access right covers existence and logic of automated decisions
Requirement: Upon a data subject's access request, the controller shall confirm whether automated decision-making including profiling under Article 22(1) and (4) takes place and shall provide meaningful information about the logic involved and its consequences.
Rationale: Wallet-side AI processing must be able to produce this information on request (the Article 14(2)(g) indirect-collection counterpart carries the same wording).
Source extract: the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in Article 22(1) and (4)
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability
Review note: Same logic-information content as AIF-050, different trigger (access request).

Title: Interoperability assessment before binding digital requirements
Requirement: Before taking a decision on new or substantially modified binding requirements, a public sector body or Union entity shall carry out an interoperability assessment.
Rationale: Public authorities that mandate wallet use or machine-readable B2G exchanges must assess cross-border interoperability effects first.
Source extract: shall carry out an interoperability assessment
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Authority-side procedure; Interoperable Europe Act.

Title: Publish assessment report in a machine-readable format
Requirement: The public sector body or Union entity that carried out an interoperability assessment shall publish a report of the outcome, in a machine-readable format facilitating automated translation, on an official website and share it electronically with the Interoperable Europe Board.
Rationale: Machine-readable publication lets AI and automated tooling consume interoperability requirements.
Source extract: in a machine-readable format facilitating automated translation
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote supports only machine-readable format facilitating automated translation.

Title: Share interoperability solutions on request
Requirement: A public sector body or Union entity shall make an interoperability solution supporting a trans-European digital public service, including technical documentation and references to open standards used, available to any other such body that requests it, subject to the stated exceptions.
Rationale: Enables reuse of wallet-related public-sector components such as connectors and registry integrations.
Source extract: shall make available to any other Union entity or public sector body that requests it an interoperability solution
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: "subject to the stated exceptions" is untestable; name exceptions or drop clause.

Title: DPP data based on open standards, machine-readable and transferable
Requirement: The economic operator creating a digital product passport shall ensure that all data in the passport is based on open standards, developed with an interoperable format and, as appropriate, machine-readable, structured, searchable and transferable through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in.
Rationale: Core machine-processability duty for any wallet that issues, holds or presents DPP data; the wallet-provider mapping is a derivation (D).
Actors: economic operator; manufacturer; business wallet provider
Source extract: shall be based on open standards, developed with an interoperable format
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote shorter than statement (machine-readable, no lock-in parts). Wallet applicability only if wallet carries DPP data.

Title: DPP linked to persistent unique product identifier via data carrier
Requirement: The economic operator creating a digital product passport shall connect it through a data carrier to a persistent unique product identifier that complies with the standards referred to in Annex III.
Rationale: Persistent identifiers allow machines, including AI agents, to resolve the passport deterministically.
Source extract: connected through a data carrier to a persistent unique product identifier
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Wallet relevance indirect; Annex III standards clause unverified.

Title: DPP fully interoperable with other passports
Requirement: The digital product passport shall be fully interoperable with other digital product passports required under delegated acts in relation to technical, semantic and organisational aspects of end-to-end communication and data transfer.
Rationale: Semantic interoperability across product groups is a precondition for AI-driven cross-sector processing of DPP data.
Actors: economic operator; manufacturer; digital product passport service provider
Source extract: fully interoperable with other digital product passports
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: "Fully interoperable" is hard to test without delegated-act profiles.

Title: DPP data authenticity, reliability and integrity ensured
Requirement: The digital product passport shall be designed and operated so that data authentication, reliability and integrity are ensured and a high level of security and privacy is provided and fraud is avoided.
Rationale: Provenance of DPP data must be verifiable before AI systems use it for decisions.
Actors: economic operator; digital product passport service provider
Source extract: data authentication, reliability and integrity shall be ensured
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Bundles security, privacy, fraud avoidance: vague, non-atomic.

Title: DPP write access restricted by access rights
Requirement: The digital product passport shall restrict the rights to introduce, modify or update data in the passport based on the access rights specified in the applicable delegated act.
Rationale: Maps to credential-based authorisation of actors, including agents, that write to a passport.
Actors: economic operator; digital product passport service provider
Source extract: rights to introduce, modify or update data in the digital product passport shall be restricted
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Access rights come from delegated acts; testable once those exist.

Title: DPP service providers do not reuse stored passport data
Requirement: A digital product passport service provider that stores or processes passport data shall not sell, reuse or process the data beyond what is necessary for the storing or processing service, unless specifically agreed with the economic operator.
Rationale: Prevents using stored DPP data for AI training or analytics without agreement.
Source extract: shall not sell, reuse or process such data, in whole or in part, beyond what is necessary
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Note: statement allows reuse if agreed with economic operator, as in quote context.

Title: Product data accessible with metadata in machine-readable format
Requirement: Connected products shall be designed and manufactured, and related services designed and provided, so that product data and related service data, including the metadata necessary to interpret and use them, are by default easily, securely, free of charge accessible in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
Rationale: Metadata for interpretation is what lets AI agents use device or product data without bespoke integration; applies to manufacturers and related-service providers, mapping to wallet-linked data flows is derived. The Article 3(1) obligation applies to connected products placed on the market after 12 September 2026 (Article 50).
Actors: manufacturer; provider of related service; data holder
Source extract: including the relevant metadata necessary to interpret and use those data
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Data Act Art 3(1) binds manufacturers of connected products, not wallet or trust services; very long multi-attribute statement.

Title: Data-space participants describe formats, vocabularies and code lists
Requirement: A participant in a data space that offers data or data services to other participants shall describe data structures, data formats, vocabularies, classification schemes, taxonomies and code lists, where available, in a publicly available and consistent manner.
Rationale: Publicly described semantics enable AI-driven mapping of data between spaces; complements EBW-DAT-001 and EBW-DAT-002, which cover points (a) and (c).
Source extract: described in a publicly available and consistent manner
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlap with EBW-DAT-001/002 as stated in rationale.

Title: Interoperability of tools automating data sharing agreements
Requirement: Where applicable, a participant in a data space that offers data or data services to other participants shall provide the means to enable interoperability of tools for automating the execution of data sharing agreements, such as smart contracts.
Rationale: Basis for machine-executed contract negotiation and enforcement between wallets or agents.
Source extract: tools for automating the execution of data sharing agreements, such as smart contracts
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: "Where applicable" and "means to enable" are hard to test.

Title: Oversight measures commensurate with the level of autonomy
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall identify human oversight measures that are commensurate with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use of the system, and shall either build them into the system where technically feasible or specify them for the deployer to implement.
Rationale: Ties the strength of oversight to how autonomous an agent is, which is the basis for mandate-defined limits. Applies only if the system is high-risk under Article 6; mapping to an agent is a derivation. Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2 December 2027 or 2 August 2028 under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: The oversight measures shall be commensurate with the risks, level of autonomy and context of use of the high-risk AI system
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Derived mapping to agents stated in rationale. Statement adds the two-way build-in or specify-for-deployer split from Art 14(3)(a)/(b), not in the truncated quote. Partly overlaps AIF-028 (same Art 14(3) location); complementary, not merged.

Title: Overseers can understand capacities and limits and monitor operation
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall provide it to the deployer in such a way that the natural persons assigned to human oversight are enabled, as appropriate and proportionate, to understand its relevant capacities and limitations and to monitor its operation, including to detect and address anomalies, dysfunctions and unexpected performance.
Rationale: A person who approves or revokes an agent's authority needs this information to do so. Applies only if the system is high-risk under Article 6; mapping to an agent is a derivation (dates as in the Article 14(3) requirement).
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: to properly understand the relevant capacities and limitations of the high-risk AI system and be able to duly monitor its operation
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Conditional on high-risk classification; derivation to agents stated.

Title: Overseers can remain aware of automation bias
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall provide it to the deployer in such a way that the natural persons assigned to human oversight are enabled, as appropriate and proportionate, to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output of the system.
Rationale: Approval prompts for agent actions invite reflexive consent; this is the Union-law basis for designing them so that approvers stay alert. Applies only if the system is high-risk under Article 6; mapping to an agent is a derivation.
Actors: provider of high-risk AI system; agent operator
Source extract: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Test criterion for 'enabled to remain aware' is undefined (inspection only). Derivation to agent approval prompts stated.

Title: Employer informs workers before using a high-risk AI system at the workplace
Requirement: Before putting a high-risk AI system into service or using it at the workplace, a deployer who is an employer shall inform the workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to its use.
Rationale: Applies where an employer deploys a high-risk agent that acts on or with employees' wallet authority; the information duty follows the rules and procedures of Union and national law on information of workers. Applies only if the system is high-risk under Article 6 (dates as in Article 14(3)).
Actors: deployer of high-risk AI system; employer
Source extract: deployers who are employers shall inform workers’ representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to the use
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Duty-holder (deployer who is an employer) and condition match the quote. 'Shall inform' mirrors Art 26(7); information follows Union and national worker-information rules.

Title: Owner can decommission an agent
Requirement: The wallet shall enable the owner to decommission an AI agent, which revokes all mandates and credentials issued to that agent.
Rationale: Derived; the OpenID Foundation whitepaper (non-normative) says agents need a formal process through to decommissioning, and states that credentials must be revocable when no longer needed; EBW-TRU-065 and EBW-TRU-066 cover revocation of a single token or mandate but not the end of life of the agent.
Sources: SRC-OIDF-AGENTIC (Section 2.9, SSO and Provisioning (agent lifecycle management))
Source extract: which require formal processes for creation, permissioning, and eventual decommissioning
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Provenance D with derivation stated; quote only says formal processes through 'eventual decommissioning', so owner-initiated cascade revocation is an EBW design choice. Overlaps TRU-066 (mandate revocation propagation) and TRU-065; complementary (end of agent vs single mandate). Define 'all credentials issued to that agent' before test.

Title: Public sector acceptance within 24 months
Requirement: By 24 months after entry into force, public sector bodies shall enable economic operators to identify and authenticate, sign or seal, submit documents and send or receive notifications using the core functionalities of European Business Wallets for reporting obligations or administrative procedures.
Rationale: Core adoption mandate for the public sector.
Source extract: public sector bodies shall enable economic operators to take the following actions
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote fragment lacks 24 months, action list and procedures scope; verify Article 16(1) text.

Title: Pre-contract disclosure of terms and limitations
Requirement: Before entering a contract, the qualified trust service provider shall inform any person seeking to use the service of the precise terms and conditions, including limitations on use, in a clear and easily accessible manner.
Rationale: Gives customers, including SMEs, transparency on service terms.
Source extract: before entering into a contractual relationship, inform, in a clear, comprehensive and easily accessible manner
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Not a business requirement; overlaps EBW-GOV-008 on limitation notice.

Title: No obligation on economic operators to adopt a business wallet
Requirement: The business wallet framework shall not impose an obligation on economic operators to obtain or use a European Business Wallet; adoption shall remain their choice.
Rationale: Derived from the proposal explanatory memorandum, which states the choice and ties it to Think Small First; the operative duty (Article 16) falls on public sector bodies only; the Council text keeps an evaluation of mandatory use (Article 21).
Source extract: the proposal does not impose any obligation on economic operators
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Negative design constraint; recital/memorandum only, Council keeps review of mandatory use.

Title: Sole traders reach wallet trust services through the EUDI Wallet
Requirement: Self-employed individuals and sole traders shall be able to use their European Digital Identity Wallets to access the trust services offered for European Business Wallets, including the secure communication channel and electronic signatures, without acquiring a full European Business Wallet.
Rationale: Derived from the explanatory memorandum; the operative basis is Article 5(3) for the qualified registered delivery service only, so the wider access is an intention, not a text duty.
Actors: self-employed person; sole trader; wallet provider
Source extract: without the need to acquire a fully-fledged Business Wallet
Clusters: K02 Wallet subject model; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Statement broader than quote and than Art 5(3); scope to secure channel and signatures is unsupported.

Title: Microenterprise onboarding by web or mobile application
Requirement: The onboarding of a microenterprise to a business wallet shall be achievable with a web-based or mobile application requiring only minimal installation and configuration and no individual contracting procedure.
Rationale: Derived from the impact assessment cost model (microenterprise one-off cost EUR 620: training EUR 520, activation EUR 100, contracting EUR 0); it is a design target, not a legal duty.
Source extract: requiring only minimal installation and configuration
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Quote only supports minimal installation; "no individual contracting" comes from footnote cost value. Not testable as written.

Title: Cost model with size-specific one-off and recurring costs
Requirement: The cost-benefit assessment of the business wallet shall distinguish microenterprises, SMEs of 10 to 250 employees and corporates, with one-off costs for training and onboarding, activation and IT implementation and contracting, and recurring licensing and maintenance fees.
Rationale: Derived from the impact assessment (Table 5: yearly cost EUR 500 micro, EUR 5,000 SME, EUR 50,000 corporate); lets pricing and onboarding be tested against the Commission assumptions.
Source extract: Licensing fee and maintenance costs €500 €5,000 €50,000
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Describes a Commission analysis method; no wallet or provider obligation.

Title: Review assesses the impact on micro-enterprises and SMEs
Requirement: The Commission report reviewing the application of the Regulation shall include a specific assessment of the impact of the Regulation on micro-enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises, and shall assess whether an obligation to use European Business Wallets is necessary.
Rationale: The Council text adds SME impact and time and cost savings to the review; the Commission text has only the question of an obligation.
Source extract: including a specific assessment of the impact of this Regulation on micro-enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Council text only; Commission obligation.

Title: Compensation for data access capped at cost for SME recipients
Requirement: Where the data recipient is an SME or a not-for-profit research organisation without non-SME partner or linked enterprises, any compensation agreed for making data available shall not exceed the costs of making the data available.
Rationale: Cost protection for small data recipients in data spaces; applies in business-to-business data sharing under Chapter III.
Source extract: any compensation agreed shall not exceed the costs referred to in paragraph 2, point (a)
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Recategorise to DAT or DOM arguably; applies to data holders.

Title: Audit of qualified providers
Requirement: A qualified trust service provider shall be audited by a conformity assessment body at least every 24 months, and the audit report shall be submitted to the supervisory body within three working days.
Rationale: Keeps qualified status dependent on regular independent assessment.
Actors: Trust service provider; Conformity assessment body; Supervisory body
Source extract: Qualified trust service providers shall be audited at their own expense at least every 24 months by a conformity assessment body.
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: No quote. Second half duplicates CER-002; remove it.

Title: Submission of conformity assessment report
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall submit the conformity assessment report to the supervisory body within three working days of receipt.
Rationale: Gives supervisors timely evidence; complements the existing 24-month audit requirement.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; supervisory body; conformity assessment body
Source extract: shall submit the resulting conformity assessment report to the supervisory body within three working days of receipt
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance

Title: Advance notice of planned audits
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall inform the supervisory body at least one month before any planned audit and allow the supervisory body to observe on request.
Rationale: Enables supervisory observation of audits.

Source extract: inform the supervisory body at the latest one month before any planned audits
