Title: Supervisory ad hoc audits at provider expense
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall accept audits or conformity assessments requested by the supervisory body at any time at the provider's expense.
Rationale: Allows supervisors to verify compliance outside the regular audit cycle.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; supervisory body
Source extract: the supervisory body may at any time audit or request a conformity assessment body to perform
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: "At provider expense" unsupported by the quote as extracted.

Title: Creation device certification validity
Requirement: The validity of a certification of a qualified electronic signature creation device shall not exceed five years, provided vulnerability assessments are carried out every two years, and the certification shall be cancelled where identified vulnerabilities are not remedied.
Rationale: Time-bounds device assurance for seals and signatures.
Source extract: shall not exceed five years, provided that vulnerabilities assessments are carried out every two years
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Cancellation clause beyond quote.

Title: Seal devices follow signature device rules
Requirement: The qualified electronic seal creation device, its certification and its remote management service shall meet the requirements applicable to signature creation devices.
Rationale: Aligns device assurance for sealing.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; device manufacturer
Source extract: Article 29 shall apply mutatis mutandis to requirements for qualified electronic seal creation devices.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: "Requirements applicable to signature devices" is not testable as written.

Title: Certificate holder reports breaches to certification body
Requirement: The holder of a certificate of conformity for a wallet solution shall notify its certification body without undue delay of any breach or compromise likely to affect conformity.
Rationale: Keeps certification current with the threat state.
Source extract: shall notify their certification body without undue delay of any breach or compromise of the wallet solution
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Certification body suspends and cancels on unremedied compromise
Requirement: The certification body shall suspend a certificate of conformity without undue delay once it confirms that a notified breach affects conformity, and shall cancel it if the breach is not remedied in a timely manner.
Rationale: Bounds the period an unsafe wallet stays certified.
Source extract: shall suspend, without undue delay, the certificate of conformity of the wallet solutions
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Quote covers suspension only; cancellation rests on 12(2).

Title: Critical-asset operations meet LoA substantial design rules
Requirement: Where critical assets relate to performing electronic identification at assurance level substantial, the European Business Wallet shall perform cryptographic operations processing critical assets in accordance with the characteristics and design requirements for electronic identification means at assurance level substantial in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.
Rationale: Ties wallet key handling to a defined assurance level. Commission text only: the Council general approach (ST 9684/26) and EP Amendment 132 delete this point.
Source extract: performed in accordance with the requirements for the characteristics and design of electronic identification means at assurance level substantial
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Quote does not name Reg 2015/1502 explicitly; ties to critical-assets definition. Contested across texts.

Title: Secure cryptographic components meet LoA substantial design
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic applications and devices shall comply with the requirements for the characteristics and design of electronic identification means at assurance level substantial in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.
Rationale: Sets the certifiable baseline for the key-protection components. Commission text only: deleted in the Council general approach and by EP Amendment 134.
Source extract: comply with the requirements for the characteristics and design of electronic identification means at assurance level substantial
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Overlaps CER-009 in assurance level; deleted by Council and EP. Contested.

Title: Verify issuance, delivery and activation at LoA substantial
Requirement: The wallet solution shall support mechanisms that enable providers of owner identification data to verify issuance, delivery and activation in compliance with assurance level substantial requirements in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.
Rationale: Sets the assurance floor for identification data issuance. The Council text and EP Amendment 140 raise this to high.
Source extract: verify issuance, delivery and activation in compliance with assurance level substantial
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Subject "wallet solution shall support mechanisms" vague; conflicts with other texts on level.

Title: Activate a unit only with a certified secure device
Requirement: The wallet provider shall activate a new wallet unit only after verifying that the unit includes a wallet secure cryptographic application and device certified as compliant with the requirements for assurance level high.
Rationale: It ties activation of a unit to the certification evidence of the key custody component.
Source extract: SHALL only activate a new Wallet Unit if it has verified that the Wallet Unit includes a WSCA/WSCD that is certified
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Standard-derived (ARF); statement says level high, quote truncated before level; verify full text.

Title: Secure device assessed at assurance level high
Requirement: National certification schemes for wallet solutions shall require that the wallet secure cryptographic device is assessed against the requirements of assurance level high as a prerequisite to certification.
Rationale: It fixes the assurance floor of the key custody component for EUDI Wallets, in contrast to the level substantial in the business wallet proposal.
Source extract: the WSCD shall be assessed against the requirements of assurance level high as set out in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Obligation on Member State schemes; relevance to EBW open.

Title: Vulnerability assessment of the secure device at AVA_VAN.5
Requirement: National certification schemes shall require the evaluation of a wallet secure cryptographic device that is within the object of certification to include a vulnerability assessment at level AVA_VAN.5 of EN ISO/IEC 15408-3, unless a lower level is duly justified to the certification body.
Rationale: It names the depth of evaluation expected for the hardware that holds the keys.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2024-2981 (Annex IV, section 2, point (3), second subparagraph)
Source extract: shall include a vulnerability assessment as set out in EN ISO/IEC 15408-3:2022 at level AVA_VAN.5
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Scheme-side; wallet-general; EBW relevance open.

Title: Device assumptions stay verified after certification
Requirement: National certification schemes shall require evaluation activities that confirm, after issuance of the certificate, that the assumptions made on the wallet secure cryptographic device are still verified, and shall require applicants to describe the measures that keep them verified throughout the certification lifecycle.
Rationale: Hardware not provided by the wallet provider can change after certification, and the assumption must be re-checked.
Source extract: to confirm after issuance of the certificate that the assumptions are still verified
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: Unsuitable secure device blocks the certificate
Requirement: National certification schemes shall deem a wallet secure cryptographic device unsuitable, so that the wallet solution is not issued a certificate of conformity, where verifications of the device remain inconclusive and compensating requirements for the wallet secure cryptographic application are not possible.
Rationale: It states the consequence when the key custody hardware cannot be shown to meet the requirements.
Source extract: the wallet solution shall not be issued a certificate of conformity
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: Evaluation of architectures with several secure devices
Requirement: National certification schemes shall include evaluation activities that ensure the overall solution offers the expected level of security where an architecture uses several wallet secure cryptographic devices or performs some operations on critical assets outside the device.
Rationale: Split-key and hosted-plus-local designs spread key operations over several components and need a combined evaluation.
Source extract: national certification schemes shall include evaluation activities to ensure that the overall solution offers the expected level of security
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Relevant to hybrid hosted/local custody options.

Title: Enforce unproven assumptions on the operating environment
Requirement: National certification schemes shall require, for each assumption on the operating environment of the wallet solution that is not backed by a certificate of conformity or other acceptable assurance information, a description of the mechanism the wallet provider uses to enforce the assumption and a justification that the mechanism is sufficient.
Rationale: Where the device is supplied by the user, the provider must show how it enforces what it assumes about that device.
Source extract: a description of the mechanism that the wallet provider uses to enforce the assumption
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: Sole control assurance level 2 for remote qualified signing in wallets
Requirement: Wallet providers and qualified trust service providers providing the remote qualified signature or seal creation part of a wallet solution shall comply with sole control assurance level 2 as defined in EN 419 241-1.
Rationale: It sets the strength of the control of the signer over a remotely held key; the standard itself was not read in this pass.
Actors: wallet provider; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: SHALL comply with Sole Control Assurance Level (SCAL) 2 as defined in CEN EN 419 241-1
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Standard not read; SCAL 2 level unverified against EN 419 241-1.

Title: CSP-B verifies certificates of conformity
Requirement: The core service provider-B shall, where applicable, verify the provided certificates of conformity for all requested roles.
Rationale: Prevents unverified role claims at onboarding.
Source extract: where applicable, verify the provided certificates of conformity for all requested roles
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: CX-Neptune preview, not certifiable. Duty-holder is CSP-B; EBW analogue is the provider verifying conformity of a role claim. Statement carries the source's 'where applicable'; testability needs the role list.

Title: Certificate lists the sites and addresses it covers
Requirement: The certificate provider shall identify in the certificate offer all sites and addresses, by BPNS and BPNA, for which the certificate is valid.
Rationale: Binds a certificate to the legal entity and its covered locations.
Source extract: MUST contain all BPNSs and BPNAs for which the certificate is valid
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Depends on BPN site/address levels that EBW does not have; would need an EBW equivalent (e.g. LEI/EUID plus address). Do not adopt BPNS/BPNA as EBW terms.

Title: Remote device provider follows the device certification report
Requirement: A qualified trust service provider managing remote qualified signature creation devices shall comply with any requirements identified in the certification report of the specific remote device.
Rationale: It ties the hosted qualified key to the evaluated configuration of the device and decides what a custody provider must evidence.
Source extract: complies with any requirements identified in the certification report of the specific remote qualified electronic signature creation device
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Quote reaches the statement. Applies only where the EBW uses QTSP-managed remote devices.

Title: Evidence for an owner-operated module before activation
Requirement: Where a hardware security module operated by the owner is to act as the secure cryptographic device of a wallet unit, the wallet provider shall obtain and record evidence of its evaluation, at the level that applies to the provider's own devices, before it activates the unit.
Rationale: Derived (criteria C2, C8 of the DEC-03 page): no source says whether an owner-run module counts as the device of Annex point 3(1); EUDI Wallet certification requires a prerequisite assessment of the device whoever provides it, and the EBW level is open (Commission substantial, Council text silent).
Source extract: the WSCD shall be assessed against the requirements of assurance level high as set out in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Derivation stated (C2, C8). Quote is the EUDI WSCD level-high rule, so "level that applies to the provider's own devices" is the bridge; do not read as law. Related GOV-050 and TRU-169.

Title: Public sector infrastructures migrate to post-quantum cryptography
Requirement: The public sector bodies that exchange data with business wallets shall consider migrating the digital infrastructures and services they operate to post-quantum cryptography as soon as possible.
Rationale: Business wallet interactions with public bodies are only as quantum-resilient as the public side. Derived: Recommendation (EU) 2024/1101 is addressed to Member States and is not binding.
Source extract: Member States should consider migrating their current digital infrastructures and services for public administrations and other critical infrastructures to Post-Quantum Cryptography as soon as possible
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Quote is Member States "should consider"; statement widens to bodies exchanging with wallets and says shall. Covered by TRN-002/003.

Title: vLEI credentials are ACDC based
Requirement: All instantiated vLEI credentials shall be ACDC compliant.
Rationale: Records that the GLEIF vLEI credential form is tied to ACDC and not to the EU attestation formats.
Source extract: All instantiated vLEI credentials MUST be ACDC compliant.
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Ecosystem constraint of GLEIF; relevant only as exclusion/bridging case.

Title: vLEI issuer and holder identifiers are KERI AIDs
Requirement: Issuer and holder identifiers of vLEI credentials shall be KERI AIDs.
Rationale: Records the KERI dependency that the project owner wants to exclude, so that any LEI credential is specified separately.
Source extract: Issuer and Holder Identifiers MUST be KERI AIDs.
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Rationale states project owner exclusion; keep as context, not as EBW requirement.

Title: DPP requirements differ per product group and legal act
Requirement: The business wallet design shall not assume a single DPP data model or access scheme, because DPP requirements are set per product group either by delegated acts under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 or by separate Union legislation.
Rationale: Derived from the Commission DPP page (read 3 October 2026): no product-specific ESPR delegated act is listed as adopted yet; iron and steel is planned for Q4 2026 and the first mandatory DPP is for batteries on 18 February 2027.
Source extract: either through the foreseen product-specific 'delegated acts' adopted under the Ecodesign Regulation
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Design guidance, not a legal duty; "shall not assume" untestable.

Title: Wallet authorisations do not create or limit a legal mandate
Requirement: Authorisations granted through the authorisation system of a European Business Wallet shall be treated as technical and shall not create, limit or otherwise affect any power of attorney or legal mandate under national or Union law.
Rationale: Derived from recital 18 of the Council text (a recital, not an operative duty); it prevents the wallet from being used as proof of legal representation beyond national law.
Actors: European Business Wallet owner; wallet provider
Source extract: to not create, limit, or otherwise affect any power of attorney or legal mandate provided under applicable national or Union law
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Recital only; Council text. Not operative in the Commission text.

Title: Existing electronic format requirements remain applicable
Requirement: Where existing Union or national law includes requirements relating to electronic formats as part of an administrative procedure, those requirements shall remain applicable and shall be observed when the core functionalities of a European Business Wallet are used.
Rationale: The principle of equivalence does not replace procedure-specific format rules.
Actors: public sector body; European Business Wallet owner
Source extract: such requirements remain applicable and shall be observed
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Council text only; "shall be observed" is by users and authorities.

Title: Council text ties legal equivalence to qualified trust services
Requirement: Where a European Business Wallet owner or authorised user makes use of a qualified trust service forming part of the core functionalities, the resulting action shall have the same legal effect as if carried out in person, in paper form or by other compliant means.
Rationale: The Council text narrows the equivalence to qualified trust services; the Commission text applies it to the core functionalities as a whole, so the legal-effect boundary is still open.
Actors: European Business Wallet owner; authorised user
Source extract: makes use of any of the qualified trust services forming part of core functionalities of a European Business Wallet
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Council narrows to qualified trust services; contested vs Commission text. Quote shows partial.

Title: Existing systems for exchange between authorities stay in place
Requirement: The Regulation shall be without prejudice to the existing systems and procedures mandated by Union law governing the exchange of documents and data between competent authorities.
Rationale: The business wallet must coexist with systems such as the business registers interconnection, not replace them.
Source extract: without prejudice to the existing systems and procedures mandated by Union law governing the exchange of documents and data between competent authorities
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Without-prejudice clause; design impact is coexistence, not new duty.

Title: Cost model assumes all public sector bodies adopt the wallet
Requirement: The sizing and cost assumptions for the business wallet ecosystem shall treat all public sector bodies as adopters, independent of the level of adoption by economic operators.
Rationale: Derived from the impact assessment footnote 71 on the cost model; it records an assumption of the Commission analysis, not a legal duty.
Source extract: The underlying assumption is that 100% of PSBs will adopt the European Business Wallets
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Records an impact assessment assumption; not a wallet or provider obligation.

Title: Machine-readable description of datasets and usage terms
Requirement: A participant in a data space that offers data or data services shall describe dataset content, use restrictions, licences, collection methodology, quality and uncertainty in a machine-readable format where applicable.
Rationale: Usage policies and contract negotiation in data spaces depend on such descriptions being machine-processable.
Source extract: the dataset content, use restrictions, licences, data collection methodology, data quality and uncertainty shall be sufficiently described
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: 'Machine-readable' and 'where applicable' absent from quote; unclear that EBW participates in a data space.

Title: Describe access means, terms of use and quality of service
Requirement: A participant in a data space that offers data or data services shall describe the technical means of access, such as APIs, with their terms of use and quality of service sufficiently to enable automatic access and transmission.
Rationale: A wallet-bound connector must expose machine-readable access terms to be interoperable.
Source extract: sufficiently described to enable automatic access and transmission of data between parties
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Terms of use and quality of service not in quote; consider merging with DAT-001.

Title: BPN credential issued by the core service provider
Requirement: The Catena-X core service provider shall issue the Business Partner Number credential that attests the BPN associated with the credential subject.
Rationale: Shows a domain-specific secondary identifier credential issued by an ecosystem authority.
Source extract: It is issued by the CSP.
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Quote 'It is issued by the CSP' is thin; 'attests the BPN' of subject is not in quote.

Title: Business Partner Number is stable and never reassigned
Requirement: A Business Partner Number shall never change structurally, shall never cease to exist and shall never be reassigned.
Rationale: Stability is what allows the BPN to serve as an ecosystem-level secondary identifier.
Source extract: never changes structurally, never ceases to exist and never is reassigned
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Wording uses 'never'; make testable; applies to Catena-X BPN issuer.

Title: Machine-readable and searchable storage of submitted data
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that all documents and information submitted as part of formation, branch registration or a filing are stored by the registers in a machine-readable and searchable format or as structured data.
Rationale: Machine-readable register content is the basis for automated retrieval and attestation by a wallet.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2019-1151 (Article 16(6) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/1151)
Source extract: stored by the registers in a machine-readable and searchable format or as structured data
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Enabler for automated retrieval; wallet only consumes.

Title: Legal-person representatives shown with EUID or registration number
Requirement: Where persons authorised to represent a company are legal persons, Member States shall ensure that the name of the company, its legal form and its EUID, or its registration number where the EUID is not applicable, are made publicly available through the system of interconnection of registers.
Rationale: Chains of representation by legal persons are identifiable by EUID, which a mandate verification can reuse. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 18(4), second subparagraph, of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: its EUID or, where the EUID is not applicable, its registration number shall be made publicly available
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote says 'shall be made publicly available'; statement adds name and legal form from article context; check.

Title: Free access to core company data including representatives
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that the name, legal form, registered office, registration number and EUID, status, and particulars of the persons currently authorised to represent the company, including whether they may act alone or jointly, are available free of charge through the system of interconnection of registers.
Rationale: Authentic, free source for legal-person identification and representation power that relying parties and wallets can use.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2019-1151 (Article 19(2) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2019/1151)
Source extract: Member States shall ensure that at least the following information and documents are available free of charge through the system of interconnection of registers
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote only says 'at least the following'; item list not in quote. Overlaps EBW-DAT-008.

Title: EU Company Certificate content on identity and representation
Requirement: The EU Company Certificate for limited liability companies shall include the name, legal form, registration number and Member State, EUID, registered office, correspondence address, status, and the persons authorised to represent the company and whether they act alone or jointly.
Rationale: Defines the attribute set for company identification and representation in the certificate and hence in any wallet attestation based on it. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16b(2), points (a) to (k), of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: shall include the following information:
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote 'shall include the following information' lacks the list; verify attribute list against full_quote.

Title: Verify third-party status with no more information than necessary
Requirement: For the purpose of verifying whether a natural or legal person qualifies as a user or as a third party, the user or third party shall not be required to provide any information beyond what is necessary, and the data holder shall not keep information on the third party’s access beyond what is necessary.
Rationale: Limits both the identity evidence requested from a data recipient and the retention of access records.
Source extract: shall not be required to provide any information beyond what is necessary
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Two obligations on different actors (recipient evidence, holder retention).

Title: Data shared on request of the user or a party acting for the user
Requirement: Upon request by a user, or by a party acting on behalf of a user, the data holder shall make readily available data and the relevant metadata available to a third party without undue delay, in a comprehensive, structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
Rationale: The law accepts a party acting on behalf of the user, so a data-space connector must be able to verify that representation (mandate).
Source extract: Upon request by a user, or by a party acting on behalf of a user, the data holder shall make available readily available data
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote supports; connector mandate verification is implication in rationale only.

Title: Smart contracts for data sharing offer robustness and access control
Requirement: The vendor of an application using smart contracts to execute a data sharing agreement shall ensure that the smart contracts are designed with access control mechanisms and a very high degree of robustness to avoid functional errors and withstand manipulation by third parties.
Rationale: Applies where a data-space connector executes agreements through smart contracts; conformity assessment and a declaration of conformity are required by Article 36(2).
Source extract: robustness and access control, to ensure that the smart contract has been designed to offer access control mechanisms
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Not wallet-related unless connector executes smart contracts; split access control vs robustness.

Title: Smart contracts can be safely terminated or interrupted
Requirement: The vendor of an application using smart contracts to execute a data sharing agreement shall ensure that a mechanism exists to terminate the continued execution of transactions and that the smart contract includes internal functions that can reset or instruct it to stop or interrupt operation.
Rationale: A kill switch and stop function for automated data sharing, relevant for revocation of data-space participation.
Source extract: safe termination and interruption, to ensure that a mechanism exists to terminate the continued execution of transactions
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Revocation link in rationale is an inference.

Title: Export of exportable data in machine-readable form on switching
Requirement: In switching between services of the same service type without published common specifications, the provider of data processing services shall, at the request of the customer, export all exportable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
Rationale: Where a wallet is offered as a cloud or software service, this is the portability duty; it mirrors the export function the proposal sets for wallets (to verify whether a wallet service is a data processing service in the Data Act sense).
Actors: provider of data processing services; customer
Source extract: export all exportable data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Applicability to wallet as data processing service unverified. Related to EBW-NFR-001.

Title: Publish the jurisdiction governing the ICT infrastructure
Requirement: Providers of data processing services shall make available on their websites, and keep up to date, the jurisdiction to which the ICT infrastructure for each service is subject and a description of measures taken to prevent unlawful international governmental access to or transfer of non-personal data.
Rationale: Sovereignty transparency that a wallet customer can use to select a provider; applicability to wallet hosting is a derivation.
Source extract: the jurisdiction to which the ICT infrastructure deployed for data processing of their individual services is subject
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Applies only if wallet hosting qualifies as data processing service.

Title: Data intermediation providers notify before starting
Requirement: Any data intermediation services provider that intends to provide data intermediation services shall submit a notification to the competent authority for data intermediation services.
Rationale: A data space operator or connector service that mediates between holders and users may fall under this notification regime; scope to be assessed per case.
Actors: data intermediation services provider; competent authority
Source extract: shall submit a notification to the competent authority for data intermediation services
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: Non-Union intermediaries designate a legal representative in the Union
Requirement: A data intermediation services provider that is not established in the Union but offers services within it shall designate a legal representative in one of the Member States in which those services are offered, mandated to be addressed by the competent authorities.
Rationale: Statutory legal representation with a mandate towards authorities, a data-space equivalent of Union establishment requirements.
Actors: data intermediation services provider; legal representative
Source extract: shall designate a legal representative in one of the Member States in which those services are offered
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)

Title: Notification identifies the provider as a legal entity
Requirement: The notification of a data intermediation services provider shall include its name, its legal status, form, ownership structure and relevant subsidiaries, and its trade register number where registered.
Rationale: The notification content corresponds to the legal-person identity data and register number that a business wallet identification attestation carries.
Source extract: where the data intermediation services provider is registered in a trade or other similar public national register, registration number
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Quote is the trade register part only; name, legal status, ownership not in quote.

Title: Commission keeps a public register of data intermediation providers
Requirement: The Commission shall keep and regularly update a public register of all data intermediation services providers providing their services in the Union, and the notified name, legal status, address, website, service description and start date shall be published in it.
Rationale: A public register a data-space participant can check as an authentic source; the published fields are listed in Article 11(10).
Source extract: The Commission shall keep and regularly update a public register of all data intermediation services providers providing their services in the Union
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Quote supports register only; published field list from rationale.

Title: Data intermediaries ensure interoperability with each other
Requirement: The data intermediation services provider shall take appropriate measures to ensure interoperability with other data intermediation services, inter alia by means of commonly used open standards in its sector.
Rationale: Counterpart to the Data Act interoperability duty for data spaces; connectors must not lock in participants.
Source extract: take appropriate measures to ensure interoperability with other data intermediation services
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: Tools to give and withdraw consent and permissions
Requirement: A data intermediation services provider that provides tools for obtaining consent from data subjects or permissions from data holders shall provide data subjects with tools to give and withdraw consent and data holders with tools to give and withdraw permissions to process data.
Rationale: Withdrawal of permission is a first-class function, as is revocation of authorisations in business wallets.
Actors: data intermediation services provider; data holder; data subject
Source extract: provide data subjects with tools to both give and withdraw consent and data holders with tools to both give and withdraw permissions
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Overlaps DAT-021; keep separate by actor.

Title: Altruism organisations provide consent and withdrawal tools
Requirement: A recognised data altruism organisation shall provide tools for obtaining consent from data subjects or permissions from data holders, and tools for easy withdrawal of such consent or permission.
Rationale: Consent management with withdrawal; the same pattern as for intermediaries.
Actors: data altruism organisation; data subject; data holder
Source extract: shall also provide tools for easy withdrawal of such consent or permission
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Different actor class; merge only if actors generalised.

Title: Credentials and presentations use one profile
Requirement: In a data space that uses the Decentralized Claims Protocol, a credential and the presentation that carries it shall use the same data model version and the same proof mechanism.
Rationale: Mixed profiles inside one presentation cannot be verified by one verification path.
Source extract: the same data model version and proof mechanism MUST be used for both credentials and presentations
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Ecosystem spec, relevance to EBW open.

Title: Data space participant identifier is a DID
Requirement: A participant in a data space that uses the Decentralized Claims Protocol shall use a decentralized identifier as its participant identifier.
Rationale: A stable, resolvable identifier is the starting point for finding the credential service and the keys of a participant.
Source extract: This specification prescribes the Participant ID MUST be a DID.
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Ecosystem spec; conflicts possible with EUID based identification.

Title: BPN issued only with a Golden Record
Requirement: The BPN issuing organisation shall issue a Business Partner Number only if a corresponding Golden Record exists.
Rationale: Ties the ecosystem identifier to a validated data record, not to self-declaration.
Source extract: a BPN is only issued if a corresponding Golden Record exists

Rationale: Makes selective disclosure behaviour predictable for relying parties.
Source extract: whether an Attestation Provider MUST, MAY, or MUST NOT make that claim selectively disclosable
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Format-specific; tech-neutral only for SD-JWT VC rulebooks.

Title: Catalogue request carries namespace, identifier and version
Requirement: The requester of a catalogue entry for an attribute shall provide a namespace unique within the catalogue and an attribute identifier, unique within the namespace, together with the version of the attribute.
Rationale: Gives each attribute a stable, versioned identity so issued attestations are unaffected by later changes.
Source extract: an identifier of the attribute, unique within the namespace, and the version of the attribute
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Merge with INT-044 candidate; quote lacks namespace part.

Title: Catalogue request carries semantic description and data type
Requirement: The requester of a catalogue entry for an attribute shall provide a semantic description and the data type of the attribute.
Rationale: Machine and human readers need the meaning and type to interpret values.
Source extract: semantic description of the attribute; (g) the data type of the attribute
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Same Article 7(5) request content; merge or keep atomic by design choice.

Title: Scheme request declares attestation formats
Requirement: The scheme owner requesting a catalogue entry shall state the format or formats of the attestations within the scope of the scheme.
Rationale: Wallets and relying parties need to know which formats a scheme issues.
Source extract: the format or formats of electronic attestation of attributes within the scope of the scheme
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Same Article 8(3) request content as INT-046.

Title: Scheme request declares namespaces, identifiers, semantics and types
Requirement: The scheme owner requesting a catalogue entry shall state the namespaces, attribute identifiers, semantic descriptions and data types of each attribute in the scheme.
Rationale: Makes a scheme semantically complete and machine-checkable.
Source extract: one or more namespaces, attribute identifiers, semantic descriptions and data types of each attribute
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)

Title: Scheme attributes identifiable by unique identifiers
Requirement: A scheme requested for inclusion in the catalogue shall contain only attributes that are identifiable based on unique identifiers.
Rationale: Rules out free-text attribute names that cannot be resolved.
Source extract: shall only contain attributes that are identifiable based on unique identifiers
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)

Title: Commission maintains owner identification scheme in the catalogue
Requirement: The Commission shall establish and maintain an attestation scheme for European Business Wallet owner identification data and list it in the catalogue of schemes.
Rationale: Makes the owner identification attestation discoverable and semantically defined.
Source extract: That scheme shall be listed in the catalogue of schemes for the attestation of attributes
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K01 Credential data model and formats; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Check overlap with INT-004/005 owner identification data.

Title: SD-JWT VC attestations carry vct pointing to Type Metadata
Requirement: The issuer of an SD-JWT VC attestation shall include the vct claim and point it to the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata.
Rationale: The type identifier is the anchor for semantics in this format.
Source extract: The vct claim shall point to the SD-JWT VC Type Metadata
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Not technology-neutral; SD-JWT VC specific.

Title: Commission attributes the unique identifier of Union entities
Requirement: Where a public sector body is a Union entity, the Commission shall create and attribute a unique identifier to that Union entity.
Rationale: Union entities have no EUID, so the Commission acts as identifier authority.
Source extract: the Commission shall create and attribute a unique identifier to that Union entity
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Complements INT-006/INT-007.

Title: Equivalence of third-country frameworks by implementing act
Requirement: Where the Commission recognises a third-country framework as equivalent to European Business Wallets, the systems under that framework shall be interoperable with the trust framework of Regulation (EU) 910/2014 and shall support at least identification, authentication and the exchange of electronic attestations of attributes.
Rationale: Defines the only route by which third-country wallet frameworks gain EU recognition.
Source extract: provided that the systems provided under that framework are interoperable with the trust framework laid down in Regulation (EU) 910/2014
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: 'support at least identification, authentication, attestations' not in quote; overlaps INT-009.

Title: EU Company Certificate contains the EUID
Requirement: The EU Company Certificate for limited liability companies shall include the EUID of the company, the registration number and the Member State where the company is registered.
Rationale: Ties the certificate content to the primary identifier. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Source extract: the EUID of the company
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote only supports EUID; registration number and Member State come from DAT-008 list.

Title: Legal person data in person identification data
Requirement: The provider of person identification data for a legal person shall include the current legal name and a unique identifier constructed in accordance with the technical specifications for cross-border identification.
Rationale: Sets the minimum legal-person identity set in the in-force wallet framework.
Source extract: a unique identifier constructed by the sending Member State in accordance with the technical specifications
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K02 Wallet subject model; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote says 'constructed by the sending Member State'; 'cross-border' qualifier unverified.

Title: LEI and other optional identifiers in legal person data
Requirement: Where a provider of person identification data for a legal person includes a Legal Entity Identifier, it shall be the LEI referred to in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1860, alongside the other optional elements (VAT, tax reference, EUID, EORI, excise number).
Rationale: Names the secondary identifiers the in-force PID set already anticipates.
Source extract: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) referred to in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1860
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: List of optional elements (VAT, EORI, excise) not in quote.

Title: One EORI number per person
Requirement: The competent customs authority shall assign only one EORI number to each person.
Rationale: EORI is a customs identifier with one-per-person uniqueness that a secondary credential can rely on.
Source extract: Only one EORI number shall be assigned in respect of each person
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Binds customs authority; used only as uniqueness assumption.

Title: LEI as legal person identity type in certificates
Requirement: When the legal person semantics identifier is used, an LEI in the organizationIdentifier attribute shall be prefixed LEI with the country code XG followed by the LEI.
Rationale: Documents a non-KERI, standards-based carrier for the LEI in qualified seal certificates.
Source extract: "LEI" for a global Legal Entity Identifier as specified in ISO 17442
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Quote shows only the 'LEI' prefix; 'XG' country code not in quote.

Title: Core owner identification attributes presented atomically
Requirement: The holder shall present the core owner identification data attributes atomically, without selective disclosure.
Rationale: Records an ecosystem profile choice that differs from the general selective disclosure function.
Source extract: Selective Disclosure: Attributes of the EBWOID SHALL NOT be selectively disclosable.
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Tension with EBW-FUN-004 selective disclosure; flag for architecture decision.

Title: Receiving register retrieves data via interconnection of registers
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that the register where the company is being formed retrieves documents and information by means of exchange of information through the system of interconnection of registers.
Rationale: Defines register-to-register retrieval as the channel for company data in cross-border procedures. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 13g(2a) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: retrieves such documents and information by means of exchange of information through the system of interconnection of registers
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps FUN-047 (same article).

Title: EUID composition
Requirement: The EUID shall comprise, at least, elements making it possible to identify the Member State of the register, the domestic register of origin and the company number in that register.
Rationale: Fixes the minimum semantics a wallet parser or verifier can rely on when processing an EUID. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16(1), second subparagraph, of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: elements making it possible to identify the Member State of the register, the domestic register of origin and the company number
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps INT-060 and INT-006 partially.

Title: EUID structure under ISO 6523 with optional verification digit
Requirement: The structure of the EUID shall be compliant with ISO 6523 and shall contain a mandatory country code, a mandatory register identifier and a mandatory registration number, and may contain a verification digit.
Rationale: Gives a concrete syntax for parsing and validating the EUID in wallet attestations.
Source extract: The structure of the EUID shall be compliant with ISO 6523
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote supports only ISO 6523; mandatory elements and verification digit unverified.

Title: EUID identifies companies and branches in register exchanges
Requirement: The EUID shall be used to unequivocally identify companies and branches for the exchange of information between registers via the platform.
Rationale: Sets the EUID as the key in BRIS messages; a wallet should carry it as the cross-border register key.
Source extract: The EUID shall be used to unequivocally identify companies and branches for the purpose of the exchange of information between registers via the platform.
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Rationale 'wallet should carry it' is a design choice, not in source.

Title: Mutual accessibility of interconnections by unique identifier
Requirement: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts on the technical specifications and detailed list of data defining mutual accessibility between the system of interconnection of registers, the beneficial ownership registers interconnection and the insolvency registers interconnection, covering use of the unique company identifier.
Rationale: Provides the basis for cross-sector use of the EUID across registers that a wallet-based identification will meet. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 24(2), point (f), of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: shall cover the use of the unique identifier for companies attributed in accordance with Article 16
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Deadline-style authority procedure.

Title: Multilingual EU Company Certificate template published
Requirement: The Commission shall publish the multilingual template for the EU Company Certificate on the European e-Justice portal in all official languages of the Union.
Rationale: A common multilingual template gives wallets a stable semantic reference. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16b(8) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: The Commission shall publish the multilingual template for the EU Company Certificate on the European e-Justice portal
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote omits 'all official languages'; confirm full Article 16b(8) text.

Title: Implementing acts on EUCC and power of attorney wallet profile
Requirement: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts by 31 July 2026 establishing the technical specifications, including compatibility with the European Digital Identity Wallet, the taxonomy and the multilingual template for the EU Company Certificate and for the digital EU power of attorney.
Rationale: Technical profile for the certificate and the power of attorney in wallets; implementing acts were not found published when checked (October 2026). Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25). The Article 24(2) deadline of 31 July 2026 passed; no implementing regulation found in the Publications Office records up to 29 September 2026.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 24(2), points (d) and (e), of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: including compatibility with the European Digital Identity Wallet as provided for in Regulation (EU) 2024/1183
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote covers only compatibility clause; deadline and taxonomy unquoted. Rationale mixes publication-status finding into rationale.

Title: Register copies and extracts compatible with the EUDI Wallet
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that electronic copies and extracts of documents and information provided by the register are compatible with the European Digital Identity Wallet.
Rationale: Register output must be storable and presentable from wallets, including business wallets built on the same format. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16a(5) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: are compatible with the European Digital Identity Wallet as provided for in Regulation (EU) 2024/1183
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Same wallet-compatibility duty as TRU-095 (certificate) and TRU-098 (authentication); extracts vs certificate differ only in object.

Title: Documents available through BRIS in a standard message format
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that the documents and information referred to in Articles 14, 14a, 19(2), 19a(2) and 19b are available through the system of interconnection of registers in a standard message format and accessible by electronic means.
Rationale: Standardised formats enable machine consumption of register data. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 18(2) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: available through the system of interconnection of registers in a standard message format and accessible by electronic means.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps EBW-INT-058 and NFR-054 only thematically.

Title: EU Inc certificate and power of attorney fit business wallets
Requirement: The EU Company Certificate and the digital EU power of attorney of an EU Inc. shall be compatible with the European Business Wallets, where available.
Rationale: Proposed explicit wallet compatibility for company evidence of the new legal form.
Source extract: shall be compatible with the European Digital Identity Wallets
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote says European Digital Identity Wallets, statement says Business Wallets 'where available'; unsupported. Near-duplicate of INT-064/TRU-095.

Title: Core functionality specifications refer to accessibility requirements
Requirement: The standards and specifications defined in the implementing acts for the core functionalities of European Business Wallets shall refer to accessibility requirements.
Rationale: The Commission's digital statement says accessibility is catered for through the implementing acts, as for the EUDI Wallet; the operative articles of COM(2025) 838 contain no accessibility clause, so the statement is the only anchor (hence derived).
Sources: SRC-EBW-PROPOSAL (Legislative financial and digital statement, point 4.3 Digital solutions, column "How is accessibility catered for?")
Source extract: will refer to accessibility requirements as it was the case for the EUDIW
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Only a financial statement anchors it; duplicated by accessibility NFR/LEG set. Statement not testable.

Title: Authority portals use EN 301 549 V3.2.1 as conformance basis
Requirement: Public sector bodies shall use the harmonised standard EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03), whose reference is published in the Official Journal, as the basis for conformity of their websites and mobile applications with the Web Accessibility Directive.
Rationale: Content meeting the published harmonised standard is presumed to conform (Directive Article 6(1)); Decision 2021/1339 replaced V2.1.2 with V3.2.1, so the target version is fixed by the Official Journal reference (use of the standard is voluntary, hence a derived design choice).
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Duty binds public sector sites under Directive 2016/2102; presumption of conformity, not mandatory.

Title: Integrated signature application supports remote QSCD API
Requirement: Where a signature creation application relies on remote qualified signature creation devices and is integrated into the wallet back-end, it shall support the application programming interface set out in the implementing acts.
Rationale: Ensures remote signing interoperability across providers.
Source extract: they shall support the application programming interface set out in the implementing acts
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Same duty as INT-074 for the EUDI wallet; align on one API.

Title: Wallets integrate one specific qualified registered delivery service
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall integrate and support the use of a specific qualified electronic registered delivery service in accordance with Articles 43 and 44 of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014.
Rationale: The legal communication channel is a mandatory part of every wallet. (EP Amendment 137 allows one or more services; the Council wording designates a protocol and standards.)
Source extract: shall integrate and support the use of a specific qualified electronic registered delivery service
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Single versus several services differs between texts; check final wording.

Title: Delivery channel based on open royalty-free standards
Requirement: The Commission shall, by implementing act, ensure that the qualified electronic registered delivery service chosen as the mandatory channel is based on open, publicly available and royalty-free standards.
Rationale: Guarantees interoperability and avoids vendor lock-in.
Source extract: based on open, publicly available and royalty-free standards to guarantee interoperability and prevent vendor lock-in
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Authorities issue owner identification data per implementing acts
Requirement: Competent authorities shall ensure that owner identification data issued to wallet units complies with the technical specifications set out in the implementing acts.
Rationale: Common format makes owner identification data portable. (Council text places this duty on wallet providers.)
Source extract: comply with the technical specifications set out in the implementing acts
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Statement says competent authorities, rationale says Council places it on providers; resolve.

Title: Signature creation application supports the listed interface
Requirement: The signature creation application used by a wallet unit shall support at least the application programming interface referred to in Annex IV of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979.
Rationale: It makes remote signing interchangeable between wallets and trust service providers.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Article 2(7)(c), inserting Article 12(4) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979)
Actors: wallet provider; signature creation application provider
Source extract: shall support at least the application programming interface referred to in Annex IV
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: EUDI profile; business wallet relevance open. Overlaps INT-075 and INT-070.

Title: Signing interface specified by ETSI TS 119 432
Requirement: The application programming interface of the signature creation application of a wallet unit shall comply with ETSI TS 119 432 v1.3.1, clauses 6.4.3, A.6, A.7 and A.8.
Rationale: It replaces the earlier reference to the Cloud Signature Consortium specification and fixes how a relying party requests a signature from a wallet.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex VI, point 2, replacing point 3 of Annex IV to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979)
Actors: wallet provider; signature creation application provider
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Consider merging with INT-074 as one requirement with the clause reference; business wallet relevance open.

Title: Wallet provider uses token status lists for instance and key status
Requirement: The wallet provider shall use Token Status Lists as the revocation mechanism for both key attestations and wallet instance attestations.
Rationale: It fixes one format for the status of wallet components.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib), point 2(e), R_GEN-1)
Source extract: A wallet provider shall use Token Status Lists (specified in IETF Token Status List) as the revocation mechanism
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Business wallet relevance open.

Title: Revocation method for mdoc attestations
Requirement: The provider of person identification data, of qualified attestations or of public-sector attestations issued in the mdoc format shall use one of the following revocation methods: short-lived attestations of 24 hours or less, an attestation status list, or an attestation revocation list.
Rationale: It limits the choices of revocation mechanism for the mdoc format.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex IV (new Annex II), clause 6.2.10.1, EAA-6.2.10.1-02)
Actors: PID provider; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: shall use one of the following methods for revocation of person identification data
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Quote mentions person identification data only; extension to qualified and public-sector attestations is not shown.

Title: Relying party that checks status supports both mdoc mechanisms
Requirement: A wallet-relying party that needs to verify the revocation status of person identification data or attestations in the mdoc format shall support both the attestation status list mechanism and the attestation revocation list mechanism.
Rationale: Issuers may choose either mechanism, so a checking relying party must handle both.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex IV (new Annex II), clause 6.2.10.1, EAA-6.2.10.1-05.1)
Source extract: it shall support both the attestation status list mechanism and the attestation revocation list mechanism
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Business wallet relevance open.

Title: Status token for mdoc revocation carries an expiry
Requirement: The token carrying the revocation list or status list of an mdoc attestation shall contain an expiry claim.
Rationale: Relying parties need the time up to which they can rely on a cached list.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex IV (new Annex II), clause 6.2.10.1, EAA-6.2.10.1-08)
Actors: PID provider; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: the exp claim shall be present
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: Discovery of recipients and delivery capabilities
Requirement: Where providers of electronic registered delivery interoperate under the reference standards of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1944, they shall bind receiver identification to the OASIS Business Document Metadata Service Location specification and capability discovery to the OASIS Service Metadata Publishing specification.
Rationale: Gives senders a standard way to find the recipient endpoint and the capabilities of the receiving provider, which the business wallet digital address relies on.
Sources: SRC-ETSI-EN-319522-4-3 (Clause 4 (Common Service Interface bindings, general concepts))
Source extract: capability discovery service is bound to OASIS Service Metadata Publisher
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Quote supports capability discovery only; receiver identification binding not quoted.

Title: Presentation requests use the certificate-hash client identifier
Requirement: A wallet-relying party shall identify itself in a presentation request with the x509_hash client identifier prefix and sign the request.
Rationale: Fixes one relying party identification method for EU interoperability, so that any wallet can authenticate any registered relying party. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Source extract: The Authorization Request shall use the Client Identifier Prefix x509_hash.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Request signing is not in the quote; EUDI HAIP profile; business wallet use is open (DEC-07).

Title: Relayed delivery messages are signed and encrypted
Requirement: The sending provider shall sign and encrypt every AS4 message that relays an electronic registered delivery message to another provider.
Rationale: Protects integrity and confidentiality on the hop between providers, which the end-user signature does not cover.
Sources: SRC-ETSI-EN-319522-4-1 (Clause 5.3 (Signing and encryption of the AS4 message))
Source extract: All AS4 messages exchanged between the ERDS shall be signed and encrypted by the sending ERDS.
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: Relay between delivery providers uses the push pattern
Requirement: A provider that relays an electronic registered delivery message over AS4 shall use the push message exchange pattern only.
Rationale: One exchange pattern across providers avoids pull-based polling differences that would break interoperability.
Source extract: ERDS shall only use the push message exchange pattern.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K12 Registered delivery and notifications
Review note: Quote says ERDS (not only relay) uses push; AS4 scope and relay restriction come from clause context, check.

Title: BPN registered as an ISO/IEC 6523 identification scheme
Requirement: The structure of the Business Partner Number shall be registered as an organisation identification scheme under ISO/IEC 6523 with the Registration Authority under an International Code Designator.
Rationale: Makes the BPN interoperable with other registered organisation identifier schemes (for example LEI) and restricts issuance to one issuing organisation.
Source extract: MUST be registered as an organization identification scheme according to ISO/IEC 6523-1:2023
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: CX-Neptune preview, not certifiable. Cross-reference EBW-INT-060 (EUID compliant with ISO 6523). Rationale 'restricts issuance to one issuing organisation' is not in quote and conflicts with EBW multi-register and multi-provider model.

Title: Wallet identified by a DID using the did:web method
Requirement: The wallet shall be associated with a Decentralized Identifier following DID v1.0 and using the did:web method.
Rationale: Participant identity rests on a web-domain-bound identifier, not on a legal-entity register entry.
Source extract: The wallet MUST be associated with a Decentralized Identifier following the DID v1.0 specification and using the did:web method.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Conflict: did:web binds identity to a web domain, not to a legal register entry; EBW identity proofing binds to legal person data. Flag for DEC-11 and DEC-03.

Title: BPN-DID resolution service provided by CSP-B
Requirement: The core service provider-B shall provide the BPN-DID resolution service that maps the BPNL of a legal entity to its DID.
Rationale: Binds the ecosystem identifier of a legal entity to its decentralised identifier at a single authority.
Source extract: is a Core Service-B that MUST be provided by the Core Service Provider-B
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K05 Trust framework and discovery

Title: BPN-DID resolution only for onboarded legal entities
Requirement: The BPN-DID resolution service shall provide mapping data exclusively for onboarded legal entities referenced by their BPNLs.
Rationale: Resolution is limited to legal entities that passed onboarding.

Title: Protection from unauthorised access with reporting
Requirement: The manufacturer of a wallet that is a product with digital elements shall, where applicable, ensure protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms, including but not limited to authentication and identity or access management systems, and report on possible unauthorised access.
Rationale: Role corrected to manufacturer and 'where applicable' (risk-assessment based) condition restored; 'ensure protection' replaces the stronger 'protect the wallet'. Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027 (Article 71(2)).
Sources: SRC-CRA (Annex I, Part I, point (2)(d); Article 13(1))
Source extract: ensure protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: 'Report on possible unauthorised access' is not in quote; overlaps NFR-012.

Title: Confidentiality and integrity of stored and transmitted data
Requirement: The manufacturer of a wallet that is a product with digital elements shall, where applicable, protect the confidentiality of stored, transmitted or otherwise processed data and protect its integrity against unauthorised manipulation or modification, and report on corruptions.
Rationale: Removed 'using state-of-the-art encryption at rest and in transit' as a mandate: the clause gives encryption only as an example ('such as by encrypting relevant data at rest or in transit by state of the art mechanisms, and by using other technical means'). Role corrected to manufacturer; 'where applicable' restored. Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027 (Article 71(2)).
Sources: SRC-CRA (Annex I, Part I, point (2)(e) and (f); Article 13(1))
Source extract: protect the confidentiality of stored, transmitted or otherwise processed data, personal or other
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Merges confidentiality (Annex I(2)(e)) and integrity/reporting (2)(f); quote covers confidentiality only.

Title: Software bill of materials for vulnerability management
Requirement: The wallet provider shall identify and document vulnerabilities and components of the wallet, including a software bill of materials in a commonly used, machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies.
Rationale: Supply chain transparency lets operators and authorities assess exposure to a component vulnerability. Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027 (Article 71(2)).
Source extract: a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at the very least the top-level dependencies
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance

Title: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and contact point
Requirement: The manufacturer of a wallet that is a product with digital elements shall put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure and take measures to facilitate sharing of vulnerability information, including by providing a contact address for reporting vulnerabilities.
Rationale: Role corrected to manufacturer; the contact address is an example within the point (6) duty to facilitate information sharing about vulnerabilities (including in third-party components), not a stand-alone duty. Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027 (Article 71(2)).
Sources: SRC-CRA (Annex I, Part II, points (5) and (6))
Source extract: put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Contact address (point 6) not in quote.

Title: Support period of at least five years
Requirement: The manufacturer shall handle the wallet's vulnerabilities for a support period of at least five years, or the expected use time if shorter, and keep each security update available for 10 years or the remainder of the support period, whichever is longer.
Rationale: Added 'whichever is longer' (Art. 13(9)); original 'or the remainder of the support period' read as an alternative that could shorten retention. Role corrected to manufacturer.
