Support period is determined by the manufacturer to reflect expected use time, minimum five years unless expected use is shorter. Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027 (Article 71(2)).
Source extract: the support period shall be at least five years
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Quote covers only 5-year support period; update availability is Art 13(9).

Title: Early warning of actively exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours
Requirement: A manufacturer aware of an actively exploited vulnerability in its wallet product shall simultaneously notify the CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA via the single reporting platform, submitting an early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours.
Rationale: Role corrected to manufacturer; 'designated CSIRT' made precise as the CSIRT designated as coordinator (Art. 14(7)); notification is simultaneous and via the single reporting platform. Reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026 (recital 126 / Art. 71).
Source extract: an early warning notification of an actively exploited vulnerability, without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Quote omits CSIRT/ENISA recipients; add 72-hour and final reports; align with other incident clocks.

Title: Automatic event logging in high-risk AI systems
Requirement: The provider of a high-risk AI system shall ensure that the system technically allows for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
Rationale: Art. 12(1) is a requirement on high-risk AI systems; the provider duty to ensure compliance is Art. 16(a). Application to AI agents acting with wallet credentials is a derivation and holds only if the agent is classified high-risk under Art. 6 (Annex I/III); not every agent is. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Assumes agents are high-risk AI systems; obligation falls on the AI provider, not the wallet.

Title: Human ability to interrupt a high-risk AI system
Requirement: A high-risk AI system acting with wallet credentials shall allow assigned natural persons to intervene in its operation or interrupt it through a stop mechanism that brings it to a safe state.
Rationale: Revocation or suspension of an agent's mandate is the wallet-side means of enforcing this stop. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: intervene in the operation of the high-risk AI system or interrupt the system through a stop button
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Conditional on high-risk classification; mandate revocation mapping is derived.
Also covered: also held in EBW-AIF-037; also held in EBW-AIF-038

Title: Resilience of high-risk AI systems against manipulation
Requirement: A high-risk AI system acting with wallet credentials shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter its use, outputs or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities.
Rationale: Prompt or input manipulation of an agent holding signing authority would directly compromise a legal person. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Not testable without defined robustness criteria; conditional on high-risk status.

Title: Disclose interaction with an AI system
Requirement: The provider of an AI system intended to interact directly with natural persons shall design it so that those persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious from context.
Rationale: Agents negotiating or presenting credentials with human counterparties must identify themselves as AI.
Source extract: informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Applies to any AI system interacting with persons; not limited to agents with credentials.

Title: Registration of high-risk AI systems in the EU database
Requirement: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III, the provider shall register itself and the system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
Rationale: Registration status can serve as evidence when a wallet verifies an AI agent's compliance claims.
Source extract: shall register themselves and their system in the EU database referred to in Article 71
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Not a wallet or trust service obligation; evidence use is speculative. Keep only if an AI-compliance attestation is specified.

Title: Digital EU power of attorney data fields
Requirement: The digital EU power of attorney template shall include at least data fields about the scope of representation, the person authorised to represent the company and the type of representation.
Rationale: These fields are the minimum content a verifier can rely on when a mandate originates from company-law representation. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16c(4) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: which shall include at least data fields about the scope of representation, the person authorised to represent the company and the type of representation
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K01 Credential data model and formats; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Template is a Commission/MS obligation; wallet must carry these fields.

Title: Digital EU power of attorney authenticated by trust services
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that the digital EU power of attorney is authenticated by means of trust services referred to in Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 and that its granting, amendment or revocation is compatible for use with the European Digital Identity Wallet.
Rationale: A wallet-based mandate is only legally anchored if the power of attorney is sealed or signed through eIDAS trust services. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16c(1), third subparagraph, of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Actors: Member State; trust service provider; wallet provider
Source extract: authenticated by means of trust services as referred to in Regulation (EU) No 910/2014
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K05 Trust framework and discovery; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Two obligations; second half unsupported by recorded quote.

Title: Acceptance of digital EU power of attorney as evidence
Requirement: A body within the scope of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 shall accept the digital EU power of attorney as evidence of the authorised person's entitlement to represent the company as specified in the document.
Rationale: Relying parties cannot demand parallel proofs of representation for procedures within the Directive's scope. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16c(2) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: shall be accepted as evidence of the authorised person’s entitlement to represent the company as specified in the document
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)

Title: Suspension of a high-risk AI system presenting a risk
Requirement: When a deployer has reason to consider that use of a high-risk AI system acting with wallet credentials may present a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1), the deployer shall without undue delay inform the provider or distributor and the market surveillance authority and suspend its use.
Rationale: A mandate should be suspended when the agent behind it is found unsafe. Chapter III Sections 1-3 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III systems) or 2 August 2028 (Annex I systems) under Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
Source extract: shall, without undue delay, inform the provider or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authority, and shall suspend the use of that system
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Wallet-credential scoping is derivation; AI Act duty applies generally, so mark as D.

Title: Same legal effect as in-person or paper action
Requirement: Where an owner uses a core functionality of the European Business Wallet, the resulting action shall have the same legal effect as if it had been lawfully carried out in person, in paper form or by other compliant means.
Rationale: Gives public bodies and counterparties legal certainty to accept wallet-based acts.
Source extract: the resulting action shall have the same legal effect as if the action had been lawfully carried out in person, in paper form
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K12 Registered delivery and notifications
Review note: Proposal only; check final wording.

Title: Equivalence for sole traders using registered delivery
Requirement: Where a self-employed person or sole trader uses the qualified electronic registered delivery service under Article 5(3), the resulting action shall have the same legal effect as if carried out in person or in paper form.
Rationale: Sole traders without a full wallet get the same acceptance for registered delivery.
Source extract: Where a self-employed person or a sole trader makes use of the qualified electronic registered delivery service
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K12 Registered delivery and notifications
Review note: Second subparagraph of Article 4; could be kept as scope extension of LEG-049.

Title: Legal effect of Commission-issued owner identification data
Requirement: Owner identification data issued by the Commission shall have the same legal effect as qualified electronic attestations of attributes and attestations of attributes issued by a public sector body responsible for an authentic source.
Rationale: Union entities obtain a primary identity with the same standing as national owners.
Source extract: shall have the same legal effect as qualified electronic attestations of attributes
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Check statement says qualified EAA equivalence only; quote truncated.

Title: No disadvantage for those without a wallet
Requirement: Access to public and private services shall not be restricted or made disadvantageous to natural or legal persons that do not use European Digital Identity Wallets.
Rationale: Counterparties without a wallet must remain reachable by other identification means.
Source extract: shall not in any way be restricted or made disadvantageous to natural or legal persons that do not use European Digital Identity Wallets
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Obligation is on service providers, not the wallet; drives counterparty-without-wallet design.

Title: Presumption of integrity and identified sender and addressee
Requirement: Data sent and received using a qualified electronic registered delivery service shall enjoy the presumption of the integrity of the data, of sending by the identified sender, of receipt by the identified addressee and of the accuracy of date and time.
Rationale: Gives legal weight to delivery towards partners reached via a delivery service.
Source extract: shall enjoy the presumption of the integrity of the data, the sending of that data by the identified sender
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote ends at the sender clause; verify full list. 'shall enjoy' is a legal effect, not a design duty.

Title: Recognition of third-country trust services
Requirement: Trust services provided by trust service providers established in a third country shall be recognised as legally equivalent to qualified trust services only where recognised by an implementing act or by an agreement under Article 218 TFEU.
Rationale: Sets the legal route for equivalence of non-EU trust services (including attestations and seals).
Source extract: are recognised by means of implementing acts or an agreement concluded between the Union and the third country
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K05 Trust framework and discovery; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: The only-where restriction is implied by Article structure; fine.

Title: No legalisation for register documents, EUCC and power of attorney
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that the EU Company Certificate, the digital EU power of attorney and certified copies and extracts provided by a register are exempted from all forms of legalisation and any similar formality.
Rationale: Cross-border acceptance of these documents without extra formalities. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 16d(1) and (2) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as inserted by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: are exempted from all forms of legalisation and any similar formality.
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability

Title: EU Inc business communication shows company name and EUID
Requirement: The EU Inc. business related communication, in digital or paper form, shall contain the company name, EUID, registered office address, digital correspondence address and digital presence address.
Rationale: Proposed rule making EUID visible in business communication, supporting its use as business wallet identifier.
Source extract: business related communication, regardless if in digital or paper form, shall contain the following information
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Verify list of items in Article 29(1) is complete; 'digital presence address' definition unclear.

Title: Consumer-facing services designed to EAA requirements
Requirement: Where a service falls under Article 2(2) of Directive (EU) 2019/882, the service provider shall design and provide the service in accordance with the accessibility requirements of that Directive.
Rationale: The Directive binds economic operators for services provided to consumers; a business wallet provider is bound only if it also offers such a service (inference), for example a consumer-facing e-commerce or electronic communications service.
Source extract: Service providers shall ensure that they design and provide services in accordance with the accessibility requirements of this Directive.
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: EAA scope for a B2B wallet is an inference; consider merging LEG-057..061 into a conditional accessibility family.

Title: Accessibility information for services in terms and conditions
Requirement: The service provider shall include in its general terms and conditions, or an equivalent document, information assessing how the service meets the accessibility requirements, and shall make that information available to the public in written and oral format, including in a manner accessible to persons with disabilities.
Rationale: Tells users and authorities how the service meets accessibility rules; for a wallet it is a documentation and publication duty on the provider.
Source extract: Service providers shall prepare the necessary information in accordance with Annex V and shall explain how the services meet the applicable accessibility requirements.
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Written and oral format detail is not in the quote; Annex V point 1 not quoted.

Title: Procedures keep the service accessible over time
Requirement: The service provider shall ensure that procedures are in place so that the provision of the service remains in conformity with the applicable accessibility requirements, taking changes in the service, in the requirements and in the harmonised standards into account.
Rationale: Accessibility is lost through updates, so the provider needs a change process that re-checks conformity.
Source extract: service providers shall ensure that procedures are in place so that the provision of services remains in conformity with the applicable accessibility requirements
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability

Title: Corrective measures and notice on accessibility non-conformity
Requirement: Where a service does not comply with the applicable accessibility requirements, the service provider shall take the corrective measures necessary to bring it into conformity and shall immediately inform the competent national authorities of the Member States in which the service is provided.
Rationale: Gives the supervisor early sight of accessibility failures and requires a fix.
Source extract: service providers shall immediately inform the competent national authorities of the Member States in which the service is provided
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Quote covers only the notification; corrective measures part not in quote. Two obligations, arguably split.

Title: Demonstrate accessibility conformity to authority on request
Requirement: Upon a reasoned request from a competent authority, the service provider shall provide all information necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the service with the applicable accessibility requirements and shall cooperate with that authority.
Rationale: Makes conformity demonstrable, so the provider must keep evidence such as test results and the burden assessment.
Source extract: provide it with all information necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the service with the applicable accessibility requirements
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Cooperation clause not in quote.

Title: Document any fundamental-alteration or burden assessment
Requirement: Where an economic operator relies on fundamental alteration or disproportionate burden, it shall document the assessment, keep the results for five years after the service was last provided, and renew the burden assessment at least every five years.
Rationale: The only route to a lawful accessibility exception is a documented and refreshed assessment; a wallet provider that relies on it must keep the evidence.
Source extract: Economic operators shall document the assessment referred to in paragraph 2.
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Quote covers only documentation; five-year retention and renewal not in quote.

Title: Authority websites and apps meet web accessibility principles
Requirement: Public sector bodies shall take the necessary measures to make their websites and mobile applications more accessible by making them perceivable, operable, understandable and robust.
Rationale: Authority portals that receive wallet-based submissions or show wallet-derived data are public sector websites; the duty reaches Member State bodies, not the wallet provider (inference on the portal being in scope, see the research note).
Source extract: Member States shall ensure that public sector bodies take the necessary measures to make their websites and mobile applications more accessible
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Directive 2016/2102 binds Member States; portal in scope is an inference.

Title: Authority portal publishes an accessibility statement
Requirement: Public sector bodies shall provide and regularly update an accessibility statement on the compliance of their websites and mobile applications, including a feedback mechanism and a link to the enforcement procedure.
Rationale: Gives business users and regulators a way to see and challenge accessibility gaps of a B2G portal.
Source extract: provide and regularly update a detailed, comprehensive and clear accessibility statement on the compliance of their websites and mobile applications
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Feedback mechanism and enforcement link not in quote.

Title: Presumption of conformity for access control standards
Requirement: Compliance with the access control requirements of Annex point 12 shall be presumed where the standards, specifications and procedures set by the implementing acts are met.
Rationale: Gives providers a route to conformity through listed standards.
Source extract: Compliance with the requirements laid down in this Article shall be presumed where the standards, specifications and procedures
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Presumption of conformity is a legal effect, not a wallet obligation; quote cites Article, statement says Annex point 12 (quote truncated).

Title: Processor contract for provider processing
Requirement: Where the wallet provider processes personal data on behalf of an owner acting as controller, the processing shall be governed by a binding contract or other legal act under which the provider processes the data only on documented instructions of the owner.
Rationale: The owner is an organisation and its users are people, so the provider may be a processor for user-level data and then needs the Article 28 contract.
Source extract: shall be governed by a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Quote covers only the contract requirement; documented-instructions part is point (a), not quoted. Role is inference.

Title: Arrangement between joint controllers
Requirement: Where an owner and a wallet provider jointly determine the purposes and means of a processing operation, they shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities by an arrangement and make its essence available to the data subject.
Rationale: Joint determination of purposes and means makes both parties responsible towards users, so the split has to be written down.
Source extract: They shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities for compliance with the obligations under this Regulation
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Quote omits the data-subject availability part (Art 26(2)); whether provider and owner are joint controllers is open.

Title: Owner ensures measures for processing by its users
Requirement: An owner that is the controller shall ensure appropriate technical and organisational measures, including training and information of the users it authorises, so that processing by those users in the wallet complies with the data protection rules.
Rationale: Processing by employees within an organisation is presumed to take place under the organisation control, so the duty to ensure compliance sits with the owner. Source is an EDPB guideline (not binding); the underlying duty is Article 24(1) GDPR.
Sources: SRC-EDPB-GL-07-2020 (Paragraph 19 (Controller, notion of entity) with footnote 9)
Source extract: adequate technical and organizational measures, including e.g. training and information
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Source is non-binding EDPB guidance; true basis Art 24 GDPR. Provenance D with standard status; consider legal status guideline.

Title: Wallet authorisation changes do not alter legal mandates
Requirement: Granting, changing or revoking an authorisation of a user in the European Business Wallet shall not by itself create, limit or revoke any power of attorney or legal mandate of that user.
Rationale: Derived from Article 5(1)(j) (without prejudice to any power of attorney or legal mandate) and recital (17) (authorisations are of a technical nature); the Council text states no duty-holder, so the wallet provider is the derived addressee.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; wallet user
Source extract: without prejudice to any power of attorney or legal mandate
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K02 Wallet subject model; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Derivation stated. Art 5(1)(j) says "without prejudice"; "shall not by itself create, limit or revoke" is a derived reading and the provider as addressee is derived.

Title: Provider states who is responsible for each key
Requirement: The wallet provider shall state in its terms of service to the owner which party is responsible for the creation, protection and use of each private key, distinguishing the wallet provider, the owner and any qualified trust service provider.
Rationale: Derived (criterion C7 of the DEC-03 page): no source allocates liability for key misuse between provider, owner and trust service provider; the ARF discussion paper places signature creation compliance on the QTSP; legal review needed, to verify.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: Although the liability on signature creation compliance is on the QTSP, the Wallet Unit shall follow applicable requirements to enable compliance of the involved QTSP.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Quote comes from a non-normative ARF discussion paper and does not reach the duty. Statement is a proposed disclosure, not law; needs legal review.

Title: Recognition of notified eID means across Member States
Requirement: Where electronic identification and authentication is required to access an online service of a public sector body, the Member State shall recognise an electronic identification means issued in another Member State under a listed scheme if its assurance level, substantial or high, is equal to or higher than the level the service requires.
Rationale: Sets the cross-border assurance rule for representatives who authenticate to a business wallet or a public service with an eID means from another Member State; it does not cover private relying parties or third countries.
Source extract: shall be recognised in the first Member State for the purposes of cross-border authentication for that service online
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Conditions (listed scheme, level) come from the full Art 6(1), not the quote. Research read the 2014 text; the consolidated text was not obtained: verify against SRC-EIDAS-CONSOL. Statement correctly limits scope to public sector.

Title: Agreements recognising third-country trust services require equivalent requirements
Requirement: An agreement under which trust services of a third country are recognised as legally equivalent to qualified trust services shall ensure that the requirements applicable to qualified trust service providers in the Union and their qualified services are met by the third-country providers and services.
Rationale: Article 14(2)(b) adds reciprocity (Union qualified services recognised in the third country); only point (a) is stated here. Without such an agreement a third-country seal or signature has no qualified effect.
Source extract: requirements applicable to qualified trust service providers established in the Union and the qualified trust services they provide are met
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Only point (a); reciprocity (b) omitted. Related LEG-054. Duty-holder is the agreement (Union), acceptable.

Title: Transfers of personal data to third countries meet Chapter V
Requirement: Any transfer of personal data to a third country or an international organisation shall take place only if the controller and processor comply with the conditions of Chapter V of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, including for onward transfers.
Rationale: Applies when a business wallet provider or relying party moves personal data of representatives to partners outside the Union; the wallet provider mapping is a derivation.
Source extract: the conditions laid down in this Chapter are complied with by the controller and processor
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Faithful to Art 44. Mapping to the wallet provider is a derivation.

Title: Appropriate safeguards where no adequacy decision exists
Requirement: In the absence of an adequacy decision, a controller or processor shall transfer personal data to a third country or an international organisation only if it has provided appropriate safeguards and enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies are available.
Rationale: Most third-country partners of a business wallet will lack an adequacy decision, so safeguards such as standard data protection clauses are the normal route.
Source extract: In the absence of a decision pursuant to Article 45(3), a controller or processor may transfer personal data to a third country
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Art 46(1) "may transfer ... only if" restated; consider merging with LEG-073 or LEG-076.

Title: No wallet services to persons listed under EU asset-freeze measures
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall not make funds or economic resources available, directly or indirectly, to or for the benefit of natural or legal persons, entities or bodies listed in Annex I to Regulation (EU) No 269/2014, and shall assess whether wallet and owner identification services are economic resources within the meaning of that prohibition.
Rationale: Derived: Article 2(2) of Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 prohibits making funds or economic resources available to listed persons and Article 17 applies it to EU-incorporated operators worldwide; that wallet services are economic resources is an interpretation to verify, and other EU sanctions regimes (for example Regulation (EU) No 833/2014) need the same check.
Source extract: No funds or economic resources shall be made available, directly or indirectly, to or for the benefit of natural persons or natural or legal persons
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Restated within Reg 269/2014 Art 2(2), quote machine-checked; provenance D. Wallet services as economic resources and other regimes (833/2014) still to verify by legal review.

Title: Third-country wallet equivalence does not replace GDPR transfer rules
Requirement: Where the exchange of attestations of attributes with a third-country wallet or framework recognised under Article 17 involves a transfer of personal data, the controller shall ensure that the conditions of Chapter V of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 are met.
Rationale: Derived: equivalence of assurances under Article 17 weighs data protection standards but is not an adequacy decision under GDPR Article 45, so it cannot replace Chapter V.
Actors: controller; provider of European Business Wallets
Source extract: allow for the support of at least an identification and authentication functionality and the exchange of electronic attestations of attributes
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Quote (Art 17(1) functionality) does not reach the statement; the point that equivalence is not an Art 45 adequacy decision is a legal interpretation to confirm. Restates LEG-073 for this context.

Title: Delegates of EU Inc. directors are bound by directors' legal obligations
Requirement: An individual to whom the directors of an EU Inc. company have delegated powers shall adhere to the legal obligations imposed on directors when exercising the delegated powers.
Rationale: Delegation by directors does not remove the legal duties attached to the power, which a wallet mandate for a delegate has to respect.
Actors: EU Inc. companies; delegate of a director
Source extract: to individuals who, in exercising the delegated powers, shall adhere to any legal obligations imposed on directors
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Source is a Commission proposal (COM(2026) 321, not adopted); may change in trilogue. Duty-holder is the delegate individual, not the wallet. Quote is truncated before 'delegated by directors'.

Title: Several directors of an EU Inc. represent the company jointly by default
Requirement: Where an EU Inc. company has several directors, the directors shall represent the company jointly.
Rationale: Joint representation is the default rule; the individual-representation exception is in Article 43(2), covered by EBW-LEG-053. A wallet mandate model has to be able to express two or more signatories acting together (see EBW-TRU-168).
Source extract: If the EU Inc. company has several directors, they shall represent the company jointly
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Matches Art 43(1) quote. Rationale cites EBW-LEG-053 for the Art 43(2) individual-representation exception, but LEG-053 is eIDAS Art 43(2) (registered delivery presumption); the EU Inc. Art 43(2) item is not in the catalogue. Fix the rationale reference (no item exists yet). Complements TRU-168 (joint signatories); not a duplicate.

Title: Users can remove all data and settings from a product permanently
Requirement: The manufacturer of a device or software that is a product with digital elements shall, where applicable, ensure that users can securely and easily remove permanently all data and settings and, where the data can be transferred to other products or systems, that the transfer is secure.
Rationale: Supports decommissioning of a device that holds wallet keys or credentials; role is the manufacturer under Article 13(1), and the duty is subject to the risk assessment ("where applicable"). Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 applies from 11 December 2027.
Sources: SRC-CRA (Annex I, Part I, point (2)(m); Article 13(1))
Source extract: provide the possibility for users to securely and easily remove on a permanent basis all data and settings
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Duty-holder manufacturer; 'where applicable' kept; applies from 11 Dec 2027. Quote omits the transfer clause (end of Annex I (2)(m)); consider extending the quote.

Title: Device records access to and modification of data, services and functions
Requirement: The manufacturer of a product with digital elements shall, where applicable, ensure that the product provides security-related information by recording and monitoring relevant internal activity, including access to or modification of data, services or functions, with an opt-out mechanism for the user.
Rationale: Gives a device-level source for a machine's own activity record, a precondition for attributing the machine's acts to its owner; role is the manufacturer under Article 13(1).
Sources: SRC-CRA (Annex I, Part I, point (2)(l); Article 13(1))
Source extract: provide security related information by recording and monitoring relevant internal activity, including the access to or modification of data, services or functions
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Matches Annex I (2)(l) including opt-out. Applies only 'where applicable' per risk assessment.

Title: Export of wallet data and records
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall enable the export of owner identification data, electronic attestations of attributes, communication logs and interaction records in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format at the owner's request or on termination of service or revocation of the provider's notification.
Rationale: Ensures portability and avoids lock-in.
Source extract: export their data, including issued European Business Wallet owner identification data, electronic attestations of attributes, communication logs, and interaction records
Clusters: K01 Credential data model and formats; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps LEG-014, FUN-031, LEG-029, OPS-002; consolidate export requirements. Triple trigger (request, termination, revocation) is acceptable.

Title: Access to a log of all transactions
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall enable the owner to access a log of all transactions.
Rationale: Provides auditability for the owner.
Source extract: access a log of all transactions
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Owner access to log of all transactions; NFR-013 defines what is logged, NFR-014 integrity. Keep as owner-access requirement.

Title: Technical and organisational measures for CIA and interoperability
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, interoperability and availability of its wallets with other business wallets and European Digital Identity Wallets.
Rationale: Sets the overall security and interoperability duty.
Source extract: confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, interoperability, and availability
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Vague 'appropriate measures'; mixes security properties and interoperability.

Title: Directory access limited to owners, representatives and providers
Requirement: The Commission shall make the European Digital Directory accessible only to owners, their authorised representatives and providers of European Business Wallets.
Rationale: Limits exposure of directory content.
Source extract: only accessible to European Business Wallet owners and their authorised representatives and providers of European Business Wallets
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K09 Privacy and data protection; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Obligation sits on the Commission; the design obligation is on the directory (restrict access). Reword as 'The directory shall...'.

Title: Accessible and plain-language trust services
Requirement: Providers of electronic identification means, trust services and the end-user products used for them shall make them available in plain and intelligible language, in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and the accessibility requirements of Directive (EU) 2019/882.
Rationale: Ensures accessibility of wallet-related user interfaces and trust services.
Source extract: made available in plain and intelligible language, in accordance with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Quote cites UN CRPD, statement cites Directive 2019/882; the accessibility reference is not in the quote.

Title: Trustworthy systems and cryptography
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall use trustworthy systems and products protected against modification that ensure technical security and reliability, including suitable cryptographic techniques.
Rationale: Core security requirement for all qualified services.
Source extract: use trustworthy systems and products that are protected against modification and ensure the technical security and reliability
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: 'Trustworthy' and 'suitable cryptographic techniques' not testable; tie to certification and crypto policy (see NFR-021, LEG-026). Quote lacks 'including suitable cryptographic techniques'.

Title: Protection against forgery and data tampering
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall take appropriate measures against forgery, theft or misappropriation of data and against unauthorised deletion, alteration or rendering data inaccessible.
Rationale: Protects integrity and availability of issued data and evidence.
Source extract: take appropriate measures against forgery, theft or
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Quote truncated at 'forgery, theft or'; the deletion and alteration part is not visible. Not testable as written; overlaps NFR-006.

Title: Remote signature creation data managed only by qualified provider
Requirement: Generating, managing or duplicating electronic signature creation data shall be carried out only on behalf of and at the request of the signatory by a qualified provider of remote creation device management.
Rationale: Restricts custody of signing keys, relevant to remote signing and sealing for legal persons.
Source extract: only on behalf of the signatory, at the request of the signatory, and by a qualified trust service provider
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Passive voice, no actor. Check applicability to seals via CER-006. Strong architecture driver for remote sealing in EBW.

Title: Limited backup of remote signature creation data
Requirement: The qualified provider managing remote signature creation devices shall duplicate creation data only for back-up, at the same security level as the original and with no more copies than needed for continuity.
Rationale: Controls key duplication risk.
Source extract: the number of duplicated datasets must not exceed the minimum needed to ensure continuity of the service
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Quote covers only the minimum number of copies; 'only for back-up' and 'same security level' are not shown.

Title: Logical separation of attestation service data
Requirement: The provider of attestation services shall keep personal data relating to the service logically separate from other data it holds.
Rationale: Data separation for privacy.
Source extract: shall be kept logically separate from other data held by the provider of electronic attestation of attributes
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Same Article 45h; combine with LEG-005 (no combination of personal data) and NFR-011.

Title: Functional separation of qualified attestation service
Requirement: The provider of qualified electronic attestation of attributes services shall implement the service in a manner functionally separate from its other services.
Rationale: Prevents cross-service leakage.
Source extract: in a manner that is functionally separate from other services provided by them
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: 'Functionally separate' is not testable without definition; applies to qualified EAA providers only.

Title: Wallet user authentication before any function
Requirement: The wallet unit shall not perform any wallet function other than wallet user authentication until the wallet unit has successfully authenticated the wallet user.
Rationale: Prevents use of a lost or unattended wallet.
Source extract: Wallet units shall not perform any functionality listed in Article 5a(4) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, except wallet user authentication
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Source is CIR 2024/2979 for EUDI wallets; EBW applicability must be confirmed. Reword 'any wallet function' to refer to the Article 5a(4) functions.

Title: Log all wallet transactions including failed ones
Requirement: The wallet instance shall log all transactions with wallet-relying parties and other wallet units, including electronic signing and sealing, irrespective of whether the transaction completes.
Rationale: Gives users and auditors a complete record of data sharing.
Source extract: wallet instances shall log all transactions with wallet-relying parties and other wallet units, including electronic signing and sealing.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: 'Irrespective of whether the transaction completes' is not in the quote. Also overlaps NFR-002, NFR-019.

Title: Log integrity, user consent for provider access, and export
Requirement: The wallet provider shall ensure integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the transaction log, shall access it only where necessary for the wallet service and on explicit prior consent of the wallet user, and shall enable the wallet user to export it.
Rationale: Protects the log from tampering and the user from silent monitoring.
Source extract: on the basis of explicit prior consent by the wallet user.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Combines integrity, consented access and export; source locations 9(3), 9(5), 9(7) differ, quote only covers consent.

Title: No presentation before authentication, policy and approval
Requirement: The wallet unit shall not present requested attributes until it has verified that the wallet user was authenticated by the secure cryptographic application, that embedded disclosure policies were processed, and that the user approved the presentation in part or in full.
Rationale: Ensures user control over every disclosure.
Source extract: do not present any requested attributes to wallet-relying parties or wallet units until the following requirements are met
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Three conditions; consider structured list. Overlaps NFR-017 and FUN-004, FUN-030.

Title: Revocation techniques hinder linkability
Requirement: Providers of qualified attestations and of public-sector authentic-source attestations shall set up revocation techniques that are privacy preserving and hinder linkability and traceability.
Rationale: Status checking must not become a tracking channel.
Source extract: revocation techniques and management methods that are privacy preserving and hindering linkability or traceability.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Overlaps NFR-018 and TRU-031. Statement scope (qualified and public sector attestations) not visible in quote.

Title: User approval before presenting any attribute
Requirement: The wallet unit shall ensure that the user approved the presentation of any attribute prior to presenting it, and shall always allow the user to refuse.
Rationale: Consent is the gate for each disclosure.
Source extract: A Wallet Unit SHALL ensure the User approved the presentation of any attribute(s) in the Wallet Unit to a Relying Party or Verifier Wallet Unit
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Duplicate of NFR-015 with additional 'always allow refusal'; keep that clause when merging.

Title: Random status list indices and herd privacy
Requirement: When using an attestation status list, the provider shall randomly assign the index of each attestation and shall represent a sufficiently large number of attestations per list to ensure herd privacy.
Rationale: Prevents the status index becoming a correlator.
Source extract: SHALL randomly assign the index for each PID or attestation, to prevent this index from becoming a correlator.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Technology-specific (status list index); reword neutrally as 'unpredictable status identifier' if neutrality is wanted. ARF text may change.

Title: Transaction log excludes presented attribute values
Requirement: For presentation and wallet-to-wallet transactions, the wallet unit shall not store the values of presented attributes in the transaction log.
Rationale: The log itself must not become a data leak.
Source extract: the log SHALL NOT contain the value of any attributes presented to the Relying Party or the Verifier Wallet Unit.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Tension with NFR-013/NFR-002 and audit needs; resolve explicitly (log metadata, not values).

Title: Intermediary deletes attributes right after forwarding
Requirement: An intermediary shall delete any attestations and user attributes obtained from the wallet unit completely and immediately after sending the attributes to the intermediated relying party.
Rationale: Limits data retention by intermediaries.
Source extract: SHALL delete any PIDs or attestations it obtained from the Wallet Unit, including any User attributes, completely and immediately
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: 'Completely and immediately' is ambiguous for logs and backups. Intermediary is not an EBW function; confirm applicability.

Title: Wallet attestations use ECCG agreed cryptographic mechanisms
Requirement: When issuing, presenting or verifying a wallet instance attestation or key attestation, the participants shall use only cryptographic algorithms included in the ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0.
Rationale: Fixes an algorithm baseline for interoperability and review.
Source extract: SHALL only use cryptographic algorithms included in the ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms v2.0.
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Hard-wires v2.0 of a document; breaks crypto agility. 'Participants' is vague.

Title: Token requests name the target MCP server
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent acts as an MCP client, the MCP client shall include the resource parameter (RFC 8707) identifying the target MCP server in both authorization requests and token requests.
Rationale: Audience-restricted tokens stop a token granted for one tool server from being replayed against another.
Source extract: MUST identify the MCP server that the client intends to use the token with.
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Protocol-specific (MCP), not technology-neutral; keep as AIF profile.

Title: MCP server validates token audience
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent exposes an MCP server, the MCP server shall validate that each access token was issued specifically for it as the intended audience.
Rationale: It enforces the security boundary between wallet-facing tools and other services.
Source extract: MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: MCP-specific.

Title: No token passthrough by MCP servers
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent exposes an MCP server, the MCP server shall not accept or forward any token that was not issued for that server.
Rationale: Token passthrough breaks accountability: downstream logs would attribute the action to the wrong identity.
Source extract: MCP servers MUST NOT accept or transit any other tokens.
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: MCP-specific.

Title: Per-client consent in MCP proxy servers
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent operates an MCP proxy server in front of a third-party API, the proxy shall keep a per-user registry of approved client IDs and obtain consent for each client before forwarding to the third-party authorization flow.
Rationale: It prevents the confused-deputy attack that obtains tokens without the user's explicit approval.
Source extract: MCP proxy servers MUST implement per-client consent and proper security controls
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: MCP-specific; narrow deployment.

Title: Explicit consent before one-click local server setup
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent supports one-click configuration of local MCP servers, it shall show the exact command without truncation, identify it as a dangerous operation and require explicit user approval before running it.
Rationale: A local server runs with the privileges of the client, which in a wallet context can reach key material.
Source extract: Show the exact command that will be executed, without truncation
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Does not belong in NFR if EBW rarely supports local MCP servers.

Title: Least-privilege scopes for agent tokens
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent acts as an MCP client, the MCP client shall request only the scopes necessary for the intended operation and elevate incrementally through step-up authorization.
Rationale: Narrow scopes limit the damage if an agent token is stolen and keep audit trails meaningful.
Source extract: MCP clients SHOULD follow the principle of least privilege by requesting only the scopes necessary
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Source says SHOULD; statement hardens to shall and adds step-up. State derivation in rationale.

Title: A2A server authenticates every request
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent implements A2A as a server, it shall authenticate every incoming request based on the credentials provided and its declared authentication requirements.
Rationale: Declared securitySchemes are only meaningful if each call is checked.
Source extract: MUST authenticate every incoming request based on the provided credentials and its declared authentication requirements.
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: A2A-specific.

Title: A2A authorisation checks on every operation
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent implements A2A as a server, it shall perform authorisation checks on every A2A operation and limit results to the authenticated caller's authorised boundaries.
Rationale: It prevents one counterparty from seeing the tasks of another.
Sources: SRC-A2A (Section 13.1 Data Access and Authorization Scoping)
Source extract: Servers MUST implement authorization checks on every A2A Protocol Operations request
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: A2A-specific.

Title: Extended Agent Card requires authentication
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent offers an A2A extended Agent Card, it shall require authentication, using a scheme declared in the public card, before returning it.
Rationale: Extended cards may carry organisation-specific capabilities that must not be public.
Sources: SRC-A2A (Section 13.3 Extended Agent Card Access Control)
Source extract: The Get Extended Agent Card operation MUST require authentication
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: A2A-specific.

Title: In-band credentials bound to the originating agent
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent passes in-task credentials in-band through a chain of A2A agents, the credentials shall be bound to the agent that originated the request.
Rationale: Otherwise any intermediary agent in the chain could reuse a credential issued for the originator.
Source extract: Credentials SHOULD be bound to the agent which originated the request
Clusters: K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Source SHOULD; rationale does not mark derivation.

Title: Audit trail for sensitive agent operations
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent implements A2A, the agent shall keep audit trails for sensitive operations and shall exclude credentials and unneeded personal data from the logs.
Rationale: The specification says SHOULD for trails and MUST NOT for sensitive log content; both are needed to attribute agent actions.
Source extract: Agents SHOULD provide audit trails for sensitive operations
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Two obligations (trail, log content); derivation stated. Overlaps NFR-033/035 and NFR-013.

Title: Audit logs record principal and agent separately
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent acts under delegated authority, the policy enforcement point shall record distinct identifiers for the human or legal-person principal and for the agent instance that performed each action.
Rationale: It makes agent actions attributable for compliance and forensics.
Source extract: unambiguously record not only who authorized an action but also which specific agent instance performed it
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Key AI-first accountability requirement; mark provenance derived if statement exceeds quote.

Title: Sender-constrained agent tokens
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent uses DPoP sender-constrained tokens, the resource server shall ensure that the public key from the DPoP proof matches the key bound to the access token.
Rationale: It stops a leaked agent token from being replayed by another party.
Source extract: Resource servers supporting DPoP MUST ensure that the public key from the DPoP proof matches the one bound to the access token.
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: DPoP-specific; conditional on using DPoP.

Title: Every authenticated agent request leaves a trace
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent uses workload identity for authentication, each authenticated request shall leave a verifiable and inspectable trace regardless of the authorisation decision.
Rationale: Denied requests are as relevant for incident analysis as granted ones.
Source extract: Each authenticated request MUST leave a verifiable and inspectable trace regardless of authentication and authorization decision.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: NFR-013 logs failed wallet transactions; keep only if agent scope needed.

Title: Agent signing keys protected, hardware-backed where available
Requirement: Where the wallet or an agent holds a DID authentication key, the key shall be protected against disclosure and shall use hardware-backed storage, an HSM or a secure enclave where available.
Rationale: The specification says SHOULD for hardware; agent keys that sign on behalf of a legal person warrant that.
Source extract: Hardware-backed key storage, an HSM, or a system secure enclave SHOULD be used where available.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Statement hardens SHOULD to shall for disclosure protection; hardware part conditional.

Title: User keeps full control of wallet use and data
Requirement: The European Digital Identity Wallet shall leave the user in full control of the use of and of the data in the wallet.
Rationale: A personal wallet cannot be controlled by an employer, which limits employer-managed use.
Source extract: Users shall have full control of the use of and of the data in their European Digital Identity Wallet
Clusters: K02 Wallet subject model; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Rationale on employer control is interpretation; Article 5a(14) concerns EUDI wallet, not EBW.

Title: No collection of wallet usage data beyond necessity
Requirement: The provider of the European Digital Identity Wallet shall not collect information about the use of the wallet which is not necessary for the provision of wallet services.
Rationale: Prevents profiling of wallet users, including professional use.
Source extract: shall neither collect information about the use of the European Digital Identity Wallet which is not necessary
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps LEG-008/LEG-007 on minimal processing; keep if wallet-usage telemetry is specific.

Title: Logging policy for signing, sealing and notifications
Requirement: The European Business Wallet provider shall provide a logging policy covering at least electronic signing, electronic sealing and notifications of all transactions, whether or not completed.
Rationale: Council text, not the Commission proposal. Makes acts of users attributable and auditable.
Source extract: shall provide an appropriate logging policy that shall include, at a minimum, electronic signing, electronic sealing, and notifications
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Council position, not adopted law; overlaps NFR-013 and NFR-002.

Title: Provider access to logs where necessary for the service
Requirement: The European Business Wallet provider shall access transaction logs only where this is necessary for the provision of the wallet services.
Rationale: Council text, not the Commission proposal. The Council text drops the prior consent condition that applies to personal wallets.
Source extract: shall be accessible to the European Business Wallets provider, where it is necessary for the provision of European Business Wallets services
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Overlaps NFR-014 consent condition; Council divergence. Verify against Commission proposal.

Title: Access events logged with verifiable proofs of authorisation
Requirement: The European Business Wallet provider shall log and timestamp all access and execution events and bind them to cryptographically verifiable proofs of authorisation suitable for audit and legal proceedings.
Rationale: Council text, not the Commission proposal. Makes it provable on whose authority an act was done.
Source extract: all access and execution events are logged, timestamped, and bound to cryptographically verifiable proofs of authorisation
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Council text; overlaps NFR-033 conceptually.

Title: Import of owner data from another provider
Requirement: The European Business Wallet provider shall enable owners to import their exported data to benefit from data portability across wallet providers.
Rationale: Council text, not the Commission proposal. Completes exit and switching beyond export.
Source extract: import their data as listed under point (l) to benefit from data portability across
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Council text; export is NFR-001/LEG-014, import is additional obligation.

Title: Unlinkability across relying parties
Requirement: The wallet solution shall enable privacy preserving techniques which ensure unlinkability across different relying parties where the attestation does not require identification of the wallet user.
Rationale: Stops relying parties from correlating the same holder.
Source extract: enable privacy preserving techniques which ensure unlinkability where the electronic attestations of attributes do not require the identification of the wallet user
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps NFR-016 revocation unlinkability; this one is broader.

Title: Cryptographic agility by modular design
Requirement: The wallet provider shall design wallet and trust-service components so that cryptographic algorithms and parameters can be replaced without redesigning the surrounding protocols or systems.
Rationale: A post-quantum transition is only feasible when cryptographic components are replaceable. Derived: the NIS Cooperation Group roadmap only recommends this and is not binding law.
Sources: SRC-NISCG-PQC-ROADMAP (Section 6.3 (Next Steps), first item; definition of cryptographic agility in Section 3.2)
Source extract: When new products are being developed, support for cryptographic agility should be considered at first.
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Derivation marked; make measurable (algorithm replaceable by configuration).

Title: Agility without in-protocol cipher suite negotiation
Requirement: The wallet provider shall not rely on run-time cipher suite negotiation as the means of achieving cryptographic agility unless downgrade attacks are demonstrably prevented.
Rationale: The roadmap warns that negotiating suites during protocol execution often leads to downgrade attacks.
Source extract: This concept must not be confused with a requirement to negotiate the cipher suite during protocol execution
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Quote is a clarification of a definition, not an obligation; consider drop or "should".

Title: Post-quantum mechanisms combined with classical mechanisms
Requirement: When the wallet provider deploys post-quantum asymmetric mechanisms, it shall use them in hybrid mode with a classically secure mechanism so that all combined mechanisms must be broken simultaneously to break the hybrid.
Rationale: Hybrid use protects against regressions in the newer post-quantum schemes.
Source extract: These hybrid modes shall ensure that all combined pre or post-quantum cryptographic mechanisms need to be broken simultaneously
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: Use recommended cryptographic suites for new signatures and seals
Requirement: The trust service provider shall use only recommended cryptographic mechanisms and key sizes to generate new signatures and seals, and shall use legacy mechanisms only where needed for interoperability with existing infrastructures.
Rationale: Fixes a clear baseline for algorithm selection and phase-out.
Sources: SRC-ETSI-TS-119312 (Clause 4, Use of SOG-IS Agreed Mechanisms)
Source extract: only SOG-IS recommended mechanisms and key sizes or cryptographic suites using these cryptographic mechanisms and key sizes should be used
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Source says "should"; legacy exception unsupported.

Title: Audit log time synchronised with UTC daily
Requirement: The trust service provider shall synchronise the time used to record events in the audit log with UTC at least once a day.
Rationale: Accurate event times underpin evidence value and incident reconstruction.
Source extract: The time used to record events as required in the audit log shall be synchronized with UTC at least once a day.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Transaction logs stay accessible as long as law requires
Requirement: The wallet provider shall keep the transaction logs accessible for as long as they are required by Union or national law.
Rationale: Sets the retention horizon of wallet logs by reference to law rather than a fixed period.
Source extract: shall remain accessible for as long as they are required by Union law or national law
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps NFR-014/013 on log availability; retention horizon is additional.

Title: ERDS signing key in a certified secure cryptographic device
Requirement: The registered delivery service provider shall hold and use the signing private key within a secure cryptographic device certified to Common Criteria EAL 4 or higher, or, until 31 December 2030, FIPS 140-3 level 3.
Rationale: Fixes key protection and shows a dated sunset for one certification route.
Source extract: The ERDS signing private key shall be held and used within a secure cryptographic device which is a trustworthy system certified
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance

Title: ERDS uses ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms
Requirement: The registered delivery service shall select and use cryptographic techniques in accordance with the Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms endorsed by the European Cybersecurity Certification Group and published by ENISA.
Rationale: Ties algorithm choice for registered delivery to an official, periodically updated list.
Source extract: The ERDS shall select and use suitable cryptographic techniques in accordance with the Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K12 Registered delivery and notifications
Review note: Same rule as NFR-021 for wallet attestations; generalise.

Title: Availability of the relying-party register API
Requirement: The national register of wallet-relying parties shall provide security functions, including security by default and by design, that ensure the availability and integrity of its common API and of the information available through it.
Rationale: Wallets depend on the register for relying-party verification.
Source extract: ensure the availability and integrity of the API and the availability of information through it
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Authority-side register operator duty; not design of EBW.

Title: No storage of personal data transmitted via the interconnection
Requirement: Member States shall ensure that registers, authorities and persons or bodies mandated under national law do not store personal data transmitted through the system of interconnection of registers for the purposes of Articles 13g, 28a and 30a, unless otherwise provided by Union or national law.
Rationale: Data-minimisation rule for transferred representative data that a wallet-side relying party must also respect. Member States apply the national measures from 31 July 2028 (Article 4(2) of Directive (EU) 2025/25).
Sources: SRC-DIR-2025-25 (Article 18(6) of Directive (EU) 2017/1132 as amended by Directive (EU) 2025/25)
Source extract: do not store personal data transmitted through the system of interconnection of registers for the purposes of Articles 13g, 28a and 30a
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Rationale claims wallet-side relying parties must respect it; not supported by quote.

Title: Security measures for BRIS communication
Requirement: Communication and distribution of information via BRIS shall include measures for confidentiality, integrity, non-repudiation of origin and receipt, security event logging, and authentication and authorisation of users and systems.
Rationale: Baseline security profile for register interconnection that counterpart wallet services can mirror.
Source extract: measures to ensure the non-repudiation of origin of the sender of information within BRIS and the non-repudiation of receipt of information;
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote covers non-repudiation only; other measures need quotes. Standard-derived (S), not a wallet duty.

Title: Wallet accessible for persons with disabilities
Requirement: Providers of European Digital Identity Wallets shall make the wallets accessible for use by persons with disabilities on an equal basis with other users, in accordance with Directive (EU) 2019/882.
Rationale: The EUDI Wallet is the personal counterpart of the business wallet; the proposal for the business wallet builds on the same framework, and whether it carries an equivalent provision in its annex was not verified.
Source extract: shall be made accessible for use, by persons with disabilities, on an equal basis with other users
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Accessibility of the personal wallet; see NFR-056 for the business wallet.

Title: Business wallet interfaces meet the same accessibility level
Requirement: The user interfaces of a European Business Wallet for authorised users shall meet at least the accessibility level that applies to European Digital Identity Wallets.
Rationale: Assumption to verify: the text of COM(2025) 838 read contains no accessibility provision for persons with disabilities (its annex was not available), eIDAS Article 15 covers trust services and end-user products used for them, and the scope of Directive (EU) 2019/882 for business-facing services was not analysed. Employees with disabilities use the wallet as users (see DEC-02).
Source extract: shall be made accessible for use, by persons with disabilities, on an equal basis with other users
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Derivation class D; the proposal text read has no accessibility provision for persons with disabilities.

Title: Business wallet accessible for persons with disabilities
Requirement: Providers of European Business Wallets shall make the European Business Wallets they provide accessible for use by persons with disabilities on an equal basis with other users.
Rationale: The Council text adds an accessibility duty for business wallet providers that the Commission proposal lacks, and it is the business wallet counterpart of the duty for EUDI Wallets (EBW-NFR-055); it would turn the assumption in EBW-NFR-056 into text.
Source extract: make the European Business Wallets they provide accessible for use, by persons with disabilities, on an equal basis with other users
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Council text, not Commission proposal; may not survive trilogue. Overlaps EBW-NFR-055/056 in intent.

Title: Wallet accessibility measured against EAA Annex I
Requirement: Providers of European Business Wallets shall provide accessibility for persons with disabilities in accordance with Annex I of Directive (EU) 2019/882, to the extent relevant.
