Rationale: Recital 20 of the Council text names the accessibility yardstick for the wallet, so the wallet's accessibility claims can be checked against a defined list; it is a recital, so the operative duty is the one in Article 6(2)(ea).
Source extract: including in accordance with Annex I of Directive (EU) 2019/882, to the extent relevant
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Recital is not operative; fold into NFR-057 as the yardstick.

Title: Service information through more than one sensory channel
Requirement: The service provider shall make the information about the functioning of the service available via more than one sensory channel, present it in an understandable way and make its content available in text formats that can generate alternative assistive formats.
Rationale: Users who cannot see or hear need the same service information in another form; it applies to wallet help and onboarding information.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2019-882 (Annex I, Section III, second indent)
Source extract: making the information available via more than one sensory channel
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Quote shows only the sensory-channel part; text-format part is rest of the indent.

Title: Service websites and apps: perceivable, operable, robust
Requirement: The service provider shall make the websites, including the related online applications, and the mobile device-based services, including mobile applications, through which a service is provided accessible in a consistent and adequate way by making them perceivable, operable, understandable and robust.
Rationale: This is the core user interface duty of the Directive for services; for a wallet it covers the web console and the mobile app where those are part of a service in scope.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2019-882 (Annex I, Section III, third indent)
Source extract: making websites, including the related online applications, and mobile device-based services, including mobile applications, accessible in a consistent and adequate way
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: Duplicates the WCAG target of NFR-063; keep the legal one as parent.

Title: Support services give accessibility information in accessible modes
Requirement: Where support services such as help desks, call centres and technical support are available, they shall provide information on the accessibility of the service and its compatibility with assistive technologies in accessible modes of communication.
Rationale: Users with disabilities need a support route they can use; it links to the support mechanism the Council text requires for business wallet owners.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2019-882 (Annex I, Section III, fourth indent)
Source extract: providing information on the accessibility of the service and its compatibility with assistive technologies, in accessible modes of communication
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability

Title: Identification and e-signature in consumer flows are accessible
Requirement: Where identification methods or electronic signatures are provided as part of an e-commerce or consumer banking service, they shall be perceivable, operable, understandable and robust.
Rationale: Derived mapping: when a wallet authentication or signing function is used inside a consumer e-commerce or consumer banking transaction (an inference, as the wallet is a business instrument), the Directive's wording applies to that function.
Sources: SRC-DIR-2019-882 (Annex I, Section IV, points (e)(i) and (g)(iii))
Source extract: providing identification methods, electronic signatures, and payment services which are perceivable, operable, understandable and robust
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Weak fit for a business wallet; consider dropping if B2C is out of scope.

Title: Wallet web interfaces satisfy WCAG 2.1 Level AA via clause 9
Requirement: Where a wallet interface is a web page, it shall conform to clauses 9.1 to 9.4 and the conformance requirements of clause 9.6 of EN 301 549 V3.2.1, which is equivalent to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
Rationale: Gives a testable, reusable target for the business wallet's web console and for authority portals; WCAG 2.2 is not part of this version.
Actors: Business wallet provider; Public sector body
Source extract: Conformance with W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1) [5] Level AA is equivalent to conforming with all of clauses 9.1 to 9.4
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Quote supports equivalence; scope to wallet interfaces is application, not stated in standard.

Title: Wallet mobile and desktop apps meet EN 301 549 clause 11
Requirement: Where a wallet interface is software that is not a web page, it shall conform to the applicable requirements of clause 11 of EN 301 549 V3.2.1, including interoperability with assistive technology and platform user preferences.
Rationale: Wallet apps are mostly non-web software; clause 11 is where their accessibility is specified, including following system contrast and font settings.
Source extract: Requirements for non-web documents and non-web software are given in clauses 10 and 11 respectively.
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Whether EN 301 549 binds the business wallet is open.

Title: Documents provided by the wallet meet EN 301 549 clause 10
Requirement: Where a wallet provides downloadable documents that are not web pages, such as receipts, notices or reports, they shall conform to the applicable requirements of clause 10 of EN 301 549 V3.2.1.
Rationale: Delivery receipts, evidence and reports are documents; the standard treats downloadable documents separately from web pages, and V3.2.1 added them to the public sector mapping.
Source extract: the present clause applies to downloadable documents
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: No single biometric as the only authentication means
Requirement: Where the wallet uses biological characteristics, it shall not rely on a particular biological characteristic as the only means of user identification or for control of the wallet.
Rationale: Users who lack a given characteristic would be excluded; the same idea appears in Annex I of Directive 2019/882 for products ("alternative to biometrics identification and control"), and it bears on wallet unlocking and user authentication.
Source extract: it shall not rely on the use of a particular biological characteristic as the only means of user identification or for control of ICT
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Biometrics unlikely central to a hosted business wallet.

Title: Accessible documentation and support communication
Requirement: The wallet provider shall make product documentation available in a web format conforming to clause 9 or a non-web format conforming to clause 10 of EN 301 549, and its support services shall accommodate the communication needs of individuals with disabilities directly or through a referral point.
Rationale: Instructions, accessibility help and the support route that the Council text requires for business wallet owners must themselves be usable by people with disabilities.
Source extract: ICT support services shall accommodate the communication needs of individuals with disabilities either directly or through a referral point.
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Two obligations; overlaps NFR-061.

Title: Wallet units meet Web Accessibility Directive requirements
Requirement: Wallet Providers shall ensure that their Wallet Units comply with the applicable requirements and standards in the directive on the accessibility of websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies.
Rationale: The EUDI ARF adds the Web Accessibility Directive for wallet units beyond the Directive 2019/882 duty in eIDAS Article 5a(21); the text cites "Directive 2016/2012" and the note cites EN 301 549 V1.1.2, both apparently outdated or mistyped (the Directive is 2016/2102, the published version V3.2.1), so a business wallet should follow the Directive and the OJ-referenced standard.
Source extract: Wallet Providers SHALL ensure that their Wallet Units comply with applicable requirements and standards in Directive 2016/2012
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Source cites Directive 2016/2012 (likely typo); statement silently corrects the number, mark the derivation.

Title: Back-end uses secure cryptographic application and device
Requirement: The European Business Wallet back-end shall use at least one wallet secure cryptographic application and wallet secure cryptographic device to manage critical assets.
Rationale: Business wallets are server-side, so critical assets must sit behind a tamper-resistant device.
Source extract: shall use at least one Wallet secure cryptographic application and Wallets secure cryptographic device to manage critical assets
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Protected channels between wallet components
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall ensure integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the communication between the wallet back-end, front-end and secure cryptographic applications and device.
Rationale: Splits across front-end, back-end and device would otherwise expose critical assets in transit. (EP Amendment 131 extends this to communication within and among all components.)
Source extract: ensure integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the communication between the Business Wallet’s back-end, front-end and secure cryptographic applications and device
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: One channel, three properties; acceptable as atomic.

Title: Cryptographic operations only after user authentication
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic applications and devices shall perform cryptographic operations involving critical assets, other than those needed to authenticate the owner, only where they have successfully authenticated the wallet user.
Rationale: Prevents key use by an unauthenticated session.
Source extract: only in cases where those applications have successfully authenticated Wallets users
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Secure generation of new cryptographic keys
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic applications and devices shall be able to securely generate new cryptographic keys.
Rationale: Keys must originate inside the protected environment.
Source extract: are able to securely generate new cryptographic keys
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Duplicates generation clause of EBW-FUN-028 (CIR), different source (proposal Annex); keep both or split FUN-028.

Title: Secure erasure of critical assets
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic applications and devices shall be able to perform secure erasure of critical assets.
Rationale: Needed for deactivation, provider change and termination.
Source extract: are able to perform secure erasure of critical assets
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Duplicates erasure clause of EBW-FUN-028; see also EBW-OPS-017.

Title: Proof of possession of private keys
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic applications and devices shall be able to generate a proof of possession of private keys.
Rationale: Underpins key binding of attestations to the unit.
Source extract: are able to generate a proof of possession of private keys
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Duplicates proof-of-possession clause of EBW-FUN-028.

Title: Protection of private keys during their lifetime
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic applications and devices shall protect the private keys they generate during the existence of the keys.
Rationale: Key compromise defeats every other control.
Source extract: protect the private keys generated by these Wallets secure cryptographic applications and devices during the existence of the keys
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Not testable without a defined protection level; tie to certification.

Title: Transaction log records relying party identity
Requirement: The wallet transaction log shall record the name, contact details and unique identifier of the corresponding relying party and its Member State of establishment, or, for other wallet units, relevant information from the wallet unit attestation.
Rationale: Makes each transaction attributable to a counterparty.
Source extract: the name, contact details, and unique identifier of the corresponding Business-Wallet-relying party and the Member State
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps NFR-013 on logging scope.

Title: Transaction log records data types requested and presented
Requirement: The wallet transaction log shall record the type or types of data requested and presented in each transaction.
Rationale: Supports accountability and data-protection review without storing values.
Source extract: the type or types of data requested and presented in the transaction
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Transaction log records reason for non-completion
Requirement: For each non-completed transaction, the wallet transaction log shall record the reason for the non-completion.
Rationale: Failed transactions must be explainable for support and audit.
Source extract: in the case of non-completed transactions, the reason for such non-completion
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of logs
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall ensure integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the logged information.
Rationale: Logs are evidence and carry business data. (The Council text adds availability.)
Source extract: ensure integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the logged information
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: NFR-014 already requires integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the transaction log (CIR basis).

Title: Back-end logs reports sent to competent authorities
Requirement: The wallet back-end shall log reports sent by the wallet user to competent authorities via the wallet unit, including interactions on notifications, regulatory compliance, data sharing and audit requests.
Rationale: Gives owners proof of what was reported to whom (B2G reporting).
Source extract: shall log reports sent by the Wallets user to the competent authorities via the Wallets unit
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)

Title: Logs accessible for as long as law requires
Requirement: The wallet logs of transactions shall remain accessible for as long as Union or national law requires them to be accessible.
Rationale: Retention follows the legal duty, not provider convenience; counterpart of EBW-NFR-049.
Source extract: shall remain accessible for as long as required to be accessible by Union law or national law
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Same obligation as EBW-NFR-049, different source.

Title: Export and portability of owner data at LoA substantial
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall support the secure export and portability of the owner's wallet data in at least an open format, so that the owner can migrate to another wallet solution, ensuring a level of assurance of at least substantial.
Rationale: Prevents lock-in. The Council text replaces the assurance condition by user authentication per point 1 and adds import; EP Amendment 136 adds import.
Source extract: secure export and portability of an owner’s European Business Wallet data in at least an open format
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K01 Credential data model and formats; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Assurance level substantial clause is not in the quote. Overlaps FUN-031 and NFR-001.

Title: Delivery channel provides end-to-end encryption
Requirement: The Commission shall, by implementing act, ensure that the qualified electronic registered delivery service chosen as the mandatory channel provides end-to-end encryption.
Rationale: Confidentiality of legal communications must not depend on the provider.
Source extract: provides end-to-end encryption to guarantee confidentiality
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Statement binds the Commission via implementing act; design duty falls on the ERDS. Check Annex point 11(2)(d) wording.

Title: Credential visibility conditioned on access rights
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall ensure that the visibility of credentials and attestations is selective and conditioned on the access rights of the acting subject.
Rationale: Staff and agents must see only what their role permits.
Source extract: visibility of credentials and attestations is selective and conditioned on access rights
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Overlaps FUN-010/FUN-035; testability depends on defined roles.

Title: Only the secure application runs critical-asset operations
Requirement: The wallet provider shall ensure that the wallet secure cryptographic application is the only component able to execute wallet cryptographic operations and any other operation with critical assets in the context of electronic identification at assurance level high.
Rationale: It confines the use of keys to one certified component, which decides what a hosted or device-based architecture must isolate.
Source extract: are the only components able to execute wallet cryptographic operations and any other operation with critical assets
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Applies to EUDI at LoA high; business wallet relevance is open.

Title: Wallet instance uses a secure cryptographic device
Requirement: The wallet provider shall ensure that each wallet instance uses at least one wallet secure cryptographic device to manage critical assets.
Rationale: It sets the minimum key custody for EUDI Wallets and is the reference point for a business wallet back-end.
Source extract: Wallet instances shall use at least one wallet secure cryptographic device to manage critical assets.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Business wallet relevance is open; parallels NFR-069.

Title: Protected channel between wallet instance and secure application
Requirement: The wallet provider shall ensure the integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the communication between wallet instances and wallet secure cryptographic applications.
Rationale: A hosted secure application or remote device is only as trustworthy as the channel to it.
Source extract: Wallet providers shall ensure integrity, authenticity and confidentiality of the communication between wallet instances and wallet secure cryptographic applications.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Parallels NFR-070 (proposal).

Title: Secure application does not export private keys
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic application shall not enable the export of private keys from the wallet secure cryptographic device.
Rationale: Non-exportable keys keep custody with the device, and make the exit path re-creation of keys rather than copying.
Source extract: A WSCA SHALL NOT enable export of private keys from a WSCD.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Tension with NFR-082 export: only keys excluded.

Title: Keys protected throughout their lifetime
Requirement: The wallet secure cryptographic application and device shall protect each private key they generated during the entire lifetime of the key, preventing its extraction in the clear.
Rationale: Key protection must cover generation, use, backup and end of life, not only storage.
Source extract: SHALL protect a private key it generated during the entire lifetime of the key
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Extraction-in-the-clear clause not in quote; drop or source it.

Title: Isolation of assets of different units on a shared device
Requirement: Where a wallet secure cryptographic application, device or keystore holds cryptographic assets of several wallet units, the wallet provider shall ensure that a wallet unit can access only the assets related to that unit.
Rationale: A provider-operated hardware module can serve many units, and one unit must never reach the keys of another.
Source extract: the Wallet Provider SHALL ensure that a Wallet Unit can only access assets that are related to that Wallet Unit
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K02 Wallet subject model

Title: Wallet provider does not read wallet contents
Requirement: The wallet provider shall not access the contents of a wallet instance, in particular the attestations present, their status, the attribute values and the transaction log.
Rationale: It limits what a provider that also hosts keys or data can see; the business wallet texts allow provider log access where necessary, so the two rules differ.
Source extract: SHALL NOT access the contents of a Wallet Instance
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Enumerated contents not in quote. Conflicts with NFR-040 and NFR-014; resolve in key custody decision.

Title: Strict access controls for contents hosted at the provider
Requirement: Where the contents of a wallet unit are stored in a service on the wallet provider back-end, the wallet provider shall specify and implement strict controls that limit its own access to those contents.
Rationale: A hosted architecture cannot rule out provider access technically, so the controls must be defined and auditable.
Source extract: SHALL specify and implement strict controls to limit access by the Wallet Provider to the contents of the Wallet Unit
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K09 Privacy and data protection; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Testability depends on defining "strict controls"; audit-based.

Title: Only the legitimate instance reaches a remote security module
Requirement: When a remote hardware security module holds critical assets of a wallet unit, the wallet provider shall take measures ensuring that only the legitimate wallet instance can access that module and use those assets.
Rationale: It is the access control that makes a provider-hosted key store acceptable for a single unit.
Source extract: the Wallet Provider takes appropriate measures to ensure that only the legitimate Wallet Instance can access the remote HSM
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Remote signing key usable only with consent
Requirement: The provider of a remote signature creation service shall allow a signing key to be used only in cases for which the signer consent has been obtained.
Rationale: It is the control that keeps a provider-held key under the control of its owner.
Source extract: Signing keys shall be usable in only those cases for which the signer's consent has been obtained.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)

Title: Explicit approval by the natural person for a legal-person signer
Requirement: Where the signer is a legal person and the authentication is linked directly to the identity, the signature activation protocol of a remote signature creation service shall include an explicit action of the natural person, identified during identity verification and allowed to sign in the name of the legal person, to approve the authorisation.
Rationale: It shows how a business key held remotely is still tied to an accountable natural person at the moment of use.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; authorised representative
Source extract: an explicit action (not just a checkbox) of the natural person identified during the identity verification process
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Directly relevant to business seal or signature held remotely.

Title: Signing key generated in a qualified creation device
Requirement: A qualified provider managing a remote qualified signature or seal creation device shall generate the signing key of the signer in a qualified signature creation device.
Rationale: It sets where the keys of a qualified remote service come into existence.
Source extract: Signer's signing key shall be generated in a QSCD.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance

Title: Session limit for identity-based remote signing
Requirement: Where the authentication is linked directly to the identity, a qualified provider managing a remote qualified creation device shall end the signature session at most 30 minutes after the end of the identity verification process.
Rationale: It bounds how long a verified identity can be used to activate a hosted key.
Source extract: the signature session shall end at most 30 minutes after the end of the identity verification process
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Wallet status lists cover at least 10 000 attestations where possible
Requirement: The wallet provider shall size its wallet instance attestation status lists, taking account of scale and architecture, so that they are large enough to prevent correlation and, where possible, relate to at least 10 000 attestations.
Rationale: List size is the privacy of status checks, and a small provider or a business wallet with few units gives a small list.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib), point 2(e), R_WIA-5)
Source extract: At a minimum, a status list shall, where possible, relate to at least 10 000 attestations.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Scale/architecture clause is not in quote. Business wallet with few units cannot reach 10 000 easily.

Title: Fresh unlinkable index for each instance attestation
Requirement: Where a wallet provider does not reuse one status index per credential issuer, it shall assign a fresh, unlinkable index value to each wallet instance attestation it issues.
Rationale: A reused index would let issuers link their interactions with the same unit.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib), point 2(e), R_WIA-3)
Source extract: the wallet provider shall assign a fresh, unlinkable index value to each wallet instance attestation it issues
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K07 Credential lifecycle

Title: Instance attestation shown only to issuers
Requirement: A wallet unit shall present a wallet instance attestation only to a provider of person identification data or an attestation provider as part of issuance, and not to a relying party or any other entity.
Rationale: Showing the attestation to relying parties would expose a tracking handle and is not how EUDI Wallets are verified; the business wallet texts and the WE BUILD rulebook differ.
Source extract: SHALL present a WIA only to a PID Provider or Attestation Provider
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Conflicts with TRU-109 and TRU-010 where unit attestation is shown to authorities or relying parties.

Title: Key attestation shown only to issuers
Requirement: A wallet unit shall present a key attestation only to a provider of person identification data or an attestation provider as part of issuance of a person identification data or key-bound attestation, and not to a relying party or any other entity.
Rationale: It keeps the key attestation from becoming a correlation handle at relying parties.
Source extract: SHALL present a KA only to a PID Provider or Attestation Provider
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Pair with NFR-100; atomic on its own.

Title: Portability stays available during a suspension
Requirement: Measures taken on the suspension of a wallet solution shall not hinder affected wallet users from exercising their right to data portability, provided this is possible without impairing the security of the critical assets.
Rationale: Users must be able to leave a suspended solution.
Source extract: shall not hinder affected wallet users from exercising their right to data portability
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K09 Privacy and data protection; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: "Hinder" is vague; test via export capability during suspension (see FUN-031).

Title: Status index and list address unique per credential
Requirement: The provider of an mdoc attestation shall ensure that the combination of status index and status list address is unique per mobile security object.
Rationale: A shared index would let relying parties correlate presentations.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex IV (new Annex II), clause 6.2.10.1, EAA-6.2.10.1-13.2)
Actors: PID provider; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: the combination of status index and URI shall be unique per MSO
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Absorbs NFR-108 (double allocation) for mdoc.

Title: No authentication to download status lists
Requirement: A provider of person identification data, an attestation provider or a wallet provider shall not require a relying party to authenticate itself before downloading an attestation status list or attestation revocation list.
Rationale: Authenticated downloads would tell the issuer who checks which list.
Actors: PID provider; attestation provider; wallet provider
Source extract: SHALL NOT require the Relying Party or Relying Party Instance to authenticate itself before downloading
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K07 Credential lifecycle; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: PID validity status published in a privacy-preserving way
Requirement: Where providers of person identification data revoke person identification data issued to wallet units, they shall make the validity status of the data they issue publicly available in a privacy preserving manner and indicate the location of that information in the data.
Rationale: It is the PID counterpart of the rule for wallet unit attestations.
Source extract: they shall make publicly available the validity status of person identification data they issue, in a privacy preserving manner
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Counterpart of TRU-031 for PID; EUDI-only unless EBW issues PID-like data.

Title: Fresh status list entry for every re-issued token
Requirement: Where a credential is re-issued, the issuer shall allocate a fresh status list entry to the re-issued credential.
Rationale: Re-using an entry would make the index a correlation handle across re-issuances.
Source extract: every re-issued Referenced Token MUST have a fresh Status List entry
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection

Title: Dedicated status entry for each token of a batch
Requirement: Where credentials are issued in batches for one-time use, the issuer shall give every credential of the batch a dedicated status list entry.
Rationale: A shared entry would let verifiers link the members of a batch.
Source extract: every Referenced Token MUST have a dedicated Status List entry
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection

Title: No double allocation of status list entries
Requirement: The status issuer shall prevent any unintended double allocation of a status list address and index to more than one credential.
Rationale: Address and index together are a unique identifier that can be used for tracking.
Sources: SRC-IETF-TSL (Section 13.3 Default Values and Double Allocation)
Source extract: The Status Issuer MUST prevent any unintended double allocation.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Generic version of NFR-103 (unique index and address); merge, keep both sources.

Title: Presentation responses are encrypted
Requirement: The wallet shall encrypt the authorisation response that carries a presentation to the wallet-relying party.
Rationale: Protects the disclosed attributes from intermediaries and from the browser or platform layer that relays the response. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Source extract: The EUDI Wallet shall encrypt the authorization response.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K09 Privacy and data protection; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: EUDI profile; bearing on business wallet open.

Title: Wallet attestation does not identify one wallet instance
Requirement: A wallet attestation presented to an issuer shall not be reused across issuers and shall not carry an identifier specific to a single wallet instance.
Rationale: A per-instance identifier in the attestation would let issuers collude to link the same wallet across services. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Source extract: They MUST NOT introduce a unique identifier specific to a single Wallet instance.
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: No-reuse-across-issuers clause not in quote; verify against HAIP 4.4.1.

Title: Mediating API sees attestation types, not attributes
Requirement: By default the wallet shall disclose to a mediating operating system or browser interface only the presence of the types of stored attestations, and shall not disclose their attributes or values.
Rationale: Limits what the platform layer learns about a user or an organisation when a request is routed through it. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Source extract: The EUDI Wallet shall by default disclose the presence of all stored EAAs' type to the mediating API
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K08 Protocols and interfaces; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: EUDI profile; bearing on business wallet open.

Title: Directory processing uses pseudonymisation where appropriate
Requirement: The Commission shall implement the European Digital Directory in accordance with data protection principles, including, where appropriate, features of pseudonymisation.
Rationale: The Directory holds personal data of economic operators, including sole traders, and the proposal asks for pseudonymisation features where they fit.
Sources: SRC-EBW-PROPOSAL (Recital 39; legislative financial statement, digital policy table (European Digital Directory))
Source extract: include, where appropriate, features of pseudonymisation
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Vague, not testable; design impact on wallet is nil.

Title: Issuers cannot track use after issuance
Requirement: The business wallet provider shall ensure that attestation providers and other parties cannot, after issuance, obtain data that allows transactions or user behaviour to be tracked, linked or correlated unless the owner explicitly authorises it.
Rationale: Article 5a(16) states this for the EUDI Wallet; the proposal has no matching text, so the project needs an explicit requirement or a decision not to apply it.
Source extract: to obtain data that allows transactions or user behaviour to be tracked, linked or correlated
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K07 Credential lifecycle; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Art 5a(16)(a) binds EUDI wallets; extension to business wallet is a project decision.

Title: List of assets subject to logging
Requirement: A trust service provider shall establish a list of the assets that are subject to logging, based on the result of its risk assessment, and keep it reviewed.
Rationale: Makes the scope of logging explicit and auditable instead of leaving it to each system.
Source extract: The relevant entities shall establish a list of assets to be subject to logging
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Quote says "relevant entities"; CIR 2024/2690 may not cover trust service providers. Verify scope.

Title: Logs kept, backed up and protected for a defined period
Requirement: A trust service provider shall maintain and back up its logs for a predefined period and shall protect them from unauthorised access or changes.
Rationale: A log that can be altered or lost cannot serve as evidence of what the service did.
Source extract: shall maintain and back up logs for a predefined period
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Quote lacks the protection clause and the TSP scope. Overlaps NFR-079 and NFR-081.

Title: Audit events cannot be easily deleted or destroyed
Requirement: A trust service provider shall log events in a way that they cannot be easily deleted or destroyed during the period in which they are required to be held, except where reliably transferred to long-term media.
Rationale: Tamper resistance of the audit trail is the base of the evidential value of the records.
Source extract: The events shall be logged in a way that they cannot be easily deleted or destroyed
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: "Easily" is not testable; consider defining tamper evidence. Overlaps NFR-079.

Title: Creation data protectable against use by others
Requirement: A qualified electronic signature creation device shall ensure, by appropriate technical and procedural means, that the electronic signature creation data can be reliably protected by the legitimate signatory against use by others.
Rationale: It is the device-level basis for sole control of signing keys and applies to seals through Article 39.
Source extract: can be reliably protected by the legitimate signatory against use by others
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Quote matches. Seals via Art 39. Related CER-006.

Title: Migration object contains no private keys
Requirement: The migration object of a wallet unit shall not contain private keys of PIDs or device-bound attestations.
Rationale: Keys do not move between wallet solutions, so exit means re-creating keys and re-issuing attestations; stated for the EUDI Wallet, no EBW text says whether keys can move.
Source extract: SHALL NOT contain any private keys of the PID or device-bound attestation
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: EUDI-only (Mig_03). Reviewer may demote or drop; verify topic number. Relates to OPS-042.

Title: Provider-held keys used only on the authority of the owner
Requirement: Where a wallet provider holds private keys of an owner in its back-end, the wallet provider shall ensure that those keys are used only on the authorisation of the owner's authorised users and not by the wallet provider itself.
Rationale: Derived (criteria C1, C7 of the DEC-03 page): Article 26(1)(c) sets sole control for advanced signatures and Article 36(1)(c) control for advanced seals, but no EBW text applies this to a non-qualified provider-hosted key.
Source extract: created using electronic signature creation data that the signatory can, with a high level of confidence, use under his sole control
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K02 Wallet subject model; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Derivation stated. Art 26(1)(c) is "sole control" of the signatory; for seals Art 36(1)(c) is weaker ("under control"). Add Art 36(1)(c) to location and treat as derived for non-qualified keys.

Title: Log names the authorised user for each signing or sealing
Requirement: The wallet provider shall record in the transaction log, for each use of a signing or sealing key, the authorised user who triggered it.
Rationale: Derived (criteria C4, C14 of the DEC-03 page): the log content in Annex point 7(2) names the relying party and data types but not the user, so use of one seal key by several users cannot be attributed.
Source extract: shall include, at a minimum, electronic signing, electronic sealing, and notifications of all transactions
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Rationale cites Annex 7(2) while location says 7(1): verify numbering. Check against privacy rules on logs (NFR-014, NFR-040).

Title: Audit trail records changes to accounts and access rules
Requirement: The asset interface shall keep, as a minimum, audit events for unauthorised access attempts, changes to identity configuration, changes to accounts of applications and users, and changes to access rules.
Rationale: Derived; shows who granted, changed or withdrew machine and user authority and when, which is what an owner needs to answer for acts of its machines.
Sources: SRC-IDTA-AAS-P4 (Part 4 (IDTA-01004 v3.1), AAS Security requirements, FR2, Auditable Events, Table 1 (S1 to S4))
Source extract: As a minimum the events listed in Table Table 1 SHALL be kept in an AAS interface audit trail.
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Event list in the statement (unauthorised access attempts, identity configuration, accounts, access rules) comes from Table 1, not the quote; check against IDTA-01004 v3.1 Table 1 (S1 to S4 security levels may differ). Derived (D stated). Related to NFR-116 and NFR-048 audit-log items.

Title: Each auditable event identifies the acting application or machine
Requirement: Each auditable event of an asset interface shall contain information to determine which application or machine took the action, and the party responsible for the interface shall ensure that this information is sufficient to resolve a dispute about who acted.
Rationale: Derived; the specification lets the identity of the actual user be left to the application, so a wallet has to link the machine identifier to the owner for the act to count as the owner's (see EBW-NFR-033 for agents).
Sources: SRC-IDTA-AAS-P4 (Part 4 (IDTA-01004 v3.1), AAS Security requirements, FR2, Non-repudiation)
Source extract: Each auditable event shall contain information to determine which AAS user application took a particular action on the AAS.
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability
Review note: Dispute-resolution sentence ('sufficient to resolve a dispute about who acted') is not in the quote (source has a separate non-repudiation text); 'application or machine' generalises 'AAS user application'. Overlaps NFR-033 and AIF-012 (agent principal/agent logging); extends to machines.

Title: Support and incident reporting mechanism for owners
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall provide a mechanism enabling owners to easily request technical support and report technical problems or other incidents having a negative impact on the use of the wallets.
Rationale: Gives owners an operational channel for faults.
Source extract: easily request technical support and report technical problems or any other incidents
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Combines support and incident reporting; acceptable. 'Easily' is not testable.

Title: Owner notification and data transfer or deletion on service end
Requirement: On suspension, revocation or voluntary termination of its services, or removal from the list of notified providers, the provider of European Business Wallets shall notify owners and ensure the transfer or deletion of owner data according to the owner's instructions.
Rationale: Protects continuity and data control at exit.
Source extract: ensure the transfer or deletion of the European Business Wallet owner data in accordance with the European Business Wallet owners instructions
Clusters: K09 Privacy and data protection; K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Notification and data transfer/deletion are separate; trigger list beyond quote should be checked at Article 7(6)(f). Overlaps NFR-001, LEG-029.

Title: Risk management by non-qualified providers
Requirement: The non-qualified trust service provider shall have policies and measures to manage legal, business, operational and other risks, including registration and onboarding, procedural checks and service management.
Rationale: Extends baseline risk management to non-qualified services consumed by business wallets.
Source extract: have appropriate policies and take corresponding measures to manage legal, business, operational and other direct or indirect risks
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Identical to OPS-005 except provider type. Merge into one requirement for all trust service providers.

Title: 24-hour breach notification by non-qualified providers
Requirement: The non-qualified trust service provider shall notify the supervisory body and affected individuals of security breaches or disruptions with significant impact without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware.
Rationale: Fixes the incident notification clock for all trust service providers.
Actors: non-qualified trust service provider; supervisory body
Source extract: no later than 24 hours of having become aware of any security breaches or disruptions
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: 'And affected individuals' not in quote. Trigger 'becoming aware' differs from OPS-006 'of the incident'; also overlaps LEG-027, LEG-028.

Title: Risk management for qualified services
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall have policies and measures to manage legal, business, operational and other risks, including registration and onboarding, procedural checks and service management.
Rationale: Complements NIS2 risk management for qualified services.
Source extract: have appropriate policies and take corresponding measures to manage legal, business, operational and other direct or indirect risks
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Merge target for OPS-003. Not testable as phrased ('appropriate policies').

Title: 24-hour security breach notification
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall notify the supervisory body, identifiable affected individuals and other relevant bodies of security breaches or disruptions with significant impact within 24 hours of the incident.
Rationale: Sets the incident reporting deadline for qualified services.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; supervisory body
Source extract: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of the incident
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Recipients (affected individuals, other bodies) not in quote; inconsistent 24-hour trigger vs OPS-004. Consolidate with LEG-027 and OPS-004.

Title: Evidence records kept after cessation
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall record and keep accessible, for as long as necessary after its activities have ceased, all relevant information on data issued and received for evidence and continuity.
Rationale: Preserves legal evidence after provider exit.
Source extract: keep accessible for as long as necessary after the activities of the qualified trust service provider have ceased
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: 'As long as necessary' not testable; sets duration by national or contractual rule.

Title: Up-to-date termination plan
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall have an up-to-date termination plan to ensure continuity of service.
Rationale: Prevents loss of service and evidence when a provider stops.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; supervisory body
Source extract: have an up-to-date termination plan to ensure the continuity of service
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Supervisor-side counterpart is GOV-018.

Title: Notify wallet users within 24 hours of revocation
Requirement: When a wallet provider has revoked a wallet unit attestation, the wallet provider shall inform the affected wallet user within 24 hours, stating the reason and the consequences, in concise and plain language.
Rationale: Users must learn quickly that their wallet no longer works.
Source extract: they shall inform affected wallet users within 24 hours of the revocation of their wallet units, including the reason for the revocation
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Clause 'in concise and plain language' not in quote. EUDI scope; EBW equivalent needs decision.

Title: Notify holders within 24 hours of PID revocation
Requirement: When a provider of person identification data has revoked person identification data, it shall inform the wallet user through a dedicated and secure channel within 24 hours, stating the reasons.
Rationale: Holders must know when a credential stops being valid.
Source extract: inform wallet users subject of those person identification data within 24 hours of the revocation and of the reasons for the revocation.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K09 Privacy and data protection; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Applies to PID providers (employee wallets only). 'Dedicated and secure channel' not in quote.

Title: Inventory of cryptographic assets
Requirement: The wallet provider and each trust service provider shall create and maintain a current inventory of the assets that perform cryptographic operations and of the assets on which cryptographic operations are performed, in a standardised format.
Rationale: An inventory is the first no-regret step for migration, incident handling and service continuity.
Sources: SRC-NISCG-PQC-ROADMAP (Section 6.2, bullet "Support mature cryptographic asset management")
Source extract: create and maintain current inventories of assets that perform cryptographic operations and of assets that have cryptographic operations performed on them
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: "Standardised format" not in quote; roadmap addresses Member States, not providers.

Title: Quantum threat in top-level risk management
Requirement: The wallet provider and each trust service provider shall include the quantum threat to cryptography in its top-level risk management and classify each use of public-key cryptography as low, medium or high quantum risk.
Rationale: Risk classification drives the migration priorities and deadlines of the roadmap.
Sources: SRC-NISCG-PQC-ROADMAP (Section 6.2, bullet "Perform quantum risk analysis"; Section 5)
Source extract: include the quantum threat to cryptography in their top-level risk management
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Low/medium/high classification of each use is not in the quote; split off or cite source. Overlaps EBW-OPS-005 and EBW-LEG-023.

Title: Security controls for keys, algorithms and devices
Requirement: The trust service provider shall apply security controls to the management of all cryptographic keys, cryptographic algorithms and cryptographic devices throughout their lifecycle.
Rationale: Covers algorithms as well as keys, which anchors agility and rollover practices.
Source extract: Appropriate security controls shall be in place for the management of any cryptographic keys, cryptographic algorithms, and cryptographic devices throughout their lifecycle.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Near-duplicate of EBW-NFR-006 and EBW-LEG-026 on cryptography controls; keep only if standard anchor is wanted.

Title: Critical vulnerabilities addressed within 48 hours
Requirement: The trust service provider shall address any critical vulnerability within 48 hours of its discovery.
Rationale: Gives a numeric patch-time target for trust service systems.
Source extract: The TSP shall address any critical vulnerability not previously addressed by the TSP, within a period of 48 hours after its discovery.
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Overlaps EBW-LEG-039 (CRA, 24h early warning) only in topic. Add "not previously addressed" nuance.

Title: Records retained for the period stated in the terms and conditions
Requirement: The trust service provider shall hold records concerning its services for a period appropriate for providing legal evidence and as notified in its terms and conditions.
Rationale: Ties retention to a published, auditable period.
Source extract: Records concerning services shall be held for a period of time as appropriate for providing necessary legal evidence and as notified
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Overlaps EBW-OPS-007 (evidence records after cessation) and EBW-OPS-018.

Title: Restore operations within the continuity plan delay after a disaster
Requirement: After a disaster, including compromise of a private signing key, the trust service provider shall restore operations within the delay established in its continuity plan and remediate the cause.
Rationale: Makes recovery time a defined, testable target, including after key compromise.
Source extract: operations shall be restored within the delay established in the continuity plan
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Overlaps EBW-LEG-024 (continuity, backup, disaster recovery); statement adds remediate-the-cause not in quote.

Title: Destroy or withdraw private keys on termination
Requirement: Before the trust service provider terminates its services, it shall destroy or withdraw from use its private keys, including backup copies, so that they cannot be retrieved.
Rationale: Prevents misuse of keys of a ceased provider.
Source extract: the TSP's private keys, including backup copies, shall be destroyed, or withdrawn from use, in a manner such that the private keys cannot be retrieved
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Related to EBW-OPS-008 termination plan.

Title: Key lifecycle logs retained seven years
Requirement: The certification service provider shall retain the log of all events relating to the lifecycle of CA-managed keys and the certificate application documentation for at least seven years after any certificate based on these records ceases to be valid.
Rationale: Provides the main numeric retention period for evidence of key and certificate lifecycle.
Source extract: The TSP shall retain the following for at least seven years after any certificate based on these records ceases to be valid
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Quote truncated before the list of retained items; statement names key lifecycle log and application documentation.

Title: Documented key generation ceremony with signed report
Requirement: The certification service provider shall conduct CA key pair generation under a documented ceremony procedure and shall produce a signed report proving that the ceremony followed that procedure and protected the integrity and confidentiality of the key pair.
Rationale: Gives evidence of how each trust anchor key was created.
Source extract: The TSP shall produce a report proving that the ceremony
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Quote only covers the report; documented procedure and signature come from adjacent GEN requirements.

Title: Inform relying parties of CA key compromise
Requirement: On compromise, loss or suspected compromise of a CA private key, the certification service provider shall treat it as a disaster, inform all subscribers and relying parties, and indicate that certificates and status information issued with that key may no longer be valid.
Rationale: Defines the incident response when a trust anchor key is compromised.
Source extract: shall address the compromise, loss or suspected compromise of a CA's private key as a disaster
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K05 Trust framework and discovery; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Two obligations; quote supports only the first. Overlaps EBW-OPS-006 and EBW-OPS-016.

Title: Inform parties when an algorithm becomes insufficient
Requirement: When an algorithm or parameter used by the certification service provider or its subscribers becomes insufficient for its remaining intended usage, the provider shall inform all subscribers and relying parties with whom it has relations and publish that information for other relying parties.
Rationale: Gives a trigger and communication duty for algorithm migration.
Source extract: become insufficient for its remaining intended usage then the TSP shall inform all subscribers and relying parties
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Pairs with EBW-TRU-076; consider merging into one algorithm-insufficiency requirement.

Title: Certification records retained at least five years after expiry
Requirement: The holder of a wallet solution certificate of conformity shall store the information provided during certification, and specimens of the certified hardware components, securely for at least five years after cancellation or expiry of the certificate.
Rationale: Defines the retention period for certification evidence.
Source extract: for at least five years after the cancellation or expiry of the relevant certificate of conformity
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Statement is compound (information and specimens) but one retention rule; acceptable.

Title: Final incident report within one month
Requirement: The trust service provider shall submit to the CSIRT or competent authority a final incident report not later than one month after submission of the incident notification.
Rationale: Complements the 24-hour notification with the later reporting steps. Derived: Article 23(4) replaces the 72-hour step for trust service providers with 24 hours, so the one-month period is counted from that notification.
Source extract: a final report not later than one month after the submission of the incident notification
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Check that the quote supports applicability to trust service providers; complements EBW-LEG-027.

Title: Update cryptographic technology on cryptanalysis developments
Requirement: Where the wallet provider serves a financial entity, it shall provide for updating or changing cryptographic technology on the basis of developments in cryptanalysis, and shall adopt mitigation and monitoring measures where it cannot update.
Rationale: Names cryptanalysis developments, including quantum advances, as the trigger for algorithm change. Derived: the obligation lies on financial entities and reaches providers through their ICT risk management.
Source extract: provisions for updating or changing, where necessary, the cryptographic technology on the basis of developments in cryptanalysis
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Derived via financial entity ICT risk; mitigation clause not in quote. Applicability limited to financial customers.

Title: Renew certificates in advance of expiry
Requirement: Where the wallet provider serves a financial entity, it shall renew certificates promptly in advance of their expiration and keep a register of certificates and certificate-storing devices.
Rationale: Prevents outages caused by expired certificates and supports trust-anchor and certificate rollover. Derived: the obligation lies on financial entities and reaches providers through their ICT risk management.
Source extract: Financial entities shall ensure the prompt renewal of certificates in advance of their expiration.
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Two obligations; register not in quote (Article 7(5)). Quote supports only renewal.

Title: Notify users within 24 hours of unit revocation
Requirement: When the provider of European Business Wallets revokes a wallet unit attestation, it shall inform the affected wallet users without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after the revocation, stating the reason and the consequences, in concise and plain language.
Rationale: Gives users prompt, understandable notice; counterpart of EBW-OPS-009 in the business wallet annex.
Source extract: no later than 24 hours from the revocation of their European Business Wallets units
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Kept as proposal counterpart of in-force OPS-009.

Title: Delivery channel availability, redundancy and fallback
Requirement: The Commission shall, by implementing act, establish procedures ensuring continuous availability, redundancy and fallback mechanisms for the qualified electronic registered delivery service in case of service failure.
Rationale: A single mandatory channel is a single point of failure.
Source extract: continuous availability, redundancy and fallback mechanisms in case of service failure
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Binds the Commission, not the wallet; restate as design requirement on the delivery channel if wanted.

Title: Remote signing key destroyed when its certificate is revoked
Requirement: The provider of a remote signature creation service shall destroy the signing key when the corresponding public key certificate is revoked.
Rationale: It ends the life of a hosted key together with its certificate and keeps revoked keys from being used.
Source extract: If the public key certificate is revoked, the corresponding signing key shall be destroyed.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K07 Credential lifecycle

Title: Remote signing key destroyed on the signer request
Requirement: The provider of a remote signature creation service shall destroy a signing key when the signer requests it.
Rationale: It gives the signer an exit and a way to end a key held at a provider.
Source extract: The SSASP shall destroy a signing key when requested by the signer.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)

Title: Maintain instance revocation status until the stated time
Requirement: Where a wallet provider signs or seals a wallet instance attestation, it shall maintain the revocation status of the relevant wallet instance until the status expiry indicated in that attestation has passed.
Rationale: Issuers can only chain the validity of a credential to a wallet if the provider commits to serving status for a stated time.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib), point 2(d), LC_WIA_3)
Source extract: it shall maintain the revocation status of the relevant wallet instance until the 'wallet_instance_status.exp' indicated in that wallet instance attestation has passed
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Parallel to OPS-031; atomic separately.

Title: Maintain key storage revocation status until the stated time
Requirement: Where a wallet provider signs or seals a key attestation, it shall maintain the revocation status of the relevant wallet secure cryptographic device or keystore until the status expiry indicated in that attestation has passed.
Rationale: It is the key-side counterpart of the commitment on instance status.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib), point 2(d), LC_KA-3)
Source extract: it shall maintain the revocation status of the relevant WSCD or keystore until the 'key_storage_status.exp' indicated in that key attestation has passed
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: Attestations show a status period of at least 31 days
Requirement: The wallet provider shall ensure that a wallet unit can always present wallet instance attestations and key attestations whose status expiry lies at least 31 days in the future at the time of presentation.
Rationale: It lets issuers set credential validity without being forced to short lives.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib), point 2(d), LC_GEN-1)
Source extract: at least 31 days in the future at the time of presentation
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Wallet provider keeps the unit-to-attestation association
Requirement: The wallet provider shall maintain, for each wallet unit it has activated, the set of instance attestations and key attestations it issued to that unit, so that the association cannot be confused with that of another unit, and shall document the procedures, controls and risk analysis in the policy on unit revocation.
Rationale: Revoking one unit needs a reliable record of which status entries belong to it.
Source extract: SHALL maintain, for each Wallet Unit it has activated, the set of WIAs and KAs it has issued to that Wallet Unit
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K07 Credential lifecycle; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Policy documentation clause is not in quote.

Title: Wallet provider regularly verifies unit security
Requirement: During the lifetime of a wallet unit, the wallet provider shall regularly verify that the security of the unit is not breached or compromised, and shall revoke the unit where a breach affects its trustworthiness or reliability.
Rationale: Compromised units are only revoked if someone looks for compromise.
Source extract: SHALL regularly verify that the security of the Wallet Unit is not breached or compromised
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Revocation clause is not in quote; "regularly" untestable, define interval.

Title: Tell the user of unit revocation outside the unit
Requirement: The wallet provider shall inform a user about the revocation of the user wallet unit through a communication channel that is independent of the wallet unit.
Rationale: A revoked unit cannot be relied on to deliver the notice.
Source extract: SHALL use a communication channel that is independent of the Wallet Unit
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Channel independence testable; see OPS-009 and FUN-053.

Title: Revoked PID kept as long as law requires
Requirement: The provider of person identification data shall keep revoked person identification data accessible for as long as required by Union law or national law.
Rationale: It preserves evidence of what was issued and revoked.
Source extract: The revoked person identification data shall remain accessible for as long as required by Union law or national law.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: EUDI PID only.

Title: Revoke a credential when its attribute values change
Requirement: The provider of a revocable PID or attestation shall revoke it if the value of one or more attributes of the corresponding logical credential changed, and the technical credential is still valid for at least 24 hours.
Rationale: A credential must not keep stating values that are no longer true.
Source extract: if the value of one or more of the attributes in the corresponding logical PID or attestation was changed
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Check against TRU-040 and TRU-134 for overlap.

Title: Trusted list availability of 99,9 percent
Requirement: The scheme operator of a trusted list shall make the list available 24 hours a day and 7 days a week with an availability of at least 99,9 % over one year.
Rationale: A relying party can only validate a trust service output if the list is reachable, so the standard fixes a minimum availability.
Source extract: TLSOs shall make their TLs available 24 hours a day and 7 days a week
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: The 99,9 % over one year figure is not in the quote; verify clause 6.4.

Title: Delivery providers archive the evidence they issue
Requirement: The provider of an electronic registered delivery service shall archive the evidence or the evidence digests for each evidence it issued.
Rationale: Evidence of sending and receipt is the product of the service, so it has to remain available to prove events later.
Source extract: The ERDSP shall archive the evidence and/or evidence digests for each evidence that it issued.
Clusters: K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K10 Evidence, logging and audit

Title: Termination plan keeps records accessible and usable
Requirement: A qualified trust service provider shall ensure that its termination plan specifies procedures that keep all relevant records it holds accessible and usable after termination.
Rationale: Outputs of a terminated service must stay verifiable, which needs the records behind them.
Source extract: ensuring the accessibility and usability of all relevant records held by the qualified trust service provider
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K10 Evidence, logging and audit
Review note: Refines OPS-008 and OPS-007; fold in as plan content.

Title: Issuers automate mandate revocation and sync with authentic sources
Requirement: The issuer of a power of attorney or power of representation attestation shall automate revocation and synchronise mandate changes with authentic sources.
Rationale: Manual revocation after a register or HR change leaves a window in which a former representative still holds valid authority.
Source extract: Issuers MUST automate revocation and synchronize mandate changes with authentic sources.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Complements TRU-162 to TRU-164.

Title: Provider states before onboarding what happens to keys on exit
Requirement: The wallet provider shall state to the owner before onboarding whether the private keys of a wallet unit can be exported or must be re-created when the owner changes provider, and which attestations and certificates must then be re-issued.
Rationale: Derived (criterion C6 of the DEC-03 page): the texts require export of data but none says whether keys move; the ARF excludes key export, so exit needs new keys and re-issued attestations.
Source extract: support the secure export and portability of an owner's European Business Wallet data in at least an open format
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote reaches data export only. "The ARF excludes key export" is an EUDI rule and does not bind the EBW; the statement is neutral and fine. Related NFR-118.

Title: Recovery after loss of the key-holding device or module
Requirement: The wallet provider shall document, for each custody model it offers, how the owner regains the ability to use a wallet unit after loss of the device or module that holds its keys, and which backup copies of keys exist.
Rationale: Derived (criterion C5 of the DEC-03 page): keys are not exportable and backup of remote qualified keys is limited to the minimum, so recovery has to be designed per custody model; the sources are silent.
Source extract: the number of duplicated datasets must not exceed the minimum needed to ensure continuity of the service
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Derivation stated (C5). Quote is about duplicated datasets only.

Title: Account lifecycle distinguishes temporary deactivation from termination
Requirement: Where the wallet owner is a financial entity, its identity management shall include a lifecycle process for identities and accounts that covers creation, change, review, temporary deactivation and termination of all accounts.
Rationale: Derived; the duty lies on financial entities. Temporary deactivation and termination are separate steps in the source, which supports modelling suspension of an authorisation apart from its revocation.
Source extract: a lifecycle management process for identities and accounts managing the creation, change, review and update, temporary deactivation, and termination of all accounts
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Financial entities only; derived. Source also lists 'update' in the lifecycle, omitted in the statement without loss.

Title: Withdraw access rights when employment ends or access is no longer necessary
Requirement: Where the wallet owner is a financial entity, its account management procedures shall provide for the withdrawal of access rights without undue delay upon termination of the employment or when the access is no longer necessary.
Rationale: Derived; closes the gap that only the leaving-employee mandate attestation (EBW-TRU-163) was sourced. The clause covers user and generic accounts, so a decommissioned service or machine account falls under "no longer necessary" by derivation.
Source extract: withdrawal of access rights without undue delay upon termination of the employment or when the access is no longer necessary
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Complements TRU-163 (issuer revokes mandate attestation on leaving); extension to machine accounts is a derivation, marked in rationale.

Title: Periodic update of access rights
Requirement: Where the wallet owner is a financial entity, its account management procedures shall provide for the update of access rights where changes are necessary and at least every 6 months for ICT systems supporting critical or important functions, and at least once a year for other ICT systems.
Rationale: Derived; gives a source-backed review interval for user authorisations, which EBW-FUN-015 and the owner-side review gap in the J1 research did not have.
Source extract: and at least every 6 months for ICT systems supporting critical or important functions
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Quote truncated before the 'once a year for other ICT systems' limb; statement follows RTS Art 21(1)(e)(iv). Related to FUN-015 only loosely; no merge.

Title: Keep roles and accounts aligned between the identity service and the asset interface
Requirement: Where a detached service authenticates users or applications and assigns their roles, the party responsible for the asset interface shall ensure that the account information, including roles, is aligned between that service and the interface.
Rationale: Derived; a revoked or suspended role in the identity service must not stay valid in the asset interface, which is a precondition for timely termination of machine and employee authority.
Sources: SRC-IDTA-AAS-P4 (Part 4 (IDTA-01004 v3.1), AAS Security requirements, FR1, Account management)
Source extract: the AAS responsible SHALL ensure that the account information is aligned between the AAS and the detached service
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Derived from IDTA Part 4 FR1; conditional 'where a detached service' matches the quote. Ecosystem specification (industrial AAS).
