Title: Transitional alternative to delivery service until 36 months
Requirement: Until 36 months after entry into force, a public sector body that does not offer the qualified electronic registered delivery service shall ensure its alternative solutions comply with Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 qualified delivery requirements and offer a gateway to the wallet qualified delivery service.
Rationale: Transitional derogation: the alternative is optional (may choose not to offer) and conditional on two provisos.
Source extract: public sector bodies may choose not to offer the qualified electronic registered delivery service
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K12 Registered delivery and notifications; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Quote says 'may choose not to offer'; 'shall support' and gateway duty not supported by quote.

Title: No stand-alone quantum-vulnerable mechanisms after 2030
Requirement: After 31 December 2030 the wallet provider shall not use quantum-vulnerable public-key mechanisms stand-alone for high-risk use cases and shall complete their transition to post-quantum or hybrid mechanisms by then.
Rationale: High-risk uses include long-term confidentiality and long-lived signing infrastructure, which the roadmap sets as the first deadline. Derived: the roadmap addresses Member States and is not binding on providers.
Sources: SRC-NISCG-PQC-ROADMAP (Section 4.1, Overview (paragraph on hybrid solutions) and Timeline, milestone 2)
Source extract: For high-risk use cases, quantum-vulnerable public-key mechanisms shall not be used stand-alone after the end of 2030
Clusters: K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: "Complete transition by then" is redundant; high-risk use cases undefined for wallets; roadmap is not binding on providers.

Title: Quantum-safe upgrade path with post-quantum signed updates
Requirement: The wallet provider shall ensure that wallet software that is expected to remain in use beyond 2030 can be upgraded to post-quantum cryptography and that its update mechanism incorporates post-quantum signature schemes for integrity and authenticity.
Rationale: Authentic updates are the channel through which later algorithm migration reaches deployed wallets.
Source extract: products entering the market with an expected lifetime beyond 2030 should be upgradable to PQC
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Quote says "should"; PQ-signed update mechanism is not in quote. Make that a separate derived requirement.

Title: Plan for post-quantum signature creation devices
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall plan for the availability of certified qualified signature and seal creation devices that support post-quantum algorithms so that its own systems, its customers and conformity assessment can migrate.
Rationale: Qualified services depend on certified devices, which must exist before providers can migrate.
Source extract: certified qualified electronic signature creation devices including PQC must be available to allow for integration in the systems of trust service providers
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: Roadmap quote is about availability, not a provider duty; "customers and conformity assessment" is not in quote.

Title: Qualified status before service start
Requirement: When a provider intends to offer a qualified trust service, the provider shall not begin the service until the qualified status is indicated in the applicable trusted list.
Rationale: Derived: Article 21(3) permits a provider to begin only after the status is indicated in the trusted lists; the prohibition before that point is the implied converse.
Source extract: may begin to provide the qualified trust service after the qualified status has been indicated in the trusted lists
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability; K05 Trust framework and discovery

Title: Trusted lists signed and machine-readable
Requirement: Member States shall establish, maintain and publish electronically signed or sealed trusted lists in a secured manner and in a form suitable for automated processing.
Rationale: Lets relying parties verify the origin of the list and process it without manual steps.
Source extract: Member States shall establish, maintain and publish, in a secured manner, the electronically signed or sealed trusted lists
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Several near-identical signed machine-readable publication duties (TRU-014,017,027,036,037).

Title: Status of a listed service at a given time
Requirement: A trusted list shall allow a relying party to determine the status of a listed trust service at a given time.
Rationale: A relying party must be able to judge a past signature or seal against the status at the time it was made.
Source extract: so that interested parties may determine the status of a listed trust service at a given time
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Derived from standard scope; "shall" adopted from descriptive text.

Title: Irreversible revocation of qualified attestations
Requirement: When a qualified electronic attestation of attributes is revoked, it shall lose its validity and its status shall not be reverted.
Rationale: Gives relying parties a stable rule: revocation of a qualified attestation is final.
Source extract: it shall lose its validity from the moment of its revocation and its status shall not in any circumstances be reverted
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Absorb TRU-025, TRU-026 and TRU-028 as additional sources.

Title: Trust anchors and status checks by relying parties
Requirement: A relying party instance shall verify the signature over a presented PID, QEAA or PuB-EAA using a trust anchor of the provider obtained from a Trusted List or LoTE.
Rationale: Trust anchors are only useful if they are used both for the credential and for its status.
Source extract: the Relying Party Instance uses a trust anchor of the Provider obtained from a LoTE or Trusted List
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Merges two actions; no quote.

Title: Invalid wallet provider status
Requirement: When the status of a wallet provider in the Wallet Provider LoTE is Invalid, PID providers and attestation providers shall refuse to issue PIDs and attestations to wallet units of that wallet provider.
Rationale: Derived: ARF 6.2.3 describes (not mandates) that after the Wallet Provider status is set to Invalid in its LoTE, providers refuse issuance; the shall form turns this expected behaviour into a requirement.
Source extract: They will therefore refuse to issue PIDs and attestations to any Wallet Unit provided by that Wallet Provider.
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture

Title: List of notified business wallet providers
Requirement: The Commission shall publish a machine-readable list of notified European Business Wallet providers that shows whether each provider is a qualified trust service provider.
Rationale: Derived: 12(3) requires a machine-readable list on the basis of the 12(2) information, which includes in point (e) the qualified-TSP indication; that the list shows the indication follows from the 'on the basis of' link.
Source extract: the Commission shall establish and maintain on the Commission’s website, in a machine-readable format, a list of providers of European Business Wallets
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Qualified-flag in the list not shown by quote.

Title: Remote onboarding via authorised representative
Requirement: Providers of European Business Wallets shall ensure that their wallets support common protocols and interfaces to securely onboard the owner remotely via an authorised representative with that representative's electronic identification means of assurance level substantial or high.
Rationale: Clause obliges providers to support protocols and interfaces for remote onboarding; the eID means is that of the authorised representative, meeting Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as regards levels substantial or high.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; authorised representative
Source extract: securely onboard the European Business Wallet owner remotely via an authorised representative
Clusters: K02 Wallet subject model; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Assurance level not in quote. Recategorise FUN is possible.

Title: Authentication of relying parties
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall support common protocols and interfaces for authenticating relying parties by implementing authentication mechanisms, where authentication is required.
Rationale: Lets the owner know to whom data is disclosed.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; relying party
Source extract: for authenticating European Business Wallet-relying parties by implementing authentication mechanisms, where authentication is required
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Conditional "where required" weakens testability.

Title: Relying party verification of wallet authenticity
Requirement: The European Business Wallet shall support interfaces for relying parties to verify the authenticity and validity of the wallet, where such verification is required.
Rationale: Relying parties must be able to trust the wallet instance.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; relying party
Source extract: for European Business Wallet-relying parties to verify the authenticity and validity of European Business Wallets
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: Wallet unit attestation with protected keys
Requirement: Providers of European Business Wallets shall ensure that their wallets support common protocols and interfaces for the provision of wallet unit attestations to all wallet units, containing public keys and corresponding private keys protected by a wallet secure cryptographic device.
Rationale: Clause requires support for protocols and interfaces for provision of attestations, not direct provision.
Source extract: provision of wallet unit attestations to all European Business Wallet units
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Key-protection clause unsupported by quote; place in own requirement.

Title: Verifiable and revocable role-attribute mappings
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall ensure that mappings between roles and attributes are verifiable, auditable, revocable and traceable to their legitimate issuers.
Rationale: Keeps delegated authority accountable.
Source extract: mappings between roles and attributes are verifiable, auditable, revocable and traceable to their legitimate issuers
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K18 Planes and evidence graph (control, data, verifiable evidence)
Review note: Four properties in one sentence: split verifiable, revocable, traceable if kept.

Title: Revocation of wallet validity
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall ensure that the validity of a wallet can be revoked on explicit owner request, on compromise, on cessation of owner activity, and where the provider is not on the list of notified providers.
Rationale: Defines mandatory revocation triggers.
Source extract: ensure that the validity of the European Business Wallets can be revoked in the following circumstances
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Overlaps FUN-029; wallet lifecycle rather than trust.

Title: Signed publication of validation mechanisms
Requirement: The Commission shall make the notified validation mechanism information available to the public through a secure channel, in electronically signed or sealed form suitable for automated processing.
Rationale: Authentic, machine-readable discovery of validation endpoints.
Source extract: in electronically signed or sealed form suitable for automated processing
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Same pattern as TRU-017.

Title: One set of identification data for third-country operators
Requirement: A provider of owner identification data shall issue identification data and a unique identifier to an economic operator established outside the Union only if identity proofing meets Article 24(1a) of Regulation (EU) 910/2014 and the operator has not been issued another set.
Rationale: Prevents duplicate identities for non-EU operators.
Source extract: has not been issued another set of European Business Wallet owner identification data
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Overlaps INT-007; statement is dense and conditional.

Title: Remedy or loss of qualified status
Requirement: Where the qualified trust service provider fails to remedy a failure to fulfil requirements within the set time limit, the supervisory body shall withdraw the qualified status of the provider or affected service.
Rationale: Defines when qualified status is lost, which relying parties must reflect in trust decisions.
Actors: supervisory body; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: shall withdraw the qualified status of that provider or of the affected service it provides
Clusters: K13 Governance, supervision and liability

Title: Commission publishes trusted list locations securely
Requirement: The Commission shall make the notified trusted list information available to the public through a secure channel in electronically signed or sealed form suitable for automated processing.
Rationale: Provides the machine-readable root for discovering all national trusted lists.
Source extract: in electronically signed or sealed form suitable for automated processing
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery

Title: Trusted list link when using the EU trust mark
Requirement: When using the EU trust mark, the qualified trust service provider shall ensure that a link to the relevant trusted list is made available on its website.
Rationale: Lets users verify qualified status behind the mark.
Source extract: shall ensure that a link to the relevant trusted list is made available on their website
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K13 Governance, supervision and liability

Title: Identity and attribute verification before issuance
Requirement: When issuing a qualified certificate or qualified electronic attestation of attributes, the qualified trust service provider shall verify the identity and, if applicable, specific attributes of the natural or legal person.
Rationale: Sets the vetting baseline for legal person identity in seals and attestations.
Actors: qualified trust service provider; legal person
Source extract: shall verify the identity and, if applicable, any specific attributes of the natural or legal person
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K07 Credential lifecycle; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)

Title: Permitted identity verification methods
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall verify identity using the European Digital Identity Wallet or a notified high-assurance means, a qualified signature or seal certificate, a conformity-assessed method of high confidence, or physical presence.
Rationale: Defines the permissible onboarding paths, including wallets as identity source.

Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote supports first method only; enumeration of methods is a long list.

Title: Permitted attribute verification methods
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall verify attributes by wallet or high-assurance means, qualified signature or seal certificate, qualified electronic attestation of attributes, a conformity-assessed method, or physical presence.
Rationale: Allows attestations to be chained from other qualified attestations and authentic sources.

Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K07 Credential lifecycle; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)

Title: Revocation published within 24 hours
Requirement: When revoking a qualified certificate, the qualified trust service provider shall register the revocation and publish the revocation status within 24 hours of receiving the request, with immediate effect on publication.

Title: Free automated validity status information
Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall provide relying parties with validity or revocation status per certificate at any time, also beyond validity, in an automated, reliable, free and efficient manner.

Actors: qualified trust service provider; relying party

Requirement: The qualified trust service provider shall apply the revocation registration, 24-hour publication and status-information rules to qualified electronic attestations of attributes.

Title: Irreversible revocation of qualified certificates
Requirement: A qualified certificate for electronic signatures shall lose its validity from the moment of revocation and its status shall not in any circumstances be reverted.

Requirement: A status element used for person identification data, qualified electronic attestations of attributes or attestations issued by or on behalf of a public sector body responsible for an authentic source shall indicate only whether the attestation is revoked or not revoked and shall not support any other status value, such as suspension.
Rationale: It rules out suspension for these credential types.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex IV (new Annex II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979), clause 4.2.11.1, EAA-4.2.11.1-06)
Actors: PID provider; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: it shall only indicate whether the attestation is revoked or not revoked and shall not support any other status values, such as suspension
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Format of status element; statement on credential not trust service. Business wallet bearing open.

Title: Short-lived attestations need no revocation
Requirement: Revocation of a short-lived electronic attestation of attributes with a validity period of 24 hours or less shall not be required.
Rationale: It allows an alternative to status checking and defines the threshold.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex IV (new Annex II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979), clause 4.2.13, EAA-4.2.13-03)
Actors: PID provider; qualified trust service provider
Source extract: Where short-lived electronic attestations of attributes with a validity period of 24 hours or less are issued, revocation shall not be required.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Not a "shall" duty; it is an exemption.

Title: Risk analysis where status information is unavailable
Requirement: A relying party shall perform a risk analysis considering all relevant factors for the use case to determine whether it accepts or refuses a PID or attestation when no reliable information on its revocation status is available.
Rationale: Offline use, expired caches and non-revocable credentials need an explicit decision rule.
Source extract: to determine whether it will accept or refuse a PID or attestation in case no reliable information regarding the revocation status
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Close to TRU-047 and TRU-135; check overlap.

Title: PID revoked when the wallet unit attestation is revoked
Requirement: A provider of person identification data shall revoke person identification data issued to a wallet unit where the wallet unit attestation of that unit has been revoked.
Rationale: It carries the revocation of the wallet down to the credentials bound to it.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Article 1(3), replacing Article 5(4)(b) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2977)
Source extract: where the wallet unit attestation of the wallet unit to which the person identification data was issued to has been revoked
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Close to FUN/TRU-040 revocation circumstances; PID only.

Title: PID revoked on the request of the wallet user
Requirement: A provider of person identification data shall revoke person identification data upon the explicit request of the wallet user to whose wallet unit the data was issued.
Rationale: It gives the user a way to end a credential, in addition to revoking the wallet.
Source extract: upon the explicit request of the wallet user to whose wallet unit
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: PID only; business wallet equivalent open.

Title: PID revocation cannot be reverted
Requirement: A provider of person identification data shall ensure that revocations of person identification data cannot be reverted.
Rationale: Irreversibility prevents a revoked credential from becoming valid again.
Source extract: shall ensure that revocations cannot be reverted
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Same rule as TRU-004/025/026/028 for PID; consider one generic requirement.

Title: Suspension of a qualified certificate is visible in status
Requirement: Where national rules provide for temporary suspension of a qualified certificate, the period of suspension shall be indicated in the certificate database and the suspension status shall be visible during the suspension from the service that gives status information.
Rationale: Relying parties must be able to see a suspension while it lasts.
Source extract: the suspension status shall be visible, during the period of suspension, from the service providing information on the status of the certificate
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Two obligations: record period, expose status.

Title: A suspended qualified certificate loses validity
Requirement: A qualified certificate that has been temporarily suspended under national rules shall lose its validity for the period of suspension.
Rationale: It states the legal effect of suspension, which differs from revocation.
Source extract: that certificate shall lose its validity for the period of suspension
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Legal effect, not a design duty.

Title: Support revocation for owner identification data valid over 24 hours
Requirement: The provider of owner identification data shall support revocation of owner identification data that has a validity longer than 24 hours.
Rationale: The rulebook of the pilot treats owner identification data as long-lived but revocable.
Source extract: Validity longer than 24 hours is permitted; therefore, revocation MUST be supported.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Derived "shall" from a permission; ecosystem rulebook, not law.

Title: Indeterminate status of owner identification data is not valid
Requirement: A relying party that checks the status of owner identification data shall treat an indeterminate status as not valid, in line with its risk policy.
Rationale: It sets the default when status cannot be determined.
Source extract: Treat any indeterminate status as non-valid per risk policy.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Overlaps TRU-047 and TRU-128; "indeterminate" undefined.

Title: A valid unit attestation is required to operate
Requirement: A European Business Wallet unit shall hold a valid wallet unit attestation in order to operate within the business wallet ecosystem.
Rationale: It ties the operation of a unit to the attestation, so that revoking the attestation stops the unit.
Source extract: A valid WUA is required for a Wallet Unit to operate within the EBW ecosystem.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K07 Credential lifecycle; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability
Review note: ADR status Proposed.

Title: A unit cannot be valid without a valid unit attestation
Requirement: A European Business Wallet unit shall not be in the state valid unless it holds both a valid wallet unit attestation and valid owner identification data.
Rationale: The consortium separates structural trust of the unit from identity trust of the owner.
Source extract: A Wallet Unit cannot be VALID without a valid WUA.
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K07 Credential lifecycle; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Depends on TRU-136; ADR status Proposed.

Title: Distribution point in trust tokens resolves to the latest list
Requirement: Where a trust service provider gives a distribution point for its trusted list in a trust service token, it shall ensure that the distribution point always resolves to the latest applicable trusted list or to a scheme list that points to it.
Rationale: Lets a relying party find the applicable list from the token itself, which is the only discovery path that starts from the artefact being validated.
Sources: SRC-ETSI-119612 (Clause 6.3 (TL Distribution Points in trust service tokens))
Source extract: always resolved to the latest available applicable TL or to a scheme including a pointer to it
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K08 Protocols and interfaces

Title: Authenticate a pointed-to list before using it
Requirement: A relying party shall authenticate a trusted list or list of trusted entities that another list points to, using one of the digital identities given in the pointer, before it uses the pointed-to list.
Rationale: Pointers are the discovery mechanism between lists; trusting a list without authenticating it with the key in the pointer would make the pointer an attack path.
Source extract: One of such digital identities shall allow successful authentication of the pointed-to list before its use.
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling

Title: Trust evaluation of a delivery service from a trusted list
Requirement: A party that evaluates trust in an electronic registered delivery service from a trusted list shall validate the service signature, link the signing certificate to the service digital identity in the list, verify that the current status is granted, and verify that the service type fits the applicable trust domain.
Rationale: Defines how a provider decides whether to relay a message to another provider, which is the discovery and trust step of the registered delivery channel.
Source extract: verify that the signing certificate can be linked to the service digital identity in the TL
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K12 Registered delivery and notifications
Review note: Four separate checks bundled.

Title: Rulebook states how to obtain the trust anchor
Requirement: The scheme provider of a rulebook for a non-qualified attestation shall specify how a relying party obtains the trust anchor needed to verify the attestation signature.
Rationale: Non-qualified attestation providers are not on a Commission list, so without a rulebook mechanism a relying party cannot find the anchor.
Sources: SRC-ARF-TRUST (Section 6.3.2.4 (trust anchors conditionally included in a Trusted List or LoTE))
Source extract: it must know how to obtain the trust anchor it needs to verify the signature over that EAA
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Provenance D; rationale states derivation.

Title: Verifier can recognise several governance authorities
Requirement: A verifier in a data space shall be able to recognise the trust anchors of more than one data space governance authority.
Rationale: Organisations that belong to several data spaces need one verification path that can honour each space own list of trusted issuers.
Source extract: Verifiers can recognize several Dataspace Governance Authorities.
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Ecosystem source; "shall be able" testable by configuration.

Title: Signed issuer metadata with the access certificate
Requirement: A provider of person identification data or electronic attestations of attributes shall publish its issuer metadata as signed metadata, signed with its access certificate.
Rationale: Lets the wallet tie the issuer endpoint and the supported credentials to a registered, authenticated provider before it requests issuance. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Source extract: The signing certificate of the signature on the Issuer Metadata shall be the access certificate of the PID/EAA Provider.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K05 Trust framework and discovery; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: EUDI profile; business wallet bearing open (DEC-07).

Title: Pre-authorised issuance only with physical presence
Requirement: A provider of person identification data that uses the pre-authorised code issuance flow shall perform user authorisation with the physical presence of the user.
Rationale: The pre-authorised flow does not protect against hijacking in remote scenarios, so remote issuance at assurance level high is excluded from it. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Source extract: PID Providers implementing the Pre-Authorised Code Flow shall perform user authorisation with the physical presence.
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K14 Conformity, certification and assurance
Review note: EUDI profile; business wallet bearing open (DEC-07).

Title: Access certificate validation stays in the wallet
Requirement: The wallet unit shall authenticate and validate wallet-relying party access certificates itself and shall not delegate this to an operating system browser or other intermediary application.
Rationale: Prevents the trust decision from moving to a platform component that the wallet provider does not control. This is an EUDI Wallet profile; its use in the business wallet is part of DEC-07.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Article 4, point (2)(a) (amending Article 3(1) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2982))
Source extract: without delegating execution of these processes to an operating system browser or other intermediary application
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Extends TRU-032 with no-delegation; could be merged. Business wallet bearing open.

Title: Preservation evidence carries qualified time stamps
Requirement: A qualified preservation service shall use qualified time stamps within the preservation evidence.
Rationale: Qualified time stamps give the presumption of accuracy of time and integrity that long-term proof of existence needs.
Source extract: Time-stamps used within the preservation evidence shall be qualified time-stamps
Clusters: K10 Evidence, logging and audit; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling
Review note: Preservation service evidence, not trust anchor; plane assurance already.

Title: CSP-B performs identity proofing of the participant
Requirement: The core service provider-B shall verify the identity of the prospective participant through an identity proofing process.
Rationale: The assurance level depends on the referenced identity proofing standard, which is a placeholder (CX-XXXX) in the page read.
Source extract: The CSP-B MUST verify the identity of the prospective participant through an identity proofing process
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Gap: no level of assurance stated; cannot be mapped to eIDAS LoA. Not verifiable as written. Cross-reference EBW-TRU-084 (LoA high legal person registration), TRU-015, TRU-114.

Title: Every participant has a compliant wallet
Requirement: Every participant shall have access to a wallet instance complying with the Catena-X wallet requirements after onboarding.
Rationale: The wallet holds the participant credentials and identifier.
Source extract: every participant MUST have access to a wallet instance complying with CX-0149 Wallet Requirements
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Overlaps TRU-151 (any wallet in the data space compliant). See TRU-151.

Title: CSP-B issues membership, BPN and framework credentials
Requirement: The core service provider-B shall issue to the prospective participant a Membership Credential, a BPN Credential and a Framework Agreement Credential, provided that the conditions for the credential claims are met.
Rationale: Onboarding ends with credentials issued by the ecosystem authority, the single trust anchor of the ecosystem.
Source extract: The CSP-B MUST issue to the prospective participant a Membership Credential, a BPN Credential, and a Framework Agreement Credential
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K05 Trust framework and discovery; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Related: DAT-003. Single issuer model conflicts with multi-issuer EBW trust list approach.

Title: CSP triggers the clearing house trust anchor
Requirement: The core service provider shall be able to trigger the clearing house trust anchor for a registration application.
Rationale: External clearing house acts as an additional trust anchor for the legal entity data.
Source extract: The Core Service Provider MUST be able to trigger the CH trust anchor.
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: CX-Neptune preview, not certifiable. CX-0009 fast-track; not certifiable. Statement is an interface capability, not a trust requirement.

Title: Wallets in the data space are compliant
Requirement: Any wallet used in the Catena-X data space shall be a Catena-X-compliant wallet.
Rationale: Single wallet profile for all participants, no alternative wallet types.
Source extract: Any wallet used in the Catena-X dataspace MUST be a Catena-X-compliant wallet.
Clusters: K15 Adoption, acceptance and cross-ecosystem interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Same obligation as TRU-148 (wallet compliant with CX-0149) from different section; merge or cross-reference.

Title: Membership Credential issued by CSP or assigned issuer
Requirement: The core service provider, or an issuer assigned by it, shall issue the Membership Credential to the participant.
Rationale: Issuer delegation by the core service provider is the trust-anchor model of the ecosystem.
Source extract: It is issued to the participant by the CSP or a core service provider assigned issuer.
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K07 Credential lifecycle; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Source sentence states fact in a normative section; the 'shall' is a derivation per the research note. Mark as derived in fidelity pass.

Title: BPN-DID resolution checks the Membership Credential
Requirement: The BPN-DID resolution service shall check the validity of the provided Membership Credential, including type, expiry, revocation and a signature by a trusted issuer, and deny access if the check fails.
Rationale: Access to the identifier directory depends on a trusted-issuer check; who is trusted is not specified.
Source extract: MUST check the validity of the provided Membership Credential, e.g., correct type, not expired, not revoked, properly signed by a trusted issuer
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K07 Credential lifecycle; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote lists checks as examples ('e.g.'); statement makes them exhaustive. Also: trusted issuer undefined, no cross-jurisdiction trust list. Cross-reference EBW trust-list requirements.

Title: Catalogue request token scope covers membership, BPN and framework credentials
Requirement: The token for requesting a catalogue shall include a scope covering the Membership Credential, the BPN Credential and the Framework Agreement Credential.
Rationale: Counterparties are identified by ecosystem credentials before any data offer is shown.
Source extract: The scope of the token for requesting a Catalog MUST include the following credentials as defined in CX-0050
Clusters: K08 Protocols and interfaces; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Protocol-specific (CX-0018, CX-0050); not neutral. Consider profile-of cross-reference.

Title: BPN access constraints validated through credentials
Requirement: Data providers and data consumers shall validate access policy constraints on the BPN or on BPNLs of a business partner group through the Membership Credential or the BPN Credential.
Rationale: Access decisions for named partners rest on issuer-attested BPNs.
Source extract: BusinessPartnerNumber and of the BPNLs contained in the BusinessPartnerGroup MUST be done via the MembershipCredential or the BpnCredential.
Clusters: K05 Trust framework and discovery; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K09 Privacy and data protection
Review note: Quote ends 'via the MembershipCredential or the BpnCredential' as in statement; consider access-policy cluster K08.

Title: Managing relation only after power of attorney is verified
Requirement: The core service provider-B shall create an "is managed by" relation between legal entities only after it has verified that the managing legal entity has legal authority or power of attorney for the managed legal entity.
Rationale: Delegation between legal entities is verified before it is recorded; the verification method is left to the Catena-X association.
Source extract: relation is only created after the Core Service Provider B has verified that the Managing Legal Entity has the legal authority / power of attorney
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Cross-reference EBW-GOV-027/representation and mandate requirements (K03). Verification method unspecified in source: not testable beyond the order of steps.

Title: Confidence level for BPNL and BPNA
Requirement: The service provider shall calculate and assign a confidence level to BPNLs and BPNAs to indicate data quality.
Rationale: Quality score combines use by members, check against official sources and data owner approval; an assurance-level analogue for partner data.
Source extract: A confidence level MUST be calculated and assigned to BPNLs and BPNAs to indicate the data quality.
Clusters: K14 Conformity, certification and assurance; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Scores 1/3/5 points; do not equate with LoA. Cross-reference EBW-TRU-084 for the eIDAS notion.

Title: Wallet provider verifies wallet instance integrity and signs the instance attestation
Requirement: The wallet provider shall verify the integrity of the wallet instance and sign or seal the wallet instance attestation.
Rationale: Ties the instance attestation to a checked wallet instance, which issuers rely on before issuing person identification data.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2026-1731 (Annex III (new Annex Ib to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979), point 2(b), TR-WIA-2)
Source extract: A wallet provider shall verify the integrity of the wallet instance and sign or seal the wallet instance attestation.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Added after CIR 2026/1731; TR-WIA-2 of new Annex Ib. Complements EBW-TRU-117 (expiry) and EBW-TRU-029 (listed certificate).

Title: Suspended mandate attestation treated as invalid
Requirement: Where a power of attorney or power of representation attestation is suspended, the relying party shall treat it as invalid for as long as the suspension lasts.
Rationale: A temporarily suspended mandate must not be exercisable, so a verifier that still accepts it would undo the owner's suspension.
Source extract: During suspension the attestation SHALL be treated as invalid.
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Rulebook 6.5 allows suspension but its status values (6.9) have no suspended value; raise with WE BUILD.

Title: Reject mandate attestations that are not active
Requirement: A relying party shall reject every power of attorney or power of representation attestation whose status is not active, including revoked, expired and unknown.
Rationale: Treating an unknown status as acceptable would let a revoked or suspended mandate pass whenever the status service is unreachable.
Source extract: Relying Parties SHALL reject every attestation except those having status `active`.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents)
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Statement adds "revoked, expired and unknown" from the 6.9 list (checked).

Title: Verify identifier, status, validity and issuer before accepting a mandate
Requirement: Before accepting a power of attorney or power of representation attestation, the relying party shall verify the attestation identifier, its current status, its validity period and the status of its issuer.
Rationale: Status checking of a mandate has to include the issuer, because a suspended issuer can no longer vouch for the mandate.
Source extract: the Relying Party SHALL verify attestation identifier, current status, validity period and issuer status
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K05 Trust framework and discovery
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Section 6.10.

Title: Revoke a mandate attestation when the principal withdraws the mandate
Requirement: The issuer of a power of attorney or power of representation attestation shall revoke it when the principal withdraws the mandate.
Rationale: The rulebook lists the trigger as mandatory but names no duty-holder; the issuer is derived from sections 4.14, 6.7 and 6.13, where the issuer validates the request and updates the status.
Sources: SRC-WEBUILD-RB (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, section 6.6 (Revocation Triggers) with sections 6.7 and 6.13)
Source extract: Principal withdraws mandate | SHALL
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Duty-holder derived from 4.14, 6.7, 6.13 (stated); confirm with WE BUILD.

Title: Revoke a mandate attestation when the representative leaves the organisation
Requirement: The issuer of a power of attorney or power of representation attestation shall revoke it when the representative leaves the organisation.
Rationale: Authority held through an employer must end with the employment; the rulebook lists the trigger as mandatory, and the issuer is derived from sections 4.14, 6.7 and 6.13.
Sources: SRC-WEBUILD-RB (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, section 6.6 (Revocation Triggers) with sections 6.7 and 6.13)
Actors: attestation issuer; wallet owner; authorised representative
Source extract: Representative leaves organization | SHALL
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Duty-holder derived from 4.14, 6.7, 6.13 (stated); confirm with WE BUILD. Issuer needs HR or register sync: see OPS-041.

Title: Revoke mandate attestations when the company is dissolved
Requirement: The issuer of a power of attorney or power of representation attestation shall revoke it when the represented company is dissolved.
Rationale: Delegated authority cannot outlive the principal; the rulebook lists the trigger as mandatory, and the issuer is derived from sections 4.14, 6.7 and 6.13.
Sources: SRC-WEBUILD-RB (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, section 6.6 (Revocation Triggers) with sections 6.7 and 6.13)
Source extract: Company dissolved | SHALL
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K07 Credential lifecycle
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. Duty-holder derived from 4.14, 6.7, 6.13 (stated); confirm with WE BUILD.

Title: Authenticate the requester before accepting a unit revocation request
Requirement: The provider of European Business Wallets shall authenticate the person who requests revocation of a wallet unit before accepting the request.
Rationale: Derived by mapping the ARF rule for EUDI wallets to the European Business Wallet, whose Annex point 1 already requires an authentication mechanism for users who request revocation; the ARF names a natural-person user, the EBW requester is an owner or authorised user.
Actors: wallet provider; wallet owner; wallet user
Source extract: The Wallet Provider SHALL authenticate the User before accepting a request to revoke the Wallet Unit.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K11 Security, resilience and incident handling; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: ARF rule is for EUDI; claim that Annex point 1 already requires an authentication mechanism for revocation requests to be verified.

Title: Revoked owner identification data leaves the structural trust of the unit intact
Requirement: When the owner identification data of a European Business Wallet unit is revoked or expires, the unit shall lose its identity validity while its wallet unit attestation stays valid.
Rationale: The consortium decision separates identity trust from structural trust, so that only the owner-identification state changes; the ADR is proposed and not final.
Source extract: Revocation of EBWOID suspends identity validity while preserving structural trust.
Clusters: K07 Credential lifecycle; K05 Trust framework and discovery; K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Statement uses "shall" and adds "or expires" and "lose", none in the quote (which says "suspends identity validity"). ADR status is Proposed: not final.

Title: Actions outside the mandate scope are rejected
Requirement: A relying party shall reject an action that falls outside the scope defined in the mandate of the acting representative.
Rationale: The rulebook names verification as the point of enforcement and rejection of the action as the failure behaviour; this limits an employee or other representative to the powers granted.
Source extract: A mandate SHALL NOT authorize actions outside its defined scope
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K01 Credential data model and formats
Review note: Verified against registered commit de79cca (rulebooks/rb-poa-pox.md, v0.7) and v0.8 of 2026-09-04: section and quote unchanged. IR-18 in 2.9 (verification, failure behaviour reject action).

Title: Joint representation requires two or more signatories acting together
Requirement: Where the representation type of the authorised signatories of a legal entity is joint, a relying party that verifies the authorised signatories attestation shall require that two or more signatories act together before it treats an act as made on behalf of the entity.
Rationale: Derived from the code-list meaning of JOINT in the authorised signatories rulebook, which gives the definition but no verifier duty; the legal effect of a joint act is national law (to verify).
Source extract: Two or more signatories are required to act together to make binding commitments on behalf of the legal entity
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K02 Wallet subject model
Review note: Reworded as in the N14 proposal and marked D; location corrected to rulebooks/rb-authorised-signatories/README.md 2.8.1 (registered commit de79cca). Legal effect of a joint act is national law (to verify).

Title: Custody model recorded per private key
Requirement: The wallet provider shall record for each private key of a wallet unit the custody model that holds it (device held by the owner, module operated by the provider, module operated by the owner, or remote service of a qualified trust service provider) and shall make the record available to the owner on request.
Rationale: Derived (criteria C1, C6, C9 of the DEC-03 page): no source says where keys must be held, so the choice must at least be recorded; Annex point 3(1) requires a secure cryptographic device but not its placement.
Source extract: shall use at least one Wallet secure cryptographic application and Wallets secure cryptographic device to manage critical assets
Clusters: K04 Key custody and wallet architecture; K13 Governance, supervision and liability
Review note: Derivation stated. Quote supports a secure device only; four-way custody list is the reviewer's model. Related GOV-050, CER-023.

Title: Council text: onboarding of the owner at assurance level high
Requirement: Providers of European Business Wallets shall ensure that their wallets support common protocols and interfaces to securely onboard the owner remotely via a legal representative or other lawfully empowered person with an electronic identification means that meets assurance level high.
Rationale: The Council text narrows the Commission proposal (EBW-TRU-008: substantial or high) to level high; the requirement follows Council text ST 9684/26 until the trilogue outcome is known.
Actors: provider of European Business Wallets; legal representative
Source extract: securely onboard the European Business Wallet owner remotely via a legal representative or other persons that are lawfully empowered to carry out the onboarding process
Clusters: K02 Wallet subject model; K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Quote now Council ST 9684/26 Art 6(1)(e), including legal representative or lawfully empowered persons, machine-checked; assurance level high in full_quote. Divergence from TRU-008 kept until trilogue. Related TRU-070.

Title: Identity proofing covers the representative of a third-country operator
Requirement: A provider of owner identification data shall issue owner identification data and a unique identifier to an economic operator established outside the Union only if the identity proofing of the operator and of its representative empowered to carry out the onboarding fulfils the identity verification methods of Article 24(1a) of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014.
Rationale: The Council text extends the proofing condition of the Commission proposal (EBW-TRU-015) to the empowered representative, which links the legal-person identity to a natural person in a third country.
Actors: provider of owner identification data; economic operator established outside the Union
Source extract: the identity proofing and verification of those economic operators and their representative empowered to carry out the onboarding process
Clusters: K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K06 Identity and identifiers
Review note: Adds the empowered representative to the TRU-015 condition.

Title: Legal person not in a status that prevents it from acting
Requirement: For identity proofing of a legal person at assurance level high, the entity responsible for registration shall check that the legal person is not known by an authoritative source to be in a status that would prevent it from acting as that legal person.
Rationale: The element is listed at level low and is cumulative for substantial and high; the existing requirement EBW-TRU-084 covers only name, legal form and unique identifier, not dissolved or insolvent entities.
Sources: SRC-CIR-2015-1502 (Annex, section 2.1.3, level Low element 3, carried into levels Substantial and High)
Source extract: The legal person is not known by an authoritative source to be in a status that would prevent it from acting as that legal person.
Clusters: K06 Identity and identifiers; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Same CIR 2015/1502 section 2.1.3; add the "status preventing it from acting" check to TRU-084.

Title: Issuer establishes the principal's authority before issuing a power of attorney
Requirement: The issuer of an EU power of attorney attestation shall reject the issuance if the authority of the principal to act on behalf of the company cannot be established.
Rationale: The rulebook gives this check as protection against invalid delegation chains in which a person without authority grants powers.
Source extract: Issuer SHALL reject issuance if principal authority cannot be established.
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW); K08 Protocols and interfaces
Review note: Source check: IR-03 confirmed at registered commit de79cca (rb-eu-poa v0.1). 'Authority cannot be established' has no stated method; testable only against a defined authentic source.

Title: Reject acts of a substitute where substitution is not allowed
Requirement: Where an EU power of attorney attestation states that substitution is not allowed, a relying party shall reject an act that a third party performs under powers the attorney has passed on.
Rationale: Derived; the rulebook defines the attribute as the attorney's right to delegate the granted powers to a third party but states no verifier behaviour for the value not_allowed.
Source extract: Whether the attorney may delegate the granted powers to a third party
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K08 Protocols and interfaces; K17 Cross-jurisdiction identity, identifiers and assurance (EBW and non-EBW)
Review note: Provenance D with derivation stated: rulebook gives the code list definition only, no verifier rule. Source check: section 2.8 exists at registered commit de79cca (rb-eu-poa v0.1). Requires detecting that a third party acts under passed-on powers, which no credential mechanism yet shows (see INT-025/029 act claim). Depends on INT-097 (optional attribute).

Title: Unique identification and authentication of systems as well as persons
Requirement: Where the wallet owner is a financial entity, its identity management policies and procedures shall ensure the unique identification and authentication of natural persons and systems accessing its information.
Rationale: Derived; the duty lies on financial entities. It is the only Union text found that names systems next to natural persons as subjects of identification and authentication for access rights.
Source extract: ensure the unique identification and authentication of natural persons and systems accessing the financial entities’ information
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K02 Wallet subject model; K16 AI-first and agent interoperability
Review note: Matches Art 20(1). Derived to wallet owners generally. Overlaps TRU-176 in subject (machines) but differs in duty-holder; not merged.

Title: Authenticate the calling machine or application before granting access
Requirement: Before granting an application or machine access to protected asset data or restricted services, the party operating the asset interface shall identify and authenticate that application.
Rationale: Derived from the IDTA security specification for the asset administration shell, an implementation artefact; only this high-level rule is used. The specification maps the rule from IEC 62443 and allows the application to stand for a non-person user.
Sources: SRC-IDTA-AAS-P4 (Part 4 (IDTA-01004 v3.1), AAS Security requirements, FR1, Identification and authentication of AAS user applications and AAS interface)
Source extract: the AAS interface SHALL ensure the identification and authentication of the AAS user application
Clusters: K03 Mandates, representation and delegation (employees, machines, agents); K16 AI-first and agent interoperability; K04 Key custody and wallet architecture
Review note: Derived; 'identification and authentication of AAS user application' generalised to machines. Related to TRU-175 (owner-side policy) and TRU-054 (agent).
